<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.2.113.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 2 s 113</a>-117; art 7 s 32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.5.39.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 5 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.17.44.0">2023 c 70 art 17 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.62.40.0">2024 c 127 art 62 s 40</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0641"><h1 class="shn">256B.0641 RECOVERY OF OVERPAYMENTS.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0641.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Recovery procedures; sources.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.72">256B.72 </a>or any law or rule to the contrary, when the commissioner or the federal government determines that an overpayment has been made by the state to any medical assistance vendor, the commissioner shall recover the overpayment as follows:</p><p>(1) if the federal share of the overpayment amount is due and owing to the federal government under federal law and regulations, the commissioner shall recover from the medical assistance vendor the federal share of the determined overpayment amount paid to that provider using the schedule of payments required by the federal government;</p><p>(2) if the overpayment to a medical assistance vendor is due to a retroactive adjustment made because the medical assistance vendor's temporary payment rate was higher than the established desk audit payment rate or because of a department error in calculating a payment rate, the commissioner shall recover from the medical assistance vendor the total amount of the overpayment within 120 days after the date on which written notice of the adjustment is sent to the medical assistance vendor or according to a schedule of payments approved by the commissioner;</p><p>(3) a medical assistance vendor is liable for the overpayment amount owed by a long-term care provider if the vendors or their owners are under common control or ownership; and</p><p>(4) in order to collect past due obligations to the department, the commissioner shall make any necessary adjustments to payments to a provider or vendor that has the same tax identification number as is assigned to a provider or vendor with past due obligations.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0641.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Overpayments to prior owners.</span></h2><p>The current owner of a nursing home, boarding care home, or intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities is liable for the overpayment amount owed by a former owner for any facility sold, transferred, or reorganized after May 15, 1987. Within 12 months of a written request by the current owner, the commissioner shall conduct a field audit of the facility for the auditable rate years during which the former owner owned the facility and issue a report of the field audit within 15 months of the written request. Nothing in this subdivision limits the liability of a former owner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0641.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Facility in receivership.</span></h2><p>Subdivision 2 does not apply to the change of ownership of a facility to a nonrelated organization while the facility to be sold, transferred or reorganized is in receivership under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.15">144A.15</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.12">245A.12,</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.13">245A.13</a>, and the commissioner during the receivership has not determined the need to place residents of the facility into a newly constructed or newly established facility. Nothing in this subdivision limits the liability of a former owner.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0641.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/9/#laws.2.39.0">1Sp1985 c 9 art 2 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/133/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 133 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.6.46.0">1991 c 292 art 6 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/207/#laws.7.22.0">1995 c 207 art 7 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 56 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.22.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/9/#laws.6.53.0">1Sp2011 c 9 art 6 s 53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/74/#laws.0.7.0">2015 c 74 s 7</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0642"><h1 class="shn">256B.0642 FEDERAL FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION.</h1><p>The commissioner may, in the aggregate, prospectively reduce payment rates for medical assistance providers receiving federal funds to avoid reduced federal financial participation resulting from rates that are in excess of the Medicare limitations.</p></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0642.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/282/#laws.3.59.0">1989 c 282 art 3 s 59</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0643"><h1 class="shn">256B.0643 VENDOR REQUEST FOR CONTESTED CASE PROCEEDING.</h1><p>Unless otherwise provided by law, a vendor of medical care, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.02#stat.256B.02.7">256B.02, subdivision 7</a>, must use this procedure to request a contested case, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.02#stat.14.02.3">14.02, subdivision 3</a>. A request for a contested case must be filed with the commissioner in writing within 60 days after the date the notification of an action or determination was mailed. The appeal request must specify:</p><p>(1) each disputed action or item;</p><p>(2) the reason for the dispute;</p><p>(3) an estimate of the dollar amount involved, if any, for each disputed item;</p><p>(4) the computation or other disposition that the appealing party believes is correct;</p><p>(5) the authority in statute or rule upon which the appealing party relies for each disputed item;</p><p>(6) the name and address of the person or firm with whom contacts may be made regarding the appeal; and</p><p>(7) other information required by the commissioner. Nothing in this section shall be construed to create a right to an administrative appeal or contested case proceeding.</p></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0643.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/568/#laws.3.53.0">1990 c 568 art 3 s 53</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0644"><h1 class="shn">256B.0644 REIMBURSEMENT UNDER OTHER STATE HEALTH CARE PROGRAMS.</h1><p class="in">(a) A vendor of medical care, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.02#stat.256B.02.7">256B.02, subdivision 7</a>, and a health maintenance organization, as defined in chapter 62D, must participate as a provider or contractor in the medical assistance program and MinnesotaCare as a condition of participating as a provider in health insurance plans and programs or contractor for state employees established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/43A.18">43A.18</a>, the public employees insurance program under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/43A.316">43A.316</a>, for health insurance plans offered to local statutory or home rule charter city, county, and school district employees, the workers' compensation system under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/176.135">176.135</a>, and insurance plans provided through the Minnesota Comprehensive Health Association under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62E.01">62E.01</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62E.19">62E.19</a>. The limitations on insurance plans offered to local government employees shall not be applicable in geographic areas where provider participation is limited by managed care contracts with the Department of Human Services. This section does not apply to dental service providers providing dental services outside the seven-county metropolitan area.</p><p class="in">(b) For providers other than health maintenance organizations, participation in the medical assistance program means that:</p><p class="in">(1) the provider accepts new medical assistance and MinnesotaCare patients;</p><p class="in">(2) for providers other than dental service providers, at least 20 percent of the provider's patients are covered by medical assistance and MinnesotaCare as their primary source of coverage; or</p><p class="in">(3) for dental service providers providing dental services in the seven-county metropolitan area, at least ten percent of the provider's patients are covered by medical assistance and MinnesotaCare as their primary source of coverage, or the provider accepts new medical assistance and MinnesotaCare patients who are children with special health care needs. For purposes of this section, "children with special health care needs" means children up to age 18 who: (i) require health and related services beyond that required by children generally; and (ii) have or are at risk for a chronic physical, developmental, behavioral, or emotional condition, including: bleeding and coagulation disorders; immunodeficiency disorders; cancer; endocrinopathy; developmental disabilities; epilepsy, cerebral palsy, and other neurological diseases; visual impairment or deafness; Down syndrome and other genetic disorders; autism; fetal alcohol syndrome; and other conditions designated by the commissioner after consultation with representatives of pediatric dental providers and consumers.</p><p class="in">(c) Patients seen on a volunteer basis by the provider at a location other than the provider's usual place of practice may be considered in meeting the participation requirement in this section. The commissioner shall establish participation requirements for health maintenance organizations. The commissioner shall provide lists of participating medical assistance providers on a quarterly basis to the commissioner of management and budget, the commissioner of labor and industry, and the commissioner of commerce. Each of the commissioners shall develop and implement procedures to exclude as participating providers in the program or programs under their jurisdiction those providers who do not participate in the medical assistance program. The commissioner of management and budget shall implement this section through contracts with participating health and dental carriers.</p><p>(d) A volunteer dentist who has signed a volunteer agreement under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.9a">256B.0625, subdivision 9a</a>, shall not be considered to be participating in medical assistance or MinnesotaCare for the purpose of this section.</p></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0644.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/549/#laws.4.13.0">1992 c 549 art 4 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/13/#laws.2.7.0">1993 c 13 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/247/#laws.4.9.0">1993 c 247 art 4 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/339/#laws.0.14.0">1993 c 339 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/345/#laws.9.14.0">1993 c 345 art 9 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/248/#laws.10.16.0">1995 c 248 art 10 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.4.33.0">1997 c 203 art 4 s 33</a>,72; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/177/#laws.0.87.0">1999 c 177 s 87</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.2.43.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 2 s 43</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/275/#laws.0.3.0">2002 c 275 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.5.12.0">2007 c 147 art 5 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/204/#laws.0.42.0">2008 c 204 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/101/#laws.2.109.0">2009 c 101 art 2 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/200/#laws.1.6.0">2010 c 200 art 1 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/1/1/#laws.16.18.0">1Sp2010 c 1 art 16 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/181/#laws.0.2.0">2012 c 181 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.4.38.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 4 s 38</a></p></div><div class="sr" id="stat.256B.0645"><b>256B.0645</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.2.123.0">2016 c 158 art 2 s 123</a>]</div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0646"><h1 class="shn">256B.0646 MINNESOTA RESTRICTED RECIPIENT PROGRAM; PERSONAL CARE ASSISTANCE SERVICES.</h1><p>(a) When a recipient's use of personal care assistance services or community first services and supports under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.85">256B.85</a> results in abusive or fraudulent billing, the commissioner may place a recipient in the Minnesota restricted recipient program under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.2165">9505.2165</a>. A recipient placed in the Minnesota restricted recipient program under this section must: (1) use a designated traditional personal care assistance provider agency; and (2) obtain a new assessment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>, including consultation with a registered or public health nurse on the long-term care consultation team pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>, subdivision 15, paragraph (b), clause (2).</p><p>(b) A recipient must comply with additional conditions for the use of personal care assistance services or community first services and supports if the commissioner determines it is necessary to prevent future misuse of personal care assistance services or abusive or fraudulent billing. Additional conditions may include but are not limited to restricting service authorizations for a duration of no more than one month and requiring a qualified professional to monitor and report services on a monthly basis.</p><p>(c) A recipient placed in the Minnesota restricted recipient program under this section may appeal the placement according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045</a>.</p></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0646.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.2.118.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 2 s 118</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.17.9.0">2022 c 98 art 17 s 9</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.065"><h1 class="shn">256B.065 SOCIAL SECURITY AMENDMENTS.</h1><p>The commissioner shall comply with requirements of the Social Security amendments of 1972 (Public Law 92-603) necessary in order to avoid loss of federal funds, and shall implement by rule, pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act, those provisions required of state agencies supervising Title XIX of the Social Security Act.</p></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.065.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/717/#laws.0.7.0">1973 c 717 s 7</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0651"><h1 class="shn">256B.0651 HOME CARE SERVICES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>(a) For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0651">256B.0651</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, the terms in paragraphs (b) to (g) have the meanings given.</p><p>(b) "Activities of daily living" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (b).</p><p>(c) "Assessment" means a review and evaluation of a recipient's need for home care services conducted in person.</p><p>(d) "Home care services" means medical assistance covered services that are home health agency services, including skilled nurse visits; home health aide visits; physical therapy, occupational therapy, respiratory therapy, and language-speech pathology therapy; home care nursing; and personal care assistance.</p><p>(e) "Home residence," effective January 1, 2010, means a residence owned or rented by the recipient either alone, with roommates of the recipient's choosing, or with an unpaid responsible party or legal representative; or a family foster home where the license holder lives with the recipient and is not paid to provide home care services for the recipient except as allowed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652#stat.256B.0652.10">256B.0652, subdivision 10</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654#stat.256B.0654.4">256B.0654, subdivision 4</a>.</p><p>(f) "Medically necessary" has the meaning given in Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0170">9505.0170</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0475">9505.0475</a>.</p><p>(g) "Ventilator-dependent" means an individual who receives mechanical ventilation for life support at least six hours per day and is expected to be or has been dependent on a ventilator for at least 30 consecutive days.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Services covered.</span></h2><p>Home care services covered under this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a> include:</p><p>(1) nursing services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.6a">256B.0625, subdivision 6a, and 256B.0653</a>;</p><p>(2) home care nursing services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.7">256B.0625, subdivision 7</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654</a>;</p><p>(3) home health services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.6a">256B.0625, subdivision 6a, and 256B.0653</a>;</p><p>(4) personal care assistance services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>;</p><p>(5) supervision of personal care assistance services provided by a qualified professional under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>;</p><p>(6) face-to-face assessments by county public health nurses for services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>; and</p><p>(7) service updates and review of temporary increases for personal care assistance services by the county public health nurse for services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Noncovered home care services.</span></h2><p>The following home care services are not eligible for payment under medical assistance:</p><p>(1) services provided in a nursing facility, hospital, or intermediate care facility with exceptions in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0653">256B.0653</a>;</p><p>(2) services for the sole purpose of monitoring medication compliance with an established medication program for a recipient;</p><p>(3) home care services for covered services under the Medicare program or any other insurance held by the recipient;</p><p>(4) services to other members of the recipient's household;</p><p>(5) any home care service included in the daily rate of the community-based residential facility where the recipient is residing;</p><p>(6) nursing and rehabilitation therapy services that are reasonably accessible to a recipient outside the recipient's place of residence, excluding the assessment, counseling and education, and personal assistance care; or</p><p>(7) Medicare evaluation or administrative nursing visits on dual-eligible recipients that do not qualify for Medicare visit billing.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2><p>MS 2008 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 14</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2><p> [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.23.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 23</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2><p>MS 2008 [Paragraph (a) renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 3a</a>]</p><p>[Paragraph (b) renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 4</a>]</p><p>[Paragraph (c) renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 7</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2><p>MS 2008 [Paragraph (a) renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 8</a>]</p><p>[Paragraph (b) renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 8</a>]</p><p>[Paragraph (c) renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 13</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2><p>MS 2008 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 9</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.</h2><p>MS 2008 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 10</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.10"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2><p> [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.23.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 23</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.11"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2><p>MS 2008 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652, subd 11</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.12"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Approval of home care services.</span></h2><p>The commissioner or the commissioner's designee shall determine the medical necessity of home care services, the level of caregiver according to subdivision 2, and the institutional comparison according to this subdivision and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652</a>, subdivisions 3a, 4 to 11, 13, and 14, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, the cost-effectiveness of services, and the amount, scope, and duration of home care services reimbursable by medical assistance, based on the assessment, primary payer coverage determination information as required, the service plan, the recipient's age, the cost of services, the recipient's medical condition, and diagnosis or disability. The commissioner may publish additional criteria for determining medical necessity according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.04">256B.04</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.13"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Recovery of excessive payments.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall seek monetary recovery from providers of payments made for services which exceed the limits established in this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0653">256B.0653</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>. This subdivision does not apply to services provided to a recipient at the previously authorized level pending an appeal under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045#stat.256.045.10">256.045, subdivision 10</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.14"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Referrals to Medicare providers required.</span></h2><p>Home care providers that do not participate in or accept Medicare assignment must refer and document the referral of dual-eligible recipients to Medicare providers when Medicare is determined to be the appropriate payer for services and supplies and equipment. Providers must be terminated from participation in the medical assistance program for failure to make these referrals.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.15"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Quality assurance for program integrity.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall establish an ongoing quality assurance process for home care services to monitor program integrity, including provider standards and training, consumer surveys, and random reviews of documentation.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.16"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Oversight of enrolled providers.</span></h2><p>The commissioner has the authority to request proof of documentation of meeting provider standards, quality standards of care, correct billing practices, and other information. Failure to comply with or to provide access and information to demonstrate compliance with laws, rules, or policies may result in suspension, denial, or termination of the provider agency's enrollment with the department.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0651.17"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Recipient protection.</span></h2><p>(a) Providers of home care services must provide each recipient with a copy of the home care bill of rights under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.44">144A.44</a> at least 30 days prior to terminating services to a recipient, if the termination results from provider sanctions under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.064">256B.064</a>, such as a payment withhold, a suspension of participation, or a termination of participation. If a home care provider determines it is unable to continue providing services to a recipient, the provider must notify the recipient, the recipient's responsible party, and the commissioner 30 days prior to terminating services to the recipient because of an action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.064">256B.064</a>, and must assist the commissioner and lead agency in supporting the recipient in transitioning to another home care provider of the recipient's choice.</p><p>(b) In the event of a payment withhold from a home care provider, a suspension of participation, or a termination of participation of a home care provider under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.064">256B.064</a>, the commissioner may inform the Office of Ombudsman for Long-Term Care and the lead agencies for all recipients with active service agreements with the provider. At the commissioner's request, the lead agencies must contact recipients to ensure that the recipients are continuing to receive needed care, and that the recipients have been given free choice of provider if they transfer to another home care provider. In addition, the commissioner or the commissioner's delegate may directly notify recipients who receive care from the provider that payments have been or will be withheld or that the provider's participation in medical assistance has been or will be suspended or terminated, if the commissioner determines that notification is necessary to protect the welfare of the recipients. For purposes of this subdivision, "lead agencies" means counties, tribes, and managed care organizations.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0651.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/568/#laws.3.51.0">1990 c 568 art 3 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.7.12.0">1991 c 292 art 7 s 12</a>,25; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/391/#laws.0.3.0">1992 c 391 s 3</a>-6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/464/#laws.2.1.0">1992 c 464 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.7.50.0">1992 c 513 art 7 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/1/1/#laws.5.51.0">1Sp1993 c 1 art 5 s 51</a>-53; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/207/#laws.6.52.0">1995 c 207 art 6 s 52</a>-55; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.5.17.0">1996 c 451 art 5 s 17</a>-20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.4.28.0">1997 c 203 art 4 s 28</a>,29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/3/3/#laws.0.9.0">3Sp1997 c 3 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.4.29.0">1998 c 407 art 4 s 29</a>-31; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.4.50.0">1999 c 245 art 4 s 50</a>-58; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/474/#laws.0.8.0">2000 c 474 s 8</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.3.29.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 3 s 29</a>-41; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/375/#laws.2.17.0">2002 c 375 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/15/#laws.1.33.0">2003 c 15 art 1 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.3.26.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 3 s 26</a>-28; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.1.49.0">2005 c 10 art 1 s 49</a>,50; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 56 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/4/#laws.7.15.0">1Sp2005 c 4 art 7 s 15</a>-19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.7.8.0">2007 c 147 art 7 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.23.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 23,85</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/352/#laws.1.8.0">2010 c 352 art 1 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/262/#laws.5.6.0">2014 c 262 art 5 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.9.5.0">2014 c 291 art 9 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.2.119.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 2 s 119</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0652"><h1 class="shn">256B.0652 AUTHORIZATION AND REVIEW OF HOME CARE SERVICES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">State coordination.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall supervise the coordination of the authorization and review of home care services that are reimbursed by medical assistance.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duties.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner may contract with or employ necessary staff, or contract with qualified agencies, to provide home care authorization and review services for medical assistance recipients who are receiving home care services.</p><p>(b) Reimbursement for the authorization function shall be made through the medical assistance administrative authority. The state shall pay the nonfederal share. The functions will be to:</p><p>(1) assess the recipient's individual need for services required to be cared for safely in the community;</p><p>(2) ensure that a care plan that meets the recipient's needs is developed by the appropriate agency or individual;</p><p>(3) ensure cost-effectiveness and nonduplication of medical assistance home care services;</p><p>(4) recommend the approval or denial of the use of medical assistance funds to pay for home care services;</p><p>(5) reassess the recipient's need for and level of home care services at a frequency determined by the commissioner;</p><p>(6) conduct on-site assessments when determined necessary by the commissioner and recommend changes to care plans that will provide more efficient and appropriate home care; and</p><p>(7) on the department's website:</p><p>(i) provide a link to MinnesotaHelp.info for a list of enrolled home care agencies with the following information: main office address, contact information for the agency, counties in which services are provided, type of home care services provided, whether the personal care assistance choice option is offered, types of qualified professionals employed, number of personal care assistants employed, and data on staff turnover; and</p><p>(ii) post data on home care services including information from both fee-for-service and managed care plans on recipients as available.</p><p>(c) In addition, the commissioner or the commissioner's designee may:</p><p>(1) review care plans, service plans, and reimbursement data for utilization of services that exceed community-based standards for home care, inappropriate home care services, medical necessity, home care services that do not meet quality of care standards, or unauthorized services and make appropriate referrals within the department or to other appropriate entities based on the findings;</p><p>(2) assist the recipient in obtaining services necessary to allow the recipient to remain safely in or return to the community;</p><p>(3) coordinate home care services with other medical assistance services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625">256B.0625</a>;</p><p>(4) assist the recipient with problems related to the provision of home care services;</p><p>(5) assure the quality of home care services; and</p><p>(6) assure that all liable third-party payers including, but not limited to, Medicare have been used prior to medical assistance for home care services.</p><p>(d) For the purposes of this section, "home care services" means medical assistance services defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625">256B.0625</a>, subdivisions 6a, 7, and 19a.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2><p>MS 2008 [Renumbered subd 12]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.3a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote"> Authorization; generally.</span></h2><p>The commissioner, or the commissioner's designee, shall review the assessment, request for temporary services, service plan, and any additional information that is submitted. The commissioner shall, within 30 days after receiving a complete request, assessment, and service plan, authorize home care services as provided in this section.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote"> Home health services.</span></h2><p>Home health services including skilled nurse visits and home health aide visits must be authorized by the commissioner or the commissioner's designee. Authorization must be based on medical necessity and cost-effectiveness when compared with other care options. The commissioner must receive the request for authorization of skilled nurse visits and home health aide visits within 20 working days of the start of service. When home health services are used in combination with personal care and home care nursing, the cost of all home care services shall be considered for cost-effectiveness.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Authorization; home care nursing services.</span></h2><p>(a) All home care nursing services shall be authorized by the commissioner or the commissioner's designee. Authorization for home care nursing services shall be based on medical necessity and cost-effectiveness when compared with alternative care options. The commissioner may authorize medically necessary home care nursing services in quarter-hour units when:</p><p>(1) the recipient requires more individual and continuous care than can be provided during a skilled nurse visit; or</p><p>(2) the cares are outside of the scope of services that can be provided by a home health aide or personal care assistant.</p><p>(b) The commissioner may authorize:</p><p>(1) up to two times the average amount of direct care hours provided in nursing facilities statewide for case mix classification "K" as established by the annual cost report submitted to the department by nursing facilities in May 1992;</p><p>(2) home care nursing in combination with other home care services and community first services and supports as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.85">256B.85 </a>up to the total cost allowed under this subdivision and subdivision 7;</p><p>(3) up to 16 hours per day if the recipient requires more nursing than the maximum number of direct care hours as established in clause (1) and, but for the provision of the nursing services, the recipient would require a hospital level of care as defined in Code of Federal Regulations, title 42, section 440.10.</p><p>(c) The commissioner may authorize up to 16 hours per day of medically necessary home care nursing services or up to 24 hours per day of medically necessary home care nursing services until such time as the commissioner is able to make a determination of eligibility for recipients who are cooperatively applying for home care services under the community alternative care program developed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>, or until it is determined by the appropriate regulatory agency that a health benefit plan is or is not required to pay for appropriate medically necessary health care services. Recipients or their representatives must cooperatively assist the commissioner in obtaining this determination. Recipients who are eligible for the community alternative care program may not receive more hours of nursing under this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0651">256B.0651</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0653">256B.0653</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659 </a>than would otherwise be authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote"> Authorization; personal care assistance and qualified professional.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) All personal care assistance services, supervision by a qualified professional, and additional services beyond the limits established in subdivision 11, must be authorized by the commissioner or the commissioner's designee before services begin except for the assessments established in subdivision 11 and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>. The authorization for personal care assistance and qualified professional services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a> must be completed within 30 days after receiving a complete request.</p><p class="in">(b) The amount of personal care assistance services authorized must be based on the recipient's home care rating. The home care rating shall be determined by the commissioner or the commissioner's designee based on information submitted to the commissioner identifying the following for recipients with dependencies in two or more activities of daily living:</p><p class="in">(1) total number of dependencies of activities of daily living as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>;</p><p class="in">(2) presence of complex health-related needs as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>; and</p><p class="in">(3) presence of Level I behavior as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>.</p><p class="in">(c) For purposes meeting the criteria in paragraph (b), the methodology to determine total time for personal care assistance services for each home care rating is based on the median paid units per day for each home care rating from fiscal year 2007 data for the personal care assistance program. Each home care rating has a base level of hours assigned. Additional time is added through the assessment and identification of the following:</p><p class="in">(1) 30 additional minutes per day for a dependency in each critical activity of daily living as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>;</p><p class="in">(2) 30 additional minutes per day for each complex health-related function as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>; and</p><p class="in">(3) 30 additional minutes per day for each behavior issue as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, subdivision 4, paragraph (d).</p><p class="in">(d) Effective July 1, 2011, the home care rating for recipients who have a dependency in one activity of daily living or Level I behavior shall equal no more than two units per day. Recipients with this home care rating are not subject to the methodology in paragraph (c) and are not eligible for more than two units per day.</p><p>(e) A limit of 96 units of qualified professional supervision may be authorized for each recipient receiving personal care assistance services. A request to the commissioner to exceed this total in a calendar year must be requested by the personal care provider agency on a form approved by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote"> Ventilator-dependent.</span></h2><p>If the recipient is ventilator-dependent, the monthly medical assistance authorization for home care services shall not exceed what the commissioner would pay for care at the highest cost hospital designated as a long-term hospital under the Medicare program. For purposes of this subdivision, home care services means all direct care services provided in the home that would be included in the payment for care at the long-term hospital. Recipients who meet the definition of ventilator dependent and the EN home care rating and utilize a combination of home care services are limited up to a total of 24 hours of home care services per day. Additional hours may be authorized when a recipient's assessment indicates a need for two staff to perform activities. Additional time is limited to four hours per day.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Authorization; time limits; amount and type.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner or the commissioner's designee shall determine the time period for which an authorization shall be effective. If the recipient continues to require home care services beyond the duration of the authorization, the home care provider must request a new authorization. A personal care provider agency must request a new personal care assistance services assessment, or service update if allowed, at least 60 days prior to the end of the current authorization time period. The request for the assessment must be made on a form approved by the commissioner. An authorization must be valid for no more than 12 months.</p><p>(b) The amount and type of personal care assistance services authorized based upon the assessment and service plan must remain in effect for the recipient whether the recipient chooses a different provider or enrolls or disenrolls from a managed care plan under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, unless the service needs of the recipient change and new assessment is warranted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, subdivision 3a.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote"> Authorization requests; temporary services.</span></h2><p>The agency nurse, independently enrolled home care nurse, or county public health nurse may request a temporary authorization for home care services. The commissioner may approve a temporary level of home care services based on the assessment, and service or care plan information, and primary payer coverage determination information as required. Authorization for a temporary level of home care services including nurse supervision is limited to the time specified by the commissioner, but shall not exceed 45 days. The level of services authorized under this provision shall have no bearing on a future authorization.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.10"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote"> Authorization for foster care setting.</span></h2><p>(a) Home care services provided in an adult or child foster care setting must receive authorization by the commissioner according to the limits established in subdivision 11.</p><p>(b) The commissioner may not authorize:</p><p>(1) home care services that are the responsibility of the foster care provider under the terms of the foster care placement agreement, assessment under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142A.607">142A.607</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.4411">260C.4411</a>, and administrative rules;</p><p>(2) personal care assistance services when the foster care license holder is also the personal care provider or personal care assistant, unless the foster home is the licensed provider's primary residence as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625">256B.0625</a>, subdivision 19a; or</p><p>(3) personal care assistant and home care nursing services when the licensed capacity is greater than six, unless all conditions for a variance under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142B.10#stat.142B.10.17">142B.10, subdivision 17</a>, are satisfied for a sibling, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.007#stat.260C.007.32">260C.007, subdivision 32</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.11"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Limits on services without authorization.</span></h2><p>A recipient may receive the following home care services during a calendar year:</p><p>(1) up to two face-to-face assessments to determine a recipient's need for personal care assistance services;</p><p>(2) one service update done to determine a recipient's need for personal care assistance services; and</p><p>(3) up to nine face-to-face skilled nurse visits.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.12"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Assessment and authorization process for persons receiving personal care assistance and developmental disabilities services.</span></h2><p> For purposes of providing informed choice, coordinating of local planning decisions, and streamlining administrative requirements, the assessment and authorization process for persons receiving both home care and home and community-based waivered services for persons with developmental disabilities shall meet the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0651">256B.0651</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654 </a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a> with the following exceptions:</p><p>(a) Upon request for home care services and subsequent assessment by the public health nurse under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0651">256B.0651</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0654">256B.0654</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, the public health nurse shall participate in the screening process, as appropriate, and, if home care services are determined to be necessary, participate in the development of a service plan coordinating the need for home care and home and community-based waivered services with the assigned county case manager, the recipient of services, and the recipient's legal representative, if any.</p><p>(b) The public health nurse shall give authorization for home care services to the extent that home care services are:</p><p>(1) medically necessary;</p><p>(2) chosen by the recipient and their legal representative, if any, from the array of home care and home and community-based waivered services available;</p><p>(3) coordinated with other services to be received by the recipient as described in the service plan; and</p><p>(4) provided within the county's reimbursement limits for home care and home and community-based waivered services for persons with developmental disabilities.</p><p>(c) If the public health agency is or may be the provider of home care services to the recipient, the public health agency shall provide the commissioner of human services with a written plan that specifies how the assessment and authorization process will be held separate and distinct from the provision of services.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.13"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Reduction of services; appeal.</span></h2><p>A recipient who appeals a reduction in previously authorized home care services may continue previously authorized services, other than temporary services under subdivision 9, pending an appeal under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045</a>. The commissioner must ensure that the recipient has a copy of the most recent service plan that contains a detailed explanation of which areas of covered personal care assistance tasks are reduced, and provide notice of the amount of time per day reduced, and the reasons for the reduction in the recipient's notice of denial, termination, or reduction.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0652.14"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote"> Authorization; exceptions.</span></h2><p>All home care services above the limits in subdivision 11 must receive the commissioner's authorization before services begin, except when:</p><p>(1) the home care services were required to treat an emergency medical condition that if not immediately treated could cause a recipient serious physical or mental disability, continuation of severe pain, or death. The provider must request retroactive authorization no later than five working days after giving the initial service. The provider must be able to substantiate the emergency by documentation such as reports, notes, and admission or discharge histories;</p><p>(2) a recipient's medical assistance eligibility has lapsed, is then retroactively reinstated, and an authorization for home care services is completed based on the date of a current assessment, eligibility, and request for authorization;</p><p>(3) a third-party payor for home care services has denied or adjusted a payment. Authorization requests must be submitted by the provider within 20 working days of the notice of denial or adjustment. A copy of the notice must be included with the request;</p><p>(4) the commissioner has determined that a county or state human services agency has made an error; or</p><p>(5) if a recipient enrolled in managed care experiences a temporary disenrollment from a health plan, the commissioner shall accept the current health plan authorization for personal care assistance services for up to 60 days. The request must be received within the first 30 days of the disenrollment. If the recipient's reenrollment in managed care is after the 60 days and before 90 days, the provider shall request an additional 30-day extension of the current health plan authorization, for a total limit of 90 days from the time of disenrollment.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0652.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/568/#laws.3.51.0">1990 c 568 art 3 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.7.12.0">1991 c 292 art 7 s 12</a>,13,25; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/391/#laws.0.3.0">1992 c 391 s 3</a>-6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/464/#laws.2.1.0">1992 c 464 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.7.50.0">1992 c 513 art 7 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/1/1/#laws.5.51.0">1Sp1993 c 1 art 5 s 51</a>-54; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/207/#laws.3.18.0">1995 c 207 art 3 s 18</a>; art 6 s 52-56; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.2.21.0">1996 c 451 art 2 s 21</a>; art 5 s 17-20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.4.28.0">1997 c 203 art 4 s 28</a>,29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/3/3/#laws.0.9.0">3Sp1997 c 3 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.4.29.0">1998 c 407 art 4 s 29</a>-31; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.4.50.0">1999 c 245 art 4 s 50</a>-58; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/474/#laws.0.8.0">2000 c 474 s 8</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.3.29.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 3 s 29</a>-41; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/375/#laws.2.17.0">2002 c 375 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.6.19.0">2007 c 147 art 6 s 19</a>-22; art 7 s 8-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/286/#laws.1.7.0">2008 c 286 art 1 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.6.9.0">2009 c 79 art 6 s 9</a>; art 8 s 23,24,26-28,85; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/173/#laws.1.22.0">2009 c 173 art 1 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/352/#laws.1.9.0">2010 c 352 art 1 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/9/#laws.7.9.0">1Sp2011 c 9 art 7 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/63/#laws.0.7.0">2013 c 63 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/262/#laws.5.6.0">2014 c 262 art 5 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.9.5.0">2014 c 291 art 9 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.5.40.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 5 s 40</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.15.2.0">2023 c 70 art 15 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/80/#laws.1.96.0">2024 c 80 art 1 s 96</a>; art 2 s 74; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/115/#laws.16.34.0">2024 c 115 art 16 s 34</a>,41</p></div><p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 5 by Laws 2023, chapter 70, article 15, section 2, is effective upon federal approval if required. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2023, chapter 70, article 15, section 2, the effective date.</p><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0653"><h1 class="shn">256B.0653 HOME HEALTH AGENCY SERVICES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2><p>This section applies to home health agency services including home health aide, skilled nursing visits, physical therapy, occupational therapy, respiratory therapy, and speech-language pathology therapy.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p><p>(a) "Assessment" means an evaluation of the recipient's medical need for home health agency services by a registered nurse or appropriate therapist that is conducted within 30 days of a request.</p><p>(b) "Home care therapies" means occupational, physical, and respiratory therapy and speech-language pathology services provided in the home by a Medicare certified home health agency.</p><p>(c) "Home health agency services" means services delivered by a home health agency to a recipient with medical needs due to illness, disability, or physical conditions in settings permitted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.6a">256B.0625, subdivision 6a</a>.</p><p>(d) "Home health aide" means an employee of a home health agency who completes medically oriented tasks written in the plan of care for a recipient.</p><p>(e) "Home health agency" means a home care provider agency that is Medicare-certified.</p><p>(f) "Occupational therapy services" mean the services defined in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0390">9505.0390</a>.</p><p>(g) "Physical therapy services" mean the services defined in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0390">9505.0390</a>.</p><p>(h) "Respiratory therapy services" mean the services defined in chapter 147C.</p><p>(i) "Speech-language pathology services" mean the services defined in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0390">9505.0390</a>.</p><p>(j) "Skilled nurse visit" means a professional nursing visit to complete nursing tasks required due to a recipient's medical condition that can only be safely provided by a professional nurse to restore and maintain optimal health.</p><p>(k) "Store-and-forward technology" means telehomecare services that do not occur in real time via synchronous transmissions such as diabetic and vital sign monitoring.</p><p>(l) "Telehomecare" means the use of telecommunications technology via live, two-way interactive audiovisual technology which may be augmented by store-and-forward technology.</p><p>(m) "Telehomecare skilled nurse visit" means a visit by a professional nurse to deliver a skilled nurse visit to a recipient located at a site other than the site where the nurse is located and is used in combination with face-to-face skilled nurse visits to adequately meet the recipient's needs.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Home health aide visits.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) Home health aide visits must be provided by a certified home health aide using a written plan of care that is updated in compliance with Medicare regulations. A home health aide shall provide hands-on personal care, perform simple procedures as an extension of therapy or nursing services, and assist in instrumental activities of daily living as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, including assuring that the person gets to medical appointments if identified in the written plan of care. Home health aide visits may be provided in the recipient's home or in the community where normal life activities take the recipient.</p><p class="in">(b) All home health aide visits must have authorization under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652</a>. The commissioner shall limit home health aide visits to no more than one visit per day per recipient.</p><p class="in">(c) Home health aides must be supervised by a registered nurse or an appropriate therapist when providing services that are an extension of therapy.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Skilled nurse visit services.</span></h2><p>(a) Skilled nurse visit services must be provided by a registered nurse or a licensed practical nurse under the supervision of a registered nurse, according to the written plan of care and accepted standards of medical and nursing practice according to chapter 148. Skilled nurse visit services must be ordered by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and documented in a plan of care that is reviewed and approved by the ordering practitioner at least once every 60 days. All skilled nurse visits must be medically necessary and provided in the recipient's home residence or in the community where normal life activities take the recipient, except as allowed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.6a">256B.0625, subdivision 6a</a>.</p><p>(b) Skilled nurse visits include face-to-face and telehomecare visits with a limit of up to two visits per day per recipient. All visits must be based on assessed needs.</p><p>(c) Telehomecare skilled nurse visits are allowed when the recipient's health status can be accurately measured and assessed without a need for a face-to-face, hands-on encounter. All telehomecare skilled nurse visits must have authorization and are paid at the same allowable rates as face-to-face skilled nurse visits.</p><p>(d) The provision of telehomecare must be made via live, two-way interactive audiovisual technology and may be augmented by utilizing store-and-forward technologies. Individually identifiable patient data obtained through real-time or store-and-forward technology must be maintained as health records according to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a>. If the video is used for research, training, or other purposes unrelated to the care of the patient, the identity of the patient must be concealed.</p><p>(e) Authorization for skilled nurse visits must be completed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0652">256B.0652</a>. A total of nine face-to-face skilled nurse visits per calendar year do not require authorization. All telehomecare skilled nurse visits require authorization.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Home care therapies.</span></h2><p>(a) Home care therapies include the following: physical therapy, occupational therapy, respiratory therapy, and speech and language pathology therapy services.</p><p>(b) Home care therapies must be:</p><p>(1) provided in the recipient's residence or in the community where normal life activities take the recipient after it has been determined the recipient is unable to access outpatient therapy;</p><p>(2) prescribed, ordered, or referred by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant, and documented in a plan of care and reviewed, according to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0390">9505.0390</a>;</p><p>(3) assessed by an appropriate therapist; and</p><p>(4) provided by a Medicare-certified home health agency enrolled as a Medicaid provider agency.</p><p>(c) Restorative and specialized maintenance therapies must be provided according to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0390">9505.0390</a>. Physical and occupational therapy assistants may be used as allowed under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0390">9505.0390</a>, subpart 1, item B.</p><p>(d) For both physical and occupational therapies, the therapist and the therapist's assistant may not both bill for services provided to a recipient on the same day.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Noncovered home health agency services.</span></h2><p>The following are not eligible for payment under medical assistance as a home health agency service:</p><p>(1) telehomecare skilled nurses services that is communication between the home care nurse and recipient that consists solely of a telephone conversation, facsimile, electronic mail, or a consultation between two health care practitioners;</p><p>(2) the following skilled nurse visits:</p><p>(i) for the purpose of monitoring medication compliance with an established medication program for a recipient;</p><p>(ii) administering or assisting with medication administration, including injections, prefilling syringes for injections, or oral medication setup of an adult recipient, when, as determined and documented by the registered nurse, the need can be met by an available pharmacy or the recipient or a family member is physically and mentally able to self-administer or prefill a medication;</p><p>(iii) services done for the sole purpose of supervision of the home health aide or personal care assistant;</p><p>(iv) services done for the sole purpose to train other home health agency workers;</p><p>(v) services done for the sole purpose of blood samples or lab draw when the recipient is able to access these services outside the home; and</p><p>(vi) Medicare evaluation or administrative nursing visits required by Medicare;</p><p>(3) home health aide visits when the following activities are the sole purpose for the visit: companionship, socialization, household tasks, transportation, and education;</p><p>(4) home care therapies provided in other settings such as a clinic or as an inpatient or when the recipient can access therapy outside of the recipient's residence; and</p><p>(5) home health agency services without qualifying documentation of a face-to-face encounter as specified in subdivision 7.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Face-to-face encounter.</span></h2><p>(a) A face-to-face encounter by a qualifying provider must be completed for all home health services regardless of the need for prior authorization, except when providing a onetime perinatal visit by skilled nursing. The face-to-face encounter may occur through telehealth as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.3b">256B.0625, subdivision 3b</a>. The encounter must be related to the primary reason the recipient requires home health services and must occur within the 90 days before or the 30 days after the start of services. The face-to-face encounter may be conducted by one of the following practitioners, licensed in Minnesota:</p><p>(1) a physician;</p><p>(2) an advanced practice registered nurse; or</p><p>(3) a physician assistant.</p><p>(b) The allowed practitioner, as described in this subdivision, performing the face-to-face encounter but who is not the ordering practitioner must communicate the clinical findings of that face-to-face encounter to the ordering practitioner. The clinical findings of that face-to-face encounter must be incorporated into a written or electronic document included in the recipient's medical record. To assure clinical correlation between the face-to-face encounter and the associated home health services, the practitioner responsible for ordering the services must:</p><p>(1) document that the face-to-face encounter, which is related to the primary reason the recipient requires home health services, occurred within the required time period; and</p><p>(2) indicate the practitioner who conducted the encounter and the date of the encounter.</p><p>(c) For home health services requiring authorization, including prior authorization, home health agencies must retain the qualifying documentation of a face-to-face encounter as part of the recipient health service record, and submit the qualifying documentation to the commissioner or the commissioner's designee upon request.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0653.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Payment rates for home health agency services.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall annually adjust payments for home health agency services to reflect the change in the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Home Health Agency Market Basket. The commissioner shall use the indices as forecasted for the midpoint of the prior rate year to the midpoint of the current rate year.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0653.history

<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.3.29.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 3 s 29</a>-41; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/375/#laws.2.17.0">2002 c 375 art 2 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/15/#laws.1.33.0">2003 c 15 art 1 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.3.26.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 3 s 26</a>-28; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.1.49.0">2005 c 10 art 1 s 49</a>,50; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/352/#laws.2.1.0">2010 c 352 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.112.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 112</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/59/#laws.0.10.0">2017 c 59 s 10</a>;
