<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.4.62.0">1999 c 245 art 4 s 62</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.9.36.0">2000 c 488 art 9 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/161/#laws.0.46.0">2001 c 161 s 46</a>,47; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.4.31.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 4 s 31</a>,32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/10/#laws.1.51.0">2005 c 10 art 1 s 51</a>,52; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/98/#laws.3.24.0">2005 c 98 art 3 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/212/#laws.3.19.0">2006 c 212 art 3 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.51.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/1/1/#laws.17.14.0">1Sp2010 c 1 art 17 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/9/#laws.7.48.0">1Sp2011 c 9 art 7 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.2.26.0">2013 c 108 art 2 s 26</a>-31,44; art 15 s 3,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/275/#laws.1.60.0">2014 c 275 art 1 s 60</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/54/#laws.2.29.0">2019 c 54 art 2 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/61/#laws.2.6.0">2023 c 61 art 2 s 6</a>,42</p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0918"><h1 class="shn">256B.0918 EMPLOYEE SCHOLARSHIP COSTS.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0918.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Program criteria.</span></h2><p>Beginning on or after October 1, 2005, within the limits of appropriations specifically available for this purpose, the commissioner shall provide funding to qualified provider applicants for employee scholarships for education in nursing and other health care fields. Employee scholarships must be for a course of study that is expected to lead to career advancement with the provider or in the field of long-term care, including home care or care of persons with disabilities, or nursing. Providers that secure this funding must use it to award scholarships to employees who work an average of at least 20 hours per week for the provider. Executive management staff without direct care duties, registered nurses, and therapists are not eligible to receive scholarships under this section.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0918.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Participating providers.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall publish a request for proposals in the State Register by August 15, 2005, specifying provider eligibility requirements, provider selection criteria, program specifics, funding mechanism, and methods of evaluation. The commissioner may publish additional requests for proposals in subsequent years. Providers who provide services funded through the following programs are eligible to apply to participate in the scholarship program: home and community-based waivered services for persons with developmental disabilities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.501">256B.501</a>; home and community-based waivered services for the elderly under chapter 256S; waivered services under community access for disability inclusion under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>; community alternative care waivered services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>; brain injury waivered services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>; nursing services and home health services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.6a">256B.0625, subdivision 6a</a>; personal care services and nursing supervision of personal care services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>; home care nursing services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.7">256B.0625, subdivision 7</a>; day training and habilitation services for adults with developmental disabilities under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/252.41">252.41</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/252.46">252.46</a>; and intermediate care facilities for persons with developmental disabilities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.5012">256B.5012</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0918.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Provider selection criteria.</span></h2><p>To be considered for scholarship funding, the provider shall submit a completed application within the time frame specified by the commissioner. In awarding funding, the commissioner shall consider the following:</p><p>(1) the size of the provider as measured in annual billing to the medical assistance program. To be eligible, a provider must receive at least $300,000 annually in medical assistance payments;</p><p>(2) the percentage of employees meeting the scholarship program recipient requirements;</p><p>(3) staff retention rates for paraprofessionals; and</p><p>(4) other criteria determined by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0918.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Funding specifics.</span></h2><p>Within the limits of appropriations specifically available for this purpose, for the rate period beginning on or after October 1, 2005, to September 30, 2007, the commissioner shall provide to each provider listed in subdivision 2 and awarded funds under subdivision 3 a medical assistance rate increase to fund scholarships up to three-tenths percent of the medical assistance reimbursement rate. The commissioner shall require providers to repay any portion of funds awarded under subdivision 3 that is not used to fund scholarships. If applications exceed available funding, funding shall be targeted to providers that employ a higher percentage of paraprofessional staff or have lower rates of turnover of paraprofessional staff. During the subsequent years of the program, the rate adjustment may be recalculated, at the discretion of the commissioner. In making a recalculation the commissioner may consider the provider's success at granting scholarships based on the amount spent during the previous year and the availability of appropriations to continue the program.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0918.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Reporting requirements.</span></h2><p>Participating providers shall report to the commissioner on a schedule determined by the commissioner and on a form supplied by the commissioner for a scholarship rate for rate periods beginning October 1, 2007. The report shall include the amount spent during the reporting period on eligible scholarships, and, for each scholarship recipient, the name of the recipient, the amount awarded, the educational institution attended, the nature of the educational program, the expected or actual program completion date, and a determination of the amount spent as a percentage of the provider's reimbursement. The commissioner shall require providers to repay all of the funds awarded under subdivision 3 if the report required in this subdivision is not filled according to the schedule determined by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0918.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Evaluation.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall report to the legislature annually, beginning March 15, 2007, on the use of these funds.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0918.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 56 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/4/#laws.8.47.0">1Sp2005 c 4 art 8 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.20.17.0">2006 c 282 art 20 s 17</a>-19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.14.2.0">2012 c 216 art 14 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/275/#laws.1.61.0">2014 c 275 art 1 s 61</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.9.5.0">2014 c 291 art 9 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/78/#laws.6.31.0">2015 c 78 art 6 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/54/#laws.2.30.0">2019 c 54 art 2 s 30</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0919"><h1 class="shn">256B.0919 ADULT FOSTER CARE AND FAMILY ADULT DAY CARE.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0919.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Adult foster care licensure capacity.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding contrary provisions of the Human Services Licensing Act and rules adopted under it, an adult foster care license holder may care for five adults age 60 years or older who do not have serious and persistent mental illness or a developmental disability.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0919.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Adult foster care; family adult day care.</span></h2><p>An adult foster care license holder who is not providing care to persons with serious and persistent mental illness or developmental disabilities may also provide family adult day care for adults age 60 years or older who do not have serious and persistent mental illness or a developmental disability. The maximum combined license capacity for adult foster care and family adult day care is five adults. A separate license is not required to provide family adult day care under this subdivision. Foster care homes providing services to five adults shall not be subject to licensure by the commissioner of health under the provisions of chapter 144, 144A, 157, or any other law requiring facility licensure by the commissioner of health.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0919.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">County certification of persons providing adult foster care to related persons.</span></h2><p class="in">A person exempt from licensure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.03#stat.245A.03.2">245A.03, subdivision 2</a>, who provides adult foster care to a related individual age 65 and older, and who meets the requirements in Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.5105">9555.5105</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.6265">9555.6265</a>, may be certified by the county to provide adult foster care. A person certified by the county to provide adult foster care may be reimbursed for services provided and eligible for funding under chapter 256S, if the relative would suffer a financial hardship as a result of providing care. For purposes of this subdivision, financial hardship refers to a situation in which a relative incurs a substantial reduction in income as a result of resigning from a full-time job or taking a leave of absence without pay from a full-time job to care for the client.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0919.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/329/#laws.1.24.0">2010 c 329 art 1 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/352/#laws.2.16.0">2010 c 352 art 2 s 16</a>]</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0919.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.7.18.0">1991 c 292 art 7 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.7.73.0">1992 c 513 art 7 s 73</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/112/#laws.0.49.0">2007 c 112 s 49</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.6.39.0">2007 c 147 art 6 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/54/#laws.2.31.0">2019 c 54 art 2 s 31</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.092"><h1 class="shn">256B.092 SERVICES FOR PERSONS WITH DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">County of financial responsibility; duties.</span></h2><p>Before any services shall be rendered to persons with developmental disabilities who are in need of social service and medical assistance, the county of financial responsibility shall conduct or arrange for a diagnostic evaluation in order to determine whether the person has or may have a developmental disability or has or may have a related condition. If the county of financial responsibility determines that the person has a developmental disability, the county shall inform the person of case management services available under this section. Except as provided in subdivision 1g or 4b, if a person is diagnosed as having a developmental disability, the county of financial responsibility shall conduct or arrange for a needs assessment by a certified assessor, and develop an assessment summary according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>, and authorize services identified in the person's support plan developed according to subdivision 1b. Diagnostic information, obtained by other providers or agencies, may be used by the county agency in determining eligibility for case management. Nothing in this section shall be construed as requiring: (1) assessment in areas agreed to as unnecessary by a certified assessor and the person, or the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, or (2) assessments in areas where there has been a functional assessment completed in the previous 12 months for which the certified assessor and the person or person's guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, agree that further assessment is not necessary. For persons under state guardianship, the certified assessor shall seek authorization from the public guardianship office for waiving any assessment requirements. Assessments related to health, safety, and protection of the person for the purpose of identifying service type, amount, and frequency or assessments required to authorize services may not be waived. To the extent possible, for wards of the commissioner the county shall consider the opinions of the parent of the person with a developmental disability when developing the person's assessment summary and support plan.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Case management services.</span></h2><p>(a) Each recipient of a home and community-based waiver shall be provided case management services by qualified vendors as described in the federally approved waiver application.</p><p>(b) Case management service activities provided to or arranged for a person include:</p><p>(1) development of the person-centered support plan under subdivision 1b;</p><p>(2) informing the individual or the individual's legal guardian or conservator, or parent if the person is a minor, of service options, including all service options available under the waiver plan;</p><p>(3) consulting with relevant medical experts or service providers;</p><p>(4) assisting the person in the identification of potential providers of chosen services, including:</p><p>(i) providers of services provided in a non-disability-specific setting;</p><p>(ii) employment service providers;</p><p>(iii) providers of services provided in settings that are not controlled by a provider; and</p><p>(iv) providers of financial management services;</p><p>(5) assisting the person to access services and assisting in appeals under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045</a>;</p><p>(6) coordination of services, if coordination is not provided by another service provider;</p><p>(7) evaluation and monitoring of the services identified in the support plan, which must incorporate at least one annual face-to-face visit by the case manager with each person; and</p><p>(8) reviewing support plans and providing the lead agency with recommendations for service authorization based upon the individual's needs identified in the support plan.</p><p>(c) Case management service activities that are provided to the person with a developmental disability shall be provided directly by county agencies or under contract. If a county agency contracts for case management services, the county agency must provide each recipient of home and community-based services who is receiving contracted case management services with the contact information the recipient may use to file a grievance with the county agency about the quality of the contracted services the recipient is receiving from a county-contracted case manager. If a county agency provides case management under contracts with other individuals or agencies and the county agency utilizes a competitive proposal process for the procurement of contracted case management services, the competitive proposal process must include evaluation criteria to ensure that the county maintains a culturally responsive program for case management services adequate to meet the needs of the population of the county. For the purposes of this section, "culturally responsive program" means a case management services program that: (1) ensures effective, equitable, comprehensive, and respectful quality care services that are responsive to individuals within a specific population's values, beliefs, practices, health literacy, preferred language, and other communication needs; and (2) is designed to address the unique needs of individuals who share a common language or racial, ethnic, or social background.</p><p>(d) Case management services must be provided by a public or private agency that is enrolled as a medical assistance provider determined by the commissioner to meet all of the requirements in the approved federal waiver plans. Case management services must not be provided to a recipient by a private agency that has a financial interest in the provision of any other services included in the recipient's support plan. For purposes of this section, "private agency" means any agency that is not identified as a lead agency under section 256B.0911, subdivision 10.</p><p>(e) Case managers are responsible for service provisions listed in paragraphs (a) and (b). Case managers shall collaborate with consumers, families, legal representatives, and relevant medical experts and service providers in the development and annual review of the person-centered support plan and habilitation plan.</p><p>(f) For persons who need a positive support transition plan as required in chapter 245D, the case manager shall participate in the development and ongoing evaluation of the plan with the expanded support team. At least quarterly, the case manager, in consultation with the expanded support team, shall evaluate the effectiveness of the plan based on progress evaluation data submitted by the licensed provider to the case manager. The evaluation must identify whether the plan has been developed and implemented in a manner to achieve the following within the required timelines:</p><p>(1) phasing out the use of prohibited procedures;</p><p>(2) acquisition of skills needed to eliminate the prohibited procedures within the plan's timeline; and</p><p>(3) accomplishment of identified outcomes.</p><p class="bl">If adequate progress is not being made, the case manager shall consult with the person's expanded support team to identify needed modifications and whether additional professional support is required to provide consultation.</p><p>(g) The Department of Human Services shall offer ongoing education in case management to case managers. Case managers shall receive no less than 20 hours of case management education and disability-related training each year. The education and training must include person-centered planning, informed choice, cultural competency, employment planning, community living planning, self-direction options, and use of technology supports. By August 1, 2024, all case managers must complete an employment support training course identified by the commissioner of human services. For case managers hired after August 1, 2024, this training must be completed within the first six months of providing case management services. For the purposes of this section, "person-centered planning" or "person-centered" has the meaning given in section 256B.0911, subdivision 10. Case managers must document completion of training in a system identified by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Support plan.</span></h2><p>(a) Each recipient of home and community-based waivered services shall be provided a copy of the written person-centered support plan that:</p><p>(1) is developed with and signed by the recipient within the timelines established by the commissioner and section 256B.0911, subdivision 29;</p><p>(2) includes the person's need for service, including identification of service needs that will be or that are met by the person's relatives, friends, and others, as well as community services used by the general public;</p><p>(3) reasonably ensures the health and welfare of the recipient;</p><p>(4) identifies the person's preferences for services as stated by the person, the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, including the person's choices made on self-directed options, services and supports to achieve employment goals, and living arrangements;</p><p>(5) provides for an informed choice, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.77#stat.256B.77.2">256B.77, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (o), of service and support providers, and identifies all available options for case management services and providers;</p><p>(6) identifies long-range and short-range goals for the person;</p><p>(7) identifies specific services and the amount and frequency of the services to be provided to the person based on assessed needs, preferences, and available resources. The person-centered support plan shall also specify other services the person needs that are not available;</p><p>(8) identifies the need for an individual program plan to be developed by the provider according to the respective state and federal licensing and certification standards, and additional assessments to be completed or arranged by the provider after service initiation;</p><p>(9) identifies provider responsibilities to implement and make recommendations for modification to the support plan;</p><p>(10) includes notice of the right to request a conciliation conference or a hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045</a>;</p><p>(11) is agreed upon and signed by the person, the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, and the authorized county representative;</p><p>(12) is reviewed by a health professional if the person has overriding medical needs that impact the delivery of services; and</p><p>(13) includes the authorized annual and monthly amounts for the services.</p><p>(b) In developing the person-centered support plan, the case manager is encouraged to include the use of volunteers, religious organizations, social clubs, and civic and service organizations to support the individual in the community. The lead agency must be held harmless for damages or injuries sustained through the use of volunteers and agencies under this paragraph, including workers' compensation liability.</p><p>(c) Approved, written, and signed changes to a consumer's services that meet the criteria in this subdivision shall be an addendum to that consumer's individual service plan.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/94/#laws.0.25.0">1991 c 94 s 25</a>; c 292 art 6 s 47]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1d.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/94/#laws.0.25.0">1991 c 94 s 25</a>; c 292 art 6 s 47]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1e"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1e.</h2><p>[Renumbered subd 1f]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1e"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1e.<span class="headnote">Coordination, evaluation, and monitoring of services.</span></h2><p>(a) If the support plan identifies the need for individual program plans for authorized services, the case manager shall assure that individual program plans are developed by the providers according to clauses (2) to (5). The providers shall assure that the individual program plans:</p><p>(1) are developed according to the respective state and federal licensing and certification requirements;</p><p>(2) are designed to achieve the goals of the support plan;</p><p>(3) are consistent with other aspects of the support plan;</p><p>(4) assure the health and welfare of the person; and</p><p>(5) are developed with consistent and coordinated approaches to services among the various service providers.</p><p>(b) The case manager shall monitor the provision of services:</p><p>(1) to assure that the support plan is being followed according to paragraph (a);</p><p>(2) to identify any changes or modifications that might be needed in the support plan, including changes resulting from recommendations of current service providers;</p><p>(3) to determine if the person's legal rights are protected, and if not, notify the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, protection services, or licensing agencies as appropriate; and</p><p>(4) to determine if the person, the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, is satisfied with the services provided.</p><p>(c) If the provider fails to develop or carry out the individual program plan according to paragraph (a), the case manager shall notify the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, the provider, the respective licensing and certification agencies, and the county board where the services are being provided. In addition, the case manager shall identify other steps needed to assure the person receives the services identified in the support plan.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1f"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1f.<span class="headnote">County waiting list.</span></h2><p>The county agency shall maintain a waiting list of persons with developmental disabilities specifying the services needed but not provided. This waiting list shall be used by county agencies to assist them in developing needed services or amending their children and community service agreements.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.1g"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1g.<span class="headnote">Conditions not requiring development of support plan.</span></h2><p>Unless otherwise required by federal law, the county agency is not required to complete a support plan as defined in subdivision 1b for:</p><p>(1) persons whose families are requesting respite care for their family member who resides with them, or whose families are requesting a family support grant and are not requesting purchase or arrangement of habilitative services; and</p><p>(2) persons with developmental disabilities, living independently without authorized services or receiving funding for services at a rehabilitation facility as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/268A.01#stat.268A.01.6">268A.01, subdivision 6</a>, and not in need of or requesting additional services.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Medical assistance.</span></h2><p>To assure quality case management to those persons who are eligible for medical assistance, the commissioner shall, upon request:</p><p>(1) provide consultation on the case management process;</p><p>(2) assist county agencies in the annual reviews of clients review process to assure that appropriate levels of service are provided to persons;</p><p>(3) provide consultation on service planning and development of services with appropriate options;</p><p>(4) provide training and technical assistance to county case managers; and</p><p>(5) authorize payment for medical assistance services according to this chapter and rules implementing it.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.2a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Medical assistance for case management activities under the state plan Medicaid option.</span></h2><p>Upon receipt of federal approval, the commissioner shall make payments to approved vendors of case management services participating in the medical assistance program to reimburse costs for providing case management service activities to medical assistance eligible persons with developmental disabilities, in accordance with the state Medicaid plan and federal requirements and limitations.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Authorization and termination of services.</span></h2><p>County agency case managers, under rules of the commissioner, shall authorize and terminate services of community and regional treatment center providers according to support plans. Services provided to persons with developmental disabilities may only be authorized and terminated by case managers or certified assessors according to (1) rules of the commissioner and (2) the support plan as defined in subdivision 1b. Medical assistance services not needed shall not be authorized by county agencies or funded by the commissioner. When purchasing or arranging for unlicensed respite care services for persons with overriding health needs, the county agency shall seek the advice of a health care professional in assessing provider staff training needs and skills necessary to meet the medical needs of the person.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.3a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Authorization of technology services.</span></h2><p>(a) Lead agencies must not implement additional requirements, in addition to those required by the commissioner, that could result in the delay of approval or implementation of technology.</p><p>(b) For individuals receiving waiver services under this section, approval or denial of technology must occur within 30 business days of the receipt of the initial request. If denied, the lead agency must submit a notice of action form clearly stating the reason for the denial, including information describing why the technology is not appropriate to meet the individual's assessed need.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Home and community-based services for developmental disabilities.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall make payments to approved vendors participating in the medical assistance program to pay costs of providing home and community-based services, including case management service activities provided as an approved home and community-based service, to medical assistance eligible persons with developmental disabilities who have been screened under subdivision 7 and according to federal requirements. Federal requirements include those services and limitations included in the federally approved application for home and community-based services for persons with developmental disabilities and subsequent amendments.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall comply with the requirements in the federally approved transition plan for the home and community-based services waivers for the elderly authorized under this section.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.4a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Demonstration projects.</span></h2><p>The commissioner may waive state rules governing home and community-based services in order to demonstrate other methods of administering these services and to improve efficiency and responsiveness to individual needs of persons with developmental disabilities, notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.055">14.055</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.056">14.056</a>. All demonstration projects approved by the commissioner must comply with state laws and federal regulations, must remain within the fiscal limitations of the home and community-based services program for persons with developmental disabilities, and must assure the health and welfare of the persons receiving services.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.4b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4b.<span class="headnote">Case management for persons receiving home and community-based services.</span></h2><p>Persons authorized for and receiving home and community-based services may select from vendors of case management which have provider agreements with the state to provide home and community-based case management service activities. This subdivision becomes effective July 1, 1992, only if the state agency is unable to secure federal approval for limiting choice of case management vendors to the county of financial responsibility.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.4c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4c.<span class="headnote">Living arrangements based on a 24-hour plan of care.</span></h2><p>(a) Notwithstanding the requirements for licensure under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9525.1860">9525.1860</a>, subpart 6, item D, and upon federal approval of an amendment to the home and community-based services waiver for persons with developmental disabilities, a person receiving home and community-based services may choose to live in their own home without requiring that the living arrangement be licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.5050">9555.5050</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.6265">9555.6265</a>, provided the following conditions are met:</p><p>(1) the person receiving home and community-based services has chosen to live in their own home;</p><p>(2) home and community-based services are provided by a qualified vendor who meets the provider standards as approved in the Minnesota home and community-based services waiver plan for persons with developmental disabilities;</p><p>(3) the person, or their legal representative, individually or with others has purchased or rents the home and the person's service provider has no financial interest in the home; and</p><p>(4) the service planning team, as defined in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9525.0004">9525.0004</a>, subpart 24, has determined that the planned services, the 24-hour plan of care, and the housing arrangement are appropriate to address the health, safety, and welfare of the person.</p><p>(b) The county agency may require safety inspections of the selected housing as part of their determination of the adequacy of the living arrangement.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.4d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4d.<span class="headnote">Medicaid reimbursement; licensed provider; related individuals.</span></h2><p class="in"> Medicaid reimbursement for the provision of supported living services to a related individual is allowed when the conditions specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.03#stat.245A.03.9">245A.03, subdivision 9</a>, are met.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Federal waivers.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall apply for any federal waivers necessary to secure, to the extent allowed by law, federal financial participation under United States Code, title 42, sections 1396 et seq., as amended, for the provision of services to persons who, in the absence of the services, would need the level of care provided in a regional treatment center or a community intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities. The commissioner may seek amendments to the waivers or apply for additional waivers under United States Code, title 42, sections 1396 et seq., as amended, to contain costs. The commissioner shall ensure that payment for the cost of providing home and community-based alternative services under the federal waiver plan shall not exceed the cost of intermediate care services including day training and habilitation services that would have been provided without the waivered services.</p><p>The commissioner shall seek an amendment to the 1915(c) home and community-based waiver to allow properly licensed adult foster care homes to provide residential services to up to five individuals with developmental disabilities. If the amendment to the waiver is approved, adult foster care providers that can accommodate five individuals shall increase their capacity to five beds, provided the providers continue to meet all applicable licensing requirements.</p><p>(b) The commissioner, in administering home and community-based waivers for persons with developmental disabilities, shall ensure that day services for eligible persons are not provided by the person's residential service provider, unless the person or the person's legal representative is offered a choice of providers and agrees in writing to provision of day services by the residential service provider. The support plan for individuals who choose to have their residential service provider provide their day services must describe how health, safety, protection, and habilitation needs will be met, including how frequent and regular contact with persons other than the residential service provider will occur. The support plan must address the provision of services during the day outside the residence on weekdays.</p><p>(c) When a lead agency is evaluating denials, reductions, or terminations of home and community-based services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0916">256B.0916</a> for an individual, the lead agency shall offer to meet with the individual or the individual's guardian in order to discuss the prioritization of service needs within the support plan. The reduction in the authorized services for an individual due to changes in funding for waivered services may not exceed the amount needed to ensure medically necessary services to meet the individual's health, safety, and welfare.</p><p>(d) The commissioner shall seek federal approval to allow for the reconfiguration of the 1915(c) home and community-based waivers in this section, as authorized under section 1915(c) of the federal Social Security Act, to implement a two-waiver program structure.</p><p>(e) The transition to two disability home and community-based services waiver programs must align with the independent living first policy under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.4905">256B.4905</a>. Unless superseded by any other state or federal law, waiver eligibility criteria shall be the same for each waiver. The waiver program that a person uses shall be determined by the support planning process and whether the person chooses to live in a provider-controlled setting or in the person's own home.</p><p>(f) Prior to July 1, 2024, the commissioner shall seek federal approval for the 1915(c) home and community-based waivers in this section, as authorized under section 1915(c) of the federal Social Security Act, to implement an individual resource allocation methodology.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.5a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.1.21.0">2009 c 79 art 1 s 21</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.5b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.<span class="headnote">Revised per diem based on legislated rate reduction.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/252.28#stat.252.28.3">252.28, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (d), if the 2009 legislature adopts a rate reduction that impacts payment to providers of adult foster care services, the commissioner may issue adult foster care licenses that permit a capacity of five adults. The application for a five-bed license must meet the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.11#stat.245A.11.2a">245A.11, subdivision 2a</a>. Prior to admission of the fifth recipient of adult foster care services, the county must negotiate a revised per diem rate for room and board and waiver services that reflects the legislated rate reduction and results in an overall average per diem reduction for all foster care recipients in that home. The revised per diem must allow the provider to maintain, as much as possible, the level of services or enhanced services provided in the residence, while mitigating the losses of the legislated rate reduction.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall adopt rules to establish required controls, documentation, and reporting of services provided in order to assure proper administration of the approved waiver plan, and to establish policy and procedures to reduce duplicative efforts and unnecessary paperwork on the part of case managers.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Assessments.</span></h2><p>(a) Assessments and reassessments shall be conducted by certified assessors according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>, and must incorporate appropriate referrals to determine eligibility for case management under subdivision 1a.</p><p>(b) For persons with developmental disabilities, a certified assessor shall evaluate the need for an institutional level of care. The assessment shall address whether home and community-based services are appropriate for persons who are at risk of placement in an intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities, or for whom there is reasonable indication that they might require this level of care. The certified assessor shall make an evaluation of need within five working days of an emergency admission of a person to an intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities.</p><p>(c) The certified assessor, with the concurrence of the person, the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, may invite other individuals to attend the assessment. With the permission of the person being assessed or the person's designated legal representative, the person's current provider of services may submit a written report outlining their recommendations regarding the person's care needs prepared by a direct service employee with at least 20 hours of service to that client. The assessor must notify the provider of the date by which this information is to be submitted. This information must be provided to the assessor and the person or the person's legal representative and must be considered prior to the finalization of the assessment.</p><p>(d) Upon federal approval, if during an assessment or reassessment the recipient is determined to be able to have the recipient's needs met through alternative services in a less restrictive setting, the case manager shall help the recipient develop a plan to transition to an appropriate less restrictive setting.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Additional certified assessor duties.</span></h2><p>In addition to the responsibilities of certified assessors described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>, for persons with developmental disabilities, the certified assessor shall:</p><p>(1) identify other noninstitutional public assistance or social service that may prevent or delay long-term residential placement;</p><p>(2) assess whether a person is in need of long-term residential care;</p><p>(3) make recommendations regarding placement and payment for:</p><p>(i) social service or public assistance support, or both, to maintain a person in the person's own home or other place of residence;</p><p>(ii) training and habilitation service, vocational rehabilitation, and employment training activities;</p><p>(iii) community residential service placement;</p><p>(iv) regional treatment center placement; or</p><p>(v) a home and community-based service alternative to community residential service or regional treatment center placement including self-directed service options;</p><p>(4) evaluate the availability, location, and quality of the services listed in clause (3), including the impact of placement alternatives on the person's ability to maintain or improve existing patterns of contact and involvement with parents and other family members;</p><p>(5) identify the cost implications of recommendations in clause (3); and</p><p>(6) make recommendations to a court as may be needed to assist the court in making decisions regarding commitment of persons with developmental disabilities.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.8a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8a.<span class="headnote">County notification.</span></h2><p>(a) If the county of financial responsibility wishes to place a person in another county for services, the county of financial responsibility shall notify the proposed county of service and the placement shall be made cooperatively between the two counties. Arrangements shall be made between the two counties for ongoing social service, including annual reviews of the person's support plan. The county where services are provided may not make changes in the person's support plan without approval by the county of financial responsibility.</p><p>(b) The county of service shall notify the county of financial responsibility if, in the case of an intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities, there has been no authorization for admission by the admission review team as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0926">256B.0926</a>.</p><p>(c) The county of service shall notify the county of financial responsibility of any concerns about the chosen provider's capacity to meet the needs of the person seeking to move to residential services in another county no later than 20 working days following receipt of the written notification. Unless other mutually acceptable arrangements are made by the involved county agencies, the county of financial responsibility is responsible for costs of social services and the costs associated with the development and maintenance of the placement. The county of service may request that the county of financial responsibility purchase case management services from the county of service or from a contracted provider of case management when the county of financial responsibility is not providing case management as defined in this section and rules adopted under this section, unless other mutually acceptable arrangements are made by the involved county agencies. Standards for payment limits under this section may be established by the commissioner. Financial disputes between counties shall be resolved as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256G.09">256G.09</a>. This subdivision also applies to home and community-based waiver services provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Reimbursement.</span></h2><p>Payment for services shall not be provided to a service provider for any person placed in an intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities prior to the person receiving an assessment by a certified assessor. The commissioner shall not deny reimbursement for: (1) a person admitted to an intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities who is assessed to need long-term supportive services, if long-term supportive services other than intermediate care are not available in that community; (2) any person admitted to an intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities under emergency circumstances; (3) any eligible person placed in the intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disabilities pending an appeal of the certified assessor's decision; or (4) any medical assistance recipient when, after full discussion of all appropriate alternatives including those that are expected to be less costly than intermediate care for persons with developmental disabilities, the person or the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the parent if the person is a minor, insists on intermediate care placement. The certified assessor shall provide documentation that the most cost-effective alternatives available were offered to this individual or the individual's legal guardian or conservator.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.10"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Admission of persons to and discharge of persons from regional treatment centers.</span></h2><p>(a) Prior to the admission of a person to a regional treatment center program for persons with developmental disabilities, the case manager shall make efforts to secure community-based alternatives. If these alternatives are rejected by the person, the person's legal guardian or conservator, or the county agency in favor of a regional treatment center placement, the case manager shall document the reasons why the alternatives were rejected.</p><p>(b) Assessment and support planning must be completed in accordance with requirements identified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>.</p><p>(c) No discharge shall take place until disputes are resolved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045#stat.256.045.4a">256.045, subdivision 4a</a>, or until a review by the commissioner is completed upon request of the chief executive officer or program director of the regional treatment center, or the county agency. For persons under public guardianship, the ombudsman may request a review or hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.11"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Residential support services.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) Upon federal approval, there is established a new service called residential support that is available on the community alternative care, community access for disability inclusion, developmental disabilities, and brain injury waivers. Existing waiver service descriptions must be modified to the extent necessary to ensure there is no duplication between other services. Residential support services must be provided by vendors licensed as a community residential setting as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.11#stat.245A.11.8">245A.11, subdivision 8</a>, a foster care setting licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.3000">2960.3000</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.3340">2960.3340</a>, or an adult foster care setting licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.5105">9555.5105</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.6265">9555.6265</a>.</p><p class="in">(b) Residential support services must meet the following criteria:</p><p class="in">(1) the residential site must have a designated person responsible for program management, oversight, development, and implementation of policies and procedures;</p><p class="in">(2) the provider of residential support services must provide supervision, training, and assistance as described in the person's support plan; and</p><p class="in">(3) the provider of residential support services must meet the requirements of licensure and additional requirements of the person's support plan.</p><p class="in">(c) Providers of residential support services that meet the definition in paragraph (a) must be licensed according to chapter 245D. Providers licensed to provide child foster care under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.3000">2960.3000</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.3340">2960.3340</a>, or adult foster care licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.5105">9555.5105</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.6265">9555.6265</a>, and that meet the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.03#stat.245A.03.7">245A.03, subdivision 7</a>, paragraph (f), are considered registered under this section.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.11a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11a.<span class="headnote">Residential support services criteria.</span></h2><p>(a) For the purposes of this subdivision, "residential support services" means the following residential support services reimbursed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.4914">256B.4914</a>: community residential services, customized living services, and 24-hour customized living services.</p><p>(b) In order to increase independent living options for people with disabilities and in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.4905">256B.4905, subdivisions 3</a> and 4, and consistent with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.03#stat.245A.03.7">245A.03, subdivision 7</a>, the commissioner must establish and implement criteria to access residential support services. The criteria for accessing residential support services must prohibit the commissioner from authorizing residential support services unless at least all of the following conditions are met:</p><p>(1) the individual has complex behavioral health or complex medical needs; and</p><p>(2) the individual's service planning team has considered all other available residential service options and determined that those options are inappropriate to meet the individual's support needs.</p><p class="in">(c) Nothing in this subdivision shall be construed as permitting the commissioner to establish criteria prohibiting the authorization of residential support services for individuals described in the statewide priorities established in subdivision 12, the transition populations in subdivision 13, and the licensing moratorium exception criteria under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.03">245A.03</a>, subdivision 7, paragraph (a).</p><p>(d) Individuals with active service agreements for residential support services on the date that the criteria for accessing residential support services become effective are exempt from the requirements of this subdivision, and the exemption from the criteria for accessing residential support services continues to apply for renewals of those service agreements.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.12"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Waiver services statewide priorities.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall establish statewide priorities for individuals on the waiting list for developmental disabilities (DD) waiver services, as of January 1, 2010. The statewide priorities must include, but are not limited to, individuals who continue to have a need for waiver services after they have maximized the use of state plan services and other funding resources, including natural supports, prior to accessing waiver services, and who meet at least one of the following criteria:</p><p>(1) no longer require the intensity of services provided where they are currently living; or</p><p>(2) make a request to move from an institutional setting.</p><p>(b) After the priorities in paragraph (a) are met, priority must also be given to individuals who meet at least one of the following criteria:</p><p>(1) have unstable living situations due to the age, incapacity, or sudden loss of the primary caregivers;</p><p>(2) are moving from an institution due to bed closures;</p><p>(3) experience a sudden closure of their current living arrangement;</p><p>(4) require protection from confirmed abuse, neglect, or exploitation;</p><p>(5) experience a sudden change in need that can no longer be met through state plan services or other funding resources alone; or</p><p>(6) meet other priorities established by the department.</p><p>(c) When allocating new enrollment resources to lead agencies, the commissioner must take into consideration the number of individuals waiting who meet statewide priorities.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.13"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Waiver allocations for transition populations.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall make available additional waiver allocations and additional necessary resources to assure timely discharges from the Anoka-Metro Regional Treatment Center and the Minnesota Security Hospital in St. Peter for individuals who meet the following criteria:</p><p>(1) are otherwise eligible for the developmental disabilities waiver under this section;</p><p>(2) who would otherwise remain at the Anoka-Metro Regional Treatment Center or the Minnesota Security Hospital;</p><p>(3) whose discharge would be significantly delayed without the available waiver allocation; and</p><p>(4) who have met treatment objectives and no longer meet hospital level of care.</p><p>(b) Additional waiver allocations under this subdivision must meet cost-effectiveness requirements of the federal approved waiver plan.</p><p>(c) Any corporate foster care home developed under this subdivision must be considered an exception under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.03#stat.245A.03.7">245A.03, subdivision 7</a>, paragraph (a).</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.092.14"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Reduce avoidable behavioral crisis emergency room admissions, psychiatric inpatient hospitalizations, and commitments to institutions.</span></h2><p>(a) Persons receiving home and community-based services authorized under this section who have had two or more admissions within a calendar year to an emergency room, psychiatric unit, or institution must receive consultation from a mental health professional as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.462#stat.245.462.18">245.462, subdivision 18</a>, or a behavioral professional as defined in the home and community-based services state plan within 30 days of discharge. The mental health professional or behavioral professional must:</p><p>(1) conduct a functional assessment of the crisis incident as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.11">245D.02, subdivision 11</a>, which led to the hospitalization with the goal of developing proactive strategies as well as necessary reactive strategies to reduce the likelihood of future avoidable hospitalizations due to a behavioral crisis;</p><p>(2) use the results of the functional assessment to amend the support plan set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.4b">245D.02, subdivision 4b</a>, to address the potential need for additional staff training, increased staffing, access to crisis mobility services, mental health services, use of technology, and crisis stabilization services in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0624">256B.0624</a>, subdivision 7; and</p><p>(3) identify the need for additional consultation, testing, and mental health crisis intervention team services as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.20">245D.02, subdivision 20</a>, psychotropic medication use and monitoring under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.051">245D.051</a>, and the frequency and duration of ongoing consultation.</p><p>(b) For the purposes of this subdivision, "institution" includes, but is not limited to, the Anoka-Metro Regional Treatment Center and the Minnesota Security Hospital.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.092.history

<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.27.77.0">2014 c 312 art 27 s 77</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/78/#laws.6.31.0">2015 c 78 art 6 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.117.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 117</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.4.6.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 4 s 6</a>,7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.13.16.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 13 s 16</a>-19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.4.36.0">2022 c 98 art 4 s 36</a>; art 17 s 12,13,26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/50/#laws.1.25.0">2023 c 50 art 1 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/61/#laws.1.18.0">2023 c 61 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/108/#laws.1.15.0">2024 c 108 art 1 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/125/#laws.1.17.0">2024 c 125 art 1 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.46.17.0">2024 c 127 art 46 s 17</a></p></div><p><b>NOTE:</b> The amendment to subdivision 4 by Laws 2021, First Special Session chapter 7, article 13, section 16, is effective upon federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2021, First Special Session chapter 7, article 13, section 16, the effective date.</p><p><b>NOTE:</b> The amendments to subdivisions 5 and 12 by Laws 2021, First Special Session chapter 7, article 13, sections 17 and 19, are effective 90 days after federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2021, First Special Session chapter 7, article 13, sections 17 and 19, the effective dates.</p><p><b>NOTE:</b> Subdivision 11a, as added by Laws 2021, First Special Session chapter 7, article 13, section 18, is effective 90 days following federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2021, First Special Session chapter 7, article 13, section 18, the effective date.</p><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0921"><h1 class="shn">256B.0921 HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES INNOVATION POOL.</h1><p class="in">The commissioner of human services shall develop an initiative to provide incentives for innovation in: (1) achieving integrated competitive employment; (2) achieving integrated competitive employment for youth under age 25 upon their graduation from school; (3) living in the most integrated setting; and (4) other outcomes determined by the commissioner. The commissioner shall seek requests for proposals and shall contract with one or more entities to provide incentive payments for meeting identified outcomes.</p></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0921.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.7.55.0">2015 c 71 art 7 s 55</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/189/#laws.18.9.0">2016 c 189 art 18 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.1.19.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 1 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.5.51.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 5 s 51</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0922"><h1 class="shn">256B.0922 ESSENTIAL COMMUNITY SUPPORTS.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0922.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Essential community supports.</span></h2><p>(a) The purpose of the essential community supports program is to provide targeted services to persons age 65 and older who need essential community support, but whose needs do not meet the level of care required for nursing facility placement under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0724#stat.144.0724.11">144.0724, subdivision 11</a>.</p><p>(b) Essential community supports are available not to exceed $400 per person per month. Essential community supports may be used as authorized within an authorization period not to exceed 12 months. Services must be available to a person who:</p><p>(1) is age 65 or older;</p><p>(2) is not eligible for medical assistance;</p><p>(3) has received a community assessment under section 256B.0911, subdivisions 17 to 21, 23, 24, or 27, and does not require the level of care provided in a nursing facility;</p><p>(4) meets the financial eligibility criteria for the alternative care program under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913#stat.256B.0913.4">256B.0913, subdivision 4</a>;</p><p>(5) has an assessment summary; and</p><p>(6) has been determined by a community assessment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0911">256B.0911</a>, subdivisions 17 to 21, 23, 24, or 27, to be a person who would require provision of at least one of the following services, as defined in the approved elderly waiver plan, in order to maintain their community residence:</p><p>(i) adult day services;</p><p>(ii) caregiver support;</p><p>(iii) homemaker support;</p><p>(iv) chores;</p><p>(v) a personal emergency response device or system;</p><p>(vi) home-delivered meals; or</p><p>(vii) community living assistance as defined by the commissioner.</p><p>(c) The person receiving any of the essential community supports in this subdivision must also receive service coordination, not to exceed $600 in a 12-month authorization period, as part of their assessment summary.</p><p>(d) A person who has been determined to be eligible for essential community supports must be reassessed at least annually and continue to meet the criteria in paragraph (b) to remain eligible for essential community supports.</p><p>(e) The commissioner is authorized to use federal matching funds for essential community supports as necessary and to meet demand for essential community supports as outlined in subdivision 2, and that amount of federal funds is appropriated to the commissioner for this purpose.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0922.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Essential community supports for people in transition.</span></h2><p>(a) Essential community supports under subdivision 1 are also available to an individual who:</p><p>(1) is receiving nursing facility services or home and community-based long-term services and supports under chapter 256S or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a> on the effective date of implementation of the revised nursing facility level of care under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0724">144.0724</a>, subdivision 11;</p><p>(2) meets one of the following criteria:</p><p>(i) due to the implementation of the revised nursing facility level of care, loses eligibility for continuing medical assistance payment of nursing facility services at the first reassessment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0724#stat.144.0724.11">144.0724, subdivision 11</a>, paragraph (b), that occurs on or after the effective date of the revised nursing facility level of care criteria under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0724#stat.144.0724.11">144.0724, subdivision 11</a>; or</p><p>(ii) due to the implementation of the revised nursing facility level of care, loses eligibility for continuing medical assistance payment of home and community-based long-term services and supports under chapter 256S or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a> at the first reassessment required under those sections that occurs on or after the effective date of implementation of the revised nursing facility level of care under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0724">144.0724</a>, subdivision 11;</p><p>(3) is not eligible for personal care attendant services; and</p><p>(4) has an assessed need for one or more of the supportive services offered under essential community supports under subdivision 1, paragraph (b), clause (6).</p><p>Individuals eligible under this paragraph includes individuals who continue to be eligible for medical assistance state plan benefits and those who are not or are no longer financially eligible for medical assistance.</p><p>(b) Additional onetime case management is available for participants under paragraph (a), not to exceed $600 per person to be used within one authorization period not to exceed 12 months. This service is provided in addition to the essential community supports benefit described under subdivision 1, paragraph (b).</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0922.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.7.13.0">2013 c 108 art 7 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.8.8.0">2014 c 291 art 8 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/54/#laws.2.32.0">2019 c 54 art 2 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.17.14.0">2022 c 98 art 17 s 14</a>,26</p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0924"><h1 class="shn">256B.0924 TARGETED CASE MANAGEMENT SERVICES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0924.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Purpose.</span></h2><p>The state recognizes that targeted case management services can decrease the need for more costly services such as multiple emergency room visits or hospitalizations by linking eligible individuals with less costly services available in the community.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0924.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given:</p><p>(a) "Targeted case management" means services which will assist medical assistance eligible persons to gain access to needed medical, social, educational, and other services. Targeted case management does not include therapy, treatment, legal, or outreach services.</p><p>(b) "Targeted case management for adults" means activities that coordinate and link social and other services designed to help eligible persons gain access to needed protective services, social, health care, mental health, habilitative, educational, vocational, recreational, advocacy, legal, chemical, health, and other related services.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0924.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Eligibility.</span></h2><p>Persons are eligible to receive targeted case management services under this section if the requirements in paragraphs (a) and (b) are met.</p><p>(a) The person must be assessed and determined by the local county agency to:</p><p>(1) be age 18 or older;</p><p>(2) be receiving medical assistance;</p><p>(3) have significant functional limitations; and</p><p>(4) be in need of service coordination to attain or maintain living in an integrated community setting.</p><p>(b) The person must be a vulnerable adult in need of adult protection as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572">626.5572</a>, or is an adult with a developmental disability as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/252A.02#stat.252A.02.2">252A.02, subdivision 2</a>, or a related condition as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.02">256B.02</a>, subdivision 11, and is not receiving home and community-based waiver services, or is an adult who lacks a permanent residence and who has been without a permanent residence for at least one year or on at least four occasions in the last three years.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0924.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Targeted case management service activities.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) For persons with developmental disabilities, targeted case management services must meet the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>.</p><p class="in">(b) For persons not eligible as a person with a developmental disability, targeted case management service activities include:</p><p class="in">(1) an assessment of the person's need for targeted case management services;</p><p class="in">(2) the development of a written personal service plan;</p><p class="in">(3) a regular review and revision of the written personal service plan with the recipient and the recipient's legal representative, and others as identified by the recipient, to ensure access to necessary services and supports identified in the plan;</p><p class="in">(4) effective communication with the recipient and the recipient's legal representative and others identified by the recipient;</p><p class="in">(5) coordination of referrals for needed services with qualified providers;</p><p class="in">(6) coordination and monitoring of the overall service delivery to ensure the quality and effectiveness of services;</p><p class="in">(7) assistance to the recipient and the recipient's legal representative to help make an informed choice of services;</p><p class="in">(8) advocating on behalf of the recipient when service barriers are encountered or referring the recipient and the recipient's legal representative to an independent advocate;</p><p class="in">(9) monitoring and evaluating services identified in the personal service plan to ensure personal outcomes are met and to ensure satisfaction with services and service delivery;</p><p class="in">(10) conducting face-to-face monitoring with the recipient at least twice a year;</p><p class="in">(11) completing and maintaining necessary documentation that supports and verifies the activities in this section;</p><p class="in">(12) coordinating with the medical assistance facility discharge planner prior to the recipient's discharge into the community; and</p><p class="in">(13) a personal service plan developed and reviewed at least annually with the recipient and the recipient's legal representative. The personal service plan must be revised when there is a change in the recipient's status. The personal service plan must identify:</p><p class="in">(i) the desired personal short and long-term outcomes;</p><p class="in">(ii) the recipient's preferences for services and supports, including development of a person-centered plan if requested; and</p><p class="in">(iii) formal and informal services and supports based on areas of assessment, such as: social, health, mental health, residence, family, educational and vocational, safety, legal, self-determination, financial, and chemical health as determined by the recipient and the recipient's legal representative and the recipient's support network.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0924.4a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Targeted case management through interactive video.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) Subject to federal approval, contact made for targeted case management by interactive video shall be eligible for payment under subdivision 6 if:</p><p class="in">(1) the person receiving targeted case management services is residing in:</p><p class="in">(i) a hospital;</p><p class="in">(ii) a nursing facility; or</p><p class="in">(iii) a residential setting licensed under chapter 245A or 245D or a boarding and lodging establishment or lodging establishment that provides supportive services or health supervision services according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/157.17">157.17</a> that is staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week;</p><p class="in">(2) interactive video is in the best interests of the person and is deemed appropriate by the person receiving targeted case management or the person's legal guardian, the case management provider, and the provider operating the setting where the person is residing;</p><p class="in">(3) the use of interactive video is approved as part of the person's written personal service or case plan; and</p><p class="in">(4) interactive video is used for up to, but not more than, 50 percent of the minimum required face-to-face contact.</p><p class="in">(b) The person receiving targeted case management or the person's legal guardian has the right to choose and consent to the use of interactive video under this subdivision and has the right to refuse the use of interactive video at any time.</p><p class="in">(c) The commissioner shall establish criteria that a targeted case management provider must attest to in order to demonstrate the safety or efficacy of delivering the service via interactive video. The attestation may include that the case management provider has:</p><p class="in">(1) written policies and procedures specific to interactive video services that are regularly reviewed and updated;</p><p class="in">(2) policies and procedures that adequately address client safety before, during, and after the interactive video services are rendered;</p><p class="in">(3) established protocols addressing how and when to discontinue interactive video services; and</p><p class="in">(4) established a quality assurance process related to interactive video services.</p><p class="in">(d) As a condition of payment, the targeted case management provider must document the following for each occurrence of targeted case management provided by interactive video:</p><p class="in">(1) the time the service began and the time the service ended, including an a.m. and p.m. designation;</p><p class="in">(2) the basis for determining that interactive video is an appropriate and effective means for delivering the service to the person receiving case management services;</p><p class="in">(3) the mode of transmission of the interactive video services and records evidencing that a particular mode of transmission was utilized;</p><p class="in">(4) the location of the originating site and the distant site; and</p><p class="in">(5) compliance with the criteria attested to by the targeted case management provider as provided in paragraph (c).</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0924.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Provider standards.</span></h2><p>County boards or providers who contract with the county are eligible to receive medical assistance reimbursement for adult targeted case management services.
