This includes sports activities, exercise groups, activities such as craft hours, leisure time, social hours, meal or snack time, trips to community activities, and tours;</p><p class="in">(ii) a social or educational service that does not have or cannot reasonably be expected to have a therapeutic outcome related to the client's emotional disturbance;</p><p class="in">(iii) prevention or education programs provided to the community; and</p><p class="in">(iv) treatment for clients with primary diagnoses of alcohol or other drug abuse.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0943.13"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Exception to excluded services.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding subdivision 12, up to 15 hours of children's therapeutic services and supports provided within a six-month period to a child with severe emotional disturbance who is residing in a hospital; a residential treatment facility licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.0580">2960.0580</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.0690">2960.0690</a>; a psychiatric residential treatment facility under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.45a">256B.0625, subdivision 45a</a>; a regional treatment center; or other institutional group setting or who is participating in a program of partial hospitalization are eligible for medical assistance payment if part of the discharge plan.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0943.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.4.8.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 4 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/228/#laws.1.38.0">2004 c 228 art 1 s 38</a>-42; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/98/#laws.2.9.0">2005 c 98 art 2 s 9</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/4/#laws.2.11.0">1Sp2005 c 4 art 2 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.8.22.0">2007 c 147 art 8 s 22</a>; art 11 s 18-21; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/234/#laws.0.4.0">2008 c 234 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.7.19.0">2009 c 79 art 7 s 19</a>,21; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/142/#laws.2.38.0">2009 c 142 art 2 s 38</a>-40; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/167/#laws.0.14.0">2009 c 167 s 14</a>-20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/303/#laws.0.5.0">2010 c 303 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/9/#laws.3.4.0">1Sp2011 c 9 art 3 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/247/#laws.5.4.0">2012 c 247 art 5 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/59/#laws.1.2.0">2013 c 59 art 1 s 2</a>-5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.4.22.0">2013 c 108 art 4 s 22</a>-25; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/262/#laws.3.12.0">2014 c 262 art 3 s 12</a>-17; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/78/#laws.2.4.0">2015 c 78 art 2 s 4</a>-12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/79/#laws.0.6.0">2017 c 79 s 6-8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/5/#laws.10.7.0">1Sp2017 c 5 art 10 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.7.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/128/#laws.0.8.0">2018 c 128 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.17.81.0">2021 c 30 art 17 s 81</a>-90; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.6.22.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 6 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.131.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 131</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.6.9.0">2022 c 98 art 6 s 9</a>-15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/25/#laws.0.141.0">2023 c 25 s 141</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/85/#laws.0.70.0">2024 c 85 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.61.24.0">2024 c 127 art 61 s 24</a>,25</p></div><p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendments to subdivisions 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, and 11 by Laws 2022, chapter 98, article 6, sections 9 to 15, are effective upon federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2022, chapter 98, article 6, sections 9 to 15, the effective dates.</p><p><b>NOTE: </b>Subdivision 8a is repealed by Laws 2022, chapter 98, article 6, section 26, effective upon federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2022, chapter 98, article 6, section 26, the effective date.</p><div class="sr" id="stat.256B.0944"><b>256B.0944</b> MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.17.113.0">2021 c 30 art 17 s 113</a>]</div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0945"><h1 class="shn">256B.0945 SERVICES FOR CHILDREN WITH SEVERE EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Residential services; provider qualifications.</span></h2><p>(a) Counties must arrange to provide residential services for children with severe emotional disturbance according to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4882">245.4882</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4885">245.4885</a>, and this section.</p><p>(b) Services must be provided by a facility that is licensed according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4882">245.4882 </a>and administrative rules promulgated thereunder, and under contract with the county.</p><p>(c) Eligible service costs may be claimed for a facility that is located in a state that borders Minnesota if:</p><p>(1) the facility is the closest facility to the child's home, providing the appropriate level of care; and</p><p>(2) the commissioner of human services has completed an inspection of the out-of-state program according to the interagency agreement with the commissioner of corrections under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.198#stat.260B.198.11">260B.198, subdivision 11</a>, paragraph (b), and the program has been certified by the commissioner of corrections under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260B.198#stat.260B.198.11">260B.198, subdivision 11</a>, paragraph (a), to substantially meet the standards applicable to children's residential mental health treatment programs under Minnesota Rules, chapter 2960. Nothing in this section requires the commissioner of human services to enforce the background study requirements under chapter 245C or the requirements related to prevention and investigation of alleged maltreatment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557</a> or chapter 260E. Complaints received by the commissioner of human services must be referred to the out-of-state licensing authority for possible follow-up.</p><p>(d) Notwithstanding paragraph (b), eligible service costs may be claimed for an out-of-state inpatient treatment facility if:</p><p>(1) the facility specializes in providing mental health services to children who are deaf, deafblind, or hard-of-hearing and who use American Sign Language as their first language;</p><p>(2) the facility is licensed by the state in which it is located; and</p><p>(3) the state in which the facility is located is a member state of the Interstate Compact on Mental Health.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Covered services.</span></h2><p>All services must be included in a child's individualized treatment or multiagency plan of care as defined in chapter 245.</p><p>For facilities that are not institutions for mental diseases according to federal statute and regulation, medical assistance covers mental health-related services that are required to be provided by a residential facility under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4882">245.4882</a> and administrative rules promulgated thereunder, except for room and board. For residential facilities determined by the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to be an institution for mental diseases, medical assistance covers medically necessary mental health services provided by the facility according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.055#stat.256B.055.13">256B.055, subdivision 13</a>, except for room and board.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Centralized disbursement of medical assistance payments.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.041">256B.041</a>, county payments for the cost of residential services provided under this section shall not be made to the commissioner of management and budget.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Payment rates.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) Notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.19">256B.19</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.041">256B.041</a>, payments to counties for residential services provided under this section by a residential facility shall:</p><p>(1) for services provided by a residential facility that is not an institution for mental diseases, only be made of federal earnings for services provided, and the nonfederal share of costs for services provided under this section shall be paid by the county from sources other than federal funds or funds used to match other federal funds. Payment to counties for services provided according to this section shall be a proportion of the per day contract rate that relates to rehabilitative mental health services and shall not include payment for costs or services that are billed to the IV-E program as room and board; and</p><p>(2) for services provided by a residential facility that is determined to be an institution for mental diseases, be equivalent to the federal share of the payment that would have been made if the residential facility were not an institution for mental diseases. The portion of the payment representing what would be the nonfederal shares shall be paid by the county. Payment to counties for services provided according to this section shall be a proportion of the per day contract rate that relates to rehabilitative mental health services and shall not include payment for costs or services that are billed to the IV-E program as room and board.</p><p class="in">(b) Per diem rates paid to providers under this section by prepaid plans shall be the proportion of the per-day contract rate that relates to rehabilitative mental health services and shall not include payment for group foster care costs or services that are billed to the county of financial responsibility. Services provided in facilities located in bordering states are eligible for reimbursement on a fee-for-service basis only as described in paragraph (a) and are not covered under prepaid health plans.</p><p class="in">(c) Payment for mental health rehabilitative services provided under this section by or under contract with an American Indian tribe or tribal organization or by agencies operated by or under contract with an American Indian tribe or tribal organization must be made according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.34">256B.0625, subdivision 34</a>, or other relevant federally approved rate-setting methodology.</p><p>(d) The commissioner shall set aside a portion not to exceed five percent of the federal funds earned for county expenditures under this section to cover the state costs of administering this section. Any unexpended funds from the set-aside shall be distributed to the counties in proportion to their earnings under this section.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.17.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 17</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.17.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 17</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.17.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 17</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.17.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 17</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.17.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 17</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0945.10"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.4.24.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 4 s 24</a>]</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0945.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.8.9.0">1999 c 245 art 8 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/340/#laws.0.4.0">2000 c 340 s 4</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/277/#laws.0.19.0">2002 c 277 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/112/#laws.2.50.0">2003 c 112 art 2 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.4.10.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 4 s 10</a>,11; art 11 s 11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.7.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.8.23.0">2007 c 147 art 8 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/101/#laws.2.109.0">2009 c 101 art 2 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/174/#laws.1.5.0">2009 c 174 art 1 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/9/#laws.8.7.0">1Sp2011 c 9 art 8 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/148/#laws.0.1.0">2012 c 148 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.8.71.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 8 s 71</a>,72; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/12/#laws.0.1.0">2019 c 12 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.6.74.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 6 s 74</a>,75; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.92.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 92</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0946"><h1 class="shn">256B.0946 CHILDREN'S INTENSIVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Required covered service components.</span></h2><p>(a) Subject to federal approval, medical assistance covers medically necessary intensive behavioral health treatment services when the services are provided by a provider entity certified under and meeting the standards in this section. The provider entity must make reasonable and good faith efforts to report individual client outcomes to the commissioner, using instruments and protocols approved by the commissioner.</p><p>(b) Intensive behavioral health treatment services to children with mental illness residing in foster family settings or with legal guardians that comprise specific required service components provided in clauses (1) to (6) are reimbursed by medical assistance when they meet the following standards:</p><p>(1) psychotherapy provided by a mental health professional or a clinical trainee;</p><p>(2) crisis planning;</p><p>(3) individual, family, and group psychoeducation services provided by a mental health professional or a clinical trainee;</p><p>(4) clinical care consultation provided by a mental health professional or a clinical trainee;</p><p>(5) individual treatment plan development as defined in section 245I.10, subdivisions 7 and 8; and</p><p>(6) service delivery payment requirements as provided under subdivision 4.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.1a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p><p>(a) "At risk" means the child has experienced severe difficulty in managing mental health and behavior in multiple settings, has received a diagnosis of mental illness within the past 180 days, and meets one of the following criteria:</p><p>(1) has previously been in a residential or inpatient mental health treatment program, including a program licensed under Minnesota Rules, chapter 2960, for mental health issues within the past six months;</p><p>(2) has a history of threatening harm to self or others and has actively engaged in self-harming or threatening behavior in the past 30 days;</p><p>(3) has experienced interventions from mental health service programs, social services, mobile crisis programs, or law enforcement, or experienced the use of seclusion and restraints in school, to maintain safety in the child's home, community, or school within the past 60 days; or</p><p>(4) has a history of repeated intervention from mental health programs, social services, mobile crisis programs, or law enforcement to maintain safety in the child's home, community, or school within the past 60 days.</p><p>(b) "Clinical care consultation" means communication from a treating clinician to other providers working with the same client to inform, inquire, and instruct regarding the client's symptoms, strategies for effective engagement, care and intervention needs, and treatment expectations across service settings, including but not limited to the client's school, social services, day care, probation, home, primary care, medication prescribers, disabilities services, and other mental health providers and to direct and coordinate clinical service components provided to the client and family.</p><p>(c) "Clinical trainee" means a staff person who is qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04">245I.04</a>, subdivision 6.</p><p>(d) "Crisis planning" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4871#stat.245.4871.9a">245.4871, subdivision 9a</a>.</p><p>(e) "Culturally appropriate" means providing mental health services in a manner that incorporates the child's cultural influences into interventions as a way to maximize resiliency factors and utilize cultural strengths and resources to promote overall wellness.</p><p>(f) "Culture" means the distinct ways of living and understanding the world that are used by a group of people and are transmitted from one generation to another or adopted by an individual.</p><p>(g) "Standard diagnostic assessment" means the assessment described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.10#stat.245I.10.6">245I.10, subdivision 6</a>.</p><p>(h) "Family" means a person who is identified by the client or the client's parent or guardian as being important to the client's mental health treatment. Family may include, but is not limited to, parents, foster parents, children, spouse, committed partners, former spouses, persons related by blood or adoption, persons who are a part of the client's permanency plan, or persons who are presently residing together as a family unit.</p><p>(i) "Foster care" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.007#stat.260C.007.18">260C.007, subdivision 18</a>.</p><p>(j) "Foster family setting" means the foster home in which the license holder resides.</p><p>(k) "Individual treatment plan" means the plan described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.10">245I.10, subdivisions 7</a> and 8.</p><p>(l) "Mental health certified family peer specialist" means a staff person who is qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04#stat.245I.04.12">245I.04, subdivision 12</a>.</p><p>(m) "Mental health professional" means a staff person who is qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04">245I.04</a>, subdivision 2.</p><p>(n) "Mental illness" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.29">245I.02, subdivision 29</a>.</p><p>(o) "Parent" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260C.007#stat.260C.007.25">260C.007, subdivision 25</a>.</p><p>(p) "Psychoeducation services" means information or demonstration provided to an individual, family, or group to explain, educate, and support the individual, family, or group in understanding a child's symptoms of mental illness, the impact on the child's development, and needed components of treatment and skill development so that the individual, family, or group can help the child to prevent relapse, prevent the acquisition of comorbid disorders, and achieve optimal mental health and long-term resilience.</p><p>(q) "Psychotherapy" means the treatment described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0671#stat.256B.0671.11">256B.0671, subdivision 11</a>.</p><p>(r) "Team consultation and treatment planning" means the coordination of treatment plans and consultation among providers in a group concerning the treatment needs of the child, including disseminating the child's treatment service schedule to all members of the service team. Team members must include all mental health professionals working with the child, a parent, the child unless the team lead or parent deem it clinically inappropriate, and at least two of the following: an individualized education program case manager; probation agent; children's mental health case manager; child welfare worker, including adoption or guardianship worker; primary care provider; foster parent; and any other member of the child's service team.</p><p>(s) "Trauma" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.38">245I.02, subdivision 38</a>.</p><p>(t) "Treatment supervision" means the supervision described under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.06">245I.06</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Determination of client eligibility.</span></h2><p>An eligible recipient is an individual, from birth through age 20, who is currently placed in a foster home licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.3000">2960.3000</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/2960.3340">2960.3340</a>, or placed in a foster home licensed under the regulations established by a federally recognized Minnesota Tribe, or who is residing in the legal guardian's home and is at risk, and has received: (1) a standard diagnostic assessment within 180 days before the start of service that documents that intensive behavioral health treatment services are medically necessary to ameliorate identified symptoms and functional impairments; and (2) a level of care assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.19">245I.02, subdivision 19</a>, that demonstrates that the individual requires intensive intervention without 24-hour medical monitoring, and a functional assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.17">245I.02, subdivision 17</a>. The level of care assessment and the functional assessment must include information gathered from the placing county, Tribe, or case manager.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Eligible mental health services providers.</span></h2><p>(a) Eligible providers for children's intensive behavioral health services must be certified by the state and must be able to demonstrate the ability to provide all of the services required in this section and meet the standards in chapter 245I, as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.011#stat.245I.011.5">245I.011, subdivision 5</a>.</p><p>(b) For purposes of this section, a provider agency must be:</p><p>(1) a county-operated entity certified by the state;</p><p>(2) an Indian Health Services facility operated by a Tribe or Tribal organization under funding authorized by United States Code, title 25, sections 450f to 450n, or title 3 of the Indian Self-Determination Act, Public Law 93-638, section 638 (facilities or providers); or</p><p>(3) a noncounty entity.</p><p>(c) Certified providers that do not meet the service delivery standards required in this section shall be subject to a decertification process.</p><p>(d) For the purposes of this section, all services delivered to a client must be provided by a mental health professional or a clinical trainee.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Service delivery payment requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) To be eligible for payment under this section, a provider must develop and practice written policies and procedures for children's intensive behavioral health services, consistent with subdivision 1, paragraph (b), and comply with the following requirements in paragraphs (b) to (n).</p><p>(b) Each previous and current mental health, school, and physical health treatment provider must be contacted to request documentation of treatment and assessments that the eligible client has received. This information must be reviewed and incorporated into the standard diagnostic assessment and team consultation and treatment planning review process.</p><p>(c) Each client receiving treatment must be assessed for a trauma history, and the client's treatment plan must document how the results of the assessment will be incorporated into treatment.</p><p>(d) The level of care assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.19">245I.02, subdivision 19</a>, and functional assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.17">245I.02, subdivision 17</a>, must be updated at least every 180 days or prior to discharge from the service, whichever comes first.</p><p>(e) Each client receiving treatment services must have an individual treatment plan that is reviewed, evaluated, and approved every 180 days using the team consultation and treatment planning process.</p><p>(f) Clinical care consultation must be provided in accordance with the client's individual treatment plan.</p><p>(g) Each client must have a crisis plan within ten days of initiating services and must have access to clinical phone support 24 hours per day, seven days per week, during the course of treatment. The crisis plan must demonstrate coordination with the local or regional mobile crisis intervention team.</p><p>(h) Services must be delivered and documented at least three days per week, equaling at least six hours of treatment per week. If the mental health professional, client, and family agree, service units may be temporarily reduced for a period of no more than 60 days in order to meet the needs of the client and family, or as part of transition or on a discharge plan to another service or level of care. The reasons for service reduction must be identified, documented, and included in the treatment plan. Billing and payment are prohibited for days on which no services are delivered and documented.</p><p>(i) Location of service delivery must be in the client's home, day care setting, school, or other community-based setting that is specified on the client's individualized treatment plan.</p><p>(j) Treatment must be developmentally and culturally appropriate for the client.</p><p>(k) Services must be delivered in continual collaboration and consultation with the client's medical providers and, in particular, with prescribers of psychotropic medications, including those prescribed on an off-label basis. Members of the service team must be aware of the medication regimen and potential side effects.</p><p>(l) Parents, siblings, foster parents, legal guardians, and members of the child's permanency plan must be involved in treatment and service delivery unless otherwise noted in the treatment plan.</p><p>(m) Transition planning for the child must be conducted starting with the first treatment plan and must be addressed throughout treatment to support the child's permanency plan and postdischarge mental health service needs.</p><p>(n) In order for a provider to receive the daily per-client encounter rate, at least one of the services listed in subdivision 1, paragraph (b), clauses (1) to (3), must be provided. The services listed in subdivision 1, paragraph (b), clauses (4) and (5), may be included as part of the daily per-client encounter rate.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2><p>MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.17.113.0">2021 c 30 art 17 s 113</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Excluded services.</span></h2><p>(a) Services in clauses (1) to (7) are not covered under this section and are not eligible for medical assistance payment as components of children's intensive behavioral health services, but may be billed separately:</p><p>(1) inpatient psychiatric hospital treatment;</p><p>(2) mental health targeted case management;</p><p>(3) partial hospitalization;</p><p>(4) medication management;</p><p>(5) children's mental health day treatment services;</p><p>(6) crisis response services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0624">256B.0624</a>;</p><p>(7) transportation; and</p><p>(8) mental health certified family peer specialist services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0616">256B.0616</a>.</p><p>(b) Children receiving intensive behavioral health services are not eligible for medical assistance reimbursement for the following services while receiving children's intensive behavioral health services:</p><p>(1) psychotherapy and skills training components of children's therapeutic services and supports under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0943">256B.0943</a>;</p><p>(2) mental health behavioral aide services as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0943">256B.0943</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (l);</p><p>(3) home and community-based waiver services;</p><p>(4) mental health residential treatment; and</p><p>(5) medical assistance room and board rate, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.056#stat.256B.056.5d">256B.056, subdivision 5d</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0946.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Medical assistance payment and rate setting.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall establish a single daily per-client encounter rate for children's intensive behavioral health services. The rate must be constructed to cover only eligible services delivered to an eligible recipient by an eligible provider, as prescribed in subdivision 1, paragraph (b).</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0946.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/4/#laws.2.12.0">1Sp2005 c 4 art 2 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.8.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.8.38.0">2007 c 147 art 8 s 38</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.4.26.0">2013 c 108 art 4 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/78/#laws.2.13.0">2015 c 78 art 2 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/128/#laws.0.10.0">2018 c 128 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.17.91.0">2021 c 30 art 17 s 91</a>-96; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.11.27.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 11 s 27</a>,28; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.4.37.0">2022 c 98 art 4 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/99/#laws.1.17.0">2022 c 99 art 1 s 17</a>-23,48; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/50/#laws.4.7.0">2023 c 50 art 4 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.9.37.0">2023 c 70 art 9 s 37</a>; art 17 s 45</p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0947"><h1 class="shn">256B.0947 INTENSIVE REHABILITATIVE MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2><p> Subject to federal approval, medical assistance covers medically necessary, intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services when the services are provided by an entity meeting the standards in this section. The provider entity must make reasonable and good faith efforts to report individual client outcomes to the commissioner, using instruments and protocols approved by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p><p>(a) "Intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services" means child rehabilitative mental health services as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0943">256B.0943</a>, except that these services are provided by a multidisciplinary staff using a total team approach consistent with assertive community treatment, as adapted for youth, and are directed to recipients who are eight years of age or older and under 21 years of age who require intensive services to prevent admission to an inpatient psychiatric hospital or placement in a residential treatment facility or who require intensive services to step down from inpatient or residential care to community-based care.</p><p>(b) "Co-occurring mental illness and substance use disorder" means a dual diagnosis of at least one form of mental illness and at least one substance use disorder. Substance use disorders include alcohol or drug abuse or dependence, excluding nicotine use.</p><p>(c) "Standard diagnostic assessment" means the assessment described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.10#stat.245I.10.6">245I.10, subdivision 6</a>.</p><p>(d) "Medication education services" means services provided individually or in groups, which focus on:</p><p>(1) educating the client and client's family or significant nonfamilial supporters about mental illness and symptoms;</p><p>(2) the role and effects of medications in treating symptoms of mental illness; and</p><p>(3) the side effects of medications.</p><p class="bl">Medication education is coordinated with medication management services and does not duplicate it. Medication education services are provided by physicians, pharmacists, or registered nurses with certification in psychiatric and mental health care.</p><p>(e) "Mental health professional" means a staff person who is qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04#stat.245I.04.2">245I.04, subdivision 2</a>.</p><p>(f) "Provider agency" means a for-profit or nonprofit organization established to administer an assertive community treatment for youth team.</p><p>(g) "Substance use disorders" means one or more of the disorders defined in the diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders, current edition.</p><p>(h) "Transition services" means:</p><p>(1) activities, materials, consultation, and coordination that ensures continuity of the client's care in advance of and in preparation for the client's move from one stage of care or life to another by maintaining contact with the client and assisting the client to establish provider relationships;</p><p>(2) providing the client with knowledge and skills needed posttransition;</p><p>(3) establishing communication between sending and receiving entities;</p><p>(4) supporting a client's request for service authorization and enrollment; and</p><p>(5) establishing and enforcing procedures and schedules.</p><p>(i) "Treatment team" means all staff who provide services to recipients under this section.</p><p>(j) "Family peer specialist" means a staff person who is qualified under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0616">256B.0616</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Client eligibility.</span></h2><p>An eligible recipient is an individual who:</p><p>(1) is eight years of age or older and under 21 years of age;</p><p>(2) is diagnosed with a serious mental illness or co-occurring mental illness and substance use disorder, for which intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services are needed;</p><p>(3) has received a level of care assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.19">245I.02, subdivision 19</a>, that indicates a need for intensive integrated intervention without 24-hour medical monitoring and a need for extensive collaboration among multiple providers;</p><p>(4) has received a functional assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.17">245I.02, subdivision 17</a>, that indicates functional impairment and a history of difficulty in functioning safely and successfully in the community, school, home, or job; or who is likely to need services from the adult mental health system during adulthood; and</p><p>(5) has had a recent standard diagnostic assessment that documents that intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services are medically necessary to ameliorate identified symptoms and functional impairments and to achieve individual transition goals.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.3a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Required service components.</span></h2><p>(a) Intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services, supports, and ancillary activities that are covered by a single daily rate per client must include the following, as needed by the individual client:</p><p>(1) individual, family, and group psychotherapy;</p><p>(2) individual, family, and group skills training, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0943">256B.0943</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (u);</p><p>(3) crisis planning as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4871#stat.245.4871.9a">245.4871, subdivision 9a</a>;</p><p>(4) medication management provided by a physician, an advanced practice registered nurse with certification in psychiatric and mental health care, or a physician assistant;</p><p>(5) mental health case management as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.20">256B.0625, subdivision 20</a>;</p><p>(6) medication education services as defined in this section;</p><p>(7) care coordination by a client-specific lead worker assigned by and responsible to the treatment team;</p><p>(8) psychoeducation of and consultation and coordination with the client's biological, adoptive, or foster family and, in the case of a youth living independently, the client's immediate nonfamilial support network;</p><p>(9) clinical consultation to a client's employer or school or to other service agencies or to the courts to assist in managing the mental illness or co-occurring disorder and to develop client support systems;</p><p>(10) coordination with, or performance of, crisis intervention and stabilization services as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0624">256B.0624</a>;</p><p>(11) transition services;</p><p>(12) co-occurring substance use disorder treatment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.11">245I.02, subdivision 11</a>; and</p><p>(13) housing access support that assists clients to find, obtain, retain, and move to safe and adequate housing. Housing access support does not provide monetary assistance for rent, damage deposits, or application fees.</p><p>(b) The provider shall ensure and document the following by means of performing the required function or by contracting with a qualified person or entity: client access to crisis intervention services, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0624">256B.0624</a>, and available 24 hours per day and seven days per week.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Provider contract requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) The intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services provider agency shall have a contract with the commissioner to provide intensive transition youth rehabilitative mental health services.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall develop performance evaluation criteria for providers, including county providers, and may require applicants and providers to submit documentation as needed to allow the commissioner to determine whether the criteria are met.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Standards for intensive nonresidential rehabilitative providers.</span></h2><p>(a) Services must meet the standards in this section and chapter 245I as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.011#stat.245I.011.5">245I.011, subdivision 5</a>.</p><p>(b) The treatment team must have specialized training in providing services to the specific age group of youth that the team serves. An individual treatment team must serve youth who are: (1) at least eight years of age or older and under 16 years of age, or (2) at least 14 years of age or older and under 21 years of age.</p><p>(c) The treatment team for intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services comprises both permanently employed core team members and client-specific team members as follows:</p><p>(1) Based on professional qualifications and client needs, clinically qualified core team members are assigned on a rotating basis as the client's lead worker to coordinate a client's care. The core team must comprise at least four full-time equivalent direct care staff and must minimally include:</p><p>(i) a mental health professional who serves as team leader to provide administrative direction and treatment supervision to the team;</p><p>(ii) an advanced-practice registered nurse with certification in psychiatric or mental health care or a board-certified child and adolescent psychiatrist, either of which must be credentialed to prescribe medications;</p><p>(iii) a mental health certified peer specialist who is qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04#stat.245I.04.10">245I.04, subdivision 10</a>, and is also a former children's mental health consumer; and</p><p>(iv) a co-occurring disorder specialist who meets the requirements under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0622#stat.256B.0622.7a">256B.0622, subdivision 7a</a>, paragraph (a), clause (4), who will provide or facilitate the provision of co-occurring disorder treatment to clients.</p><p>(2) The core team may also include any of the following:</p><p>(i) additional mental health professionals;</p><p>(ii) a vocational specialist;</p><p>(iii) an educational specialist with knowledge and experience working with youth regarding special education requirements and goals, special education plans, and coordination of educational activities with health care activities;</p><p>(iv) a child and adolescent psychiatrist who may be retained on a consultant basis;</p><p>(v) a clinical trainee qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04#stat.245I.04.6">245I.04, subdivision 6</a>;</p><p>(vi) a mental health practitioner qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04#stat.245I.04.4">245I.04, subdivision 4</a>;</p><p>(vii) a case management service provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4871#stat.245.4871.4">245.4871, subdivision 4</a>;</p><p>(viii) a housing access specialist; and</p><p>(ix) a family peer specialist as defined in subdivision 2, paragraph (j).</p><p>(3) A treatment team may include, in addition to those in clause (1) or (2), ad hoc members not employed by the team who consult on a specific client and who must accept overall clinical direction from the treatment team for the duration of the client's placement with the treatment team and must be paid by the provider agency at the rate for a typical session by that provider with that client or at a rate negotiated with the client-specific member. Client-specific treatment team members may include:</p><p>(i) the mental health professional treating the client prior to placement with the treatment team;</p><p>(ii) the client's current substance use counselor, if applicable;</p><p>(iii) a lead member of the client's individualized education program team or school-based mental health provider, if applicable;</p><p>(iv) a representative from the client's health care home or primary care clinic, as needed to ensure integration of medical and behavioral health care;</p><p>(v) the client's probation officer or other juvenile justice representative, if applicable; and</p><p>(vi) the client's current vocational or employment counselor, if applicable.</p><p>(d) The treatment supervisor shall be an active member of the treatment team and shall function as a practicing clinician at least on a part-time basis. The treatment team shall meet with the treatment supervisor at least weekly to discuss recipients' progress and make rapid adjustments to meet recipients' needs. The team meeting must include client-specific case reviews and general treatment discussions among team members. Client-specific case reviews and planning must be documented in the individual client's treatment record.</p><p>(e) The staffing ratio must not exceed ten clients to one full-time equivalent treatment team position.</p><p>(f) The treatment team shall serve no more than 80 clients at any one time. Should local demand exceed the team's capacity, an additional team must be established rather than exceed this limit.</p><p>(g) Nonclinical staff shall have prompt access in person or by telephone to a mental health practitioner, clinical trainee, or mental health professional. The provider shall have the capacity to promptly and appropriately respond to emergent needs and make any necessary staffing adjustments to ensure the health and safety of clients.</p><p>(h) The intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services provider shall participate in evaluation of the assertive community treatment for youth (Youth ACT) model as conducted by the commissioner, including the collection and reporting of data and the reporting of performance measures as specified by contract with the commissioner.</p><p>(i) A regional treatment team may serve multiple counties.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Service standards.</span></h2><p>The standards in this subdivision apply to intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services.</p><p>(a) The treatment team must use team treatment, not an individual treatment model.</p><p>(b) Services must be available at times that meet client needs.</p><p>(c) Services must be age-appropriate and meet the specific needs of the client.</p><p>(d) The level of care assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.19">245I.02, subdivision 19</a>, and functional assessment as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.02#stat.245I.02.17">245I.02, subdivision 17</a>, must be updated at least every six months or prior to discharge from the service, whichever comes first.</p><p>(e) The treatment team must complete an individual treatment plan for each client, according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.10">245I.10, subdivisions 7</a> and 8, and the individual treatment plan must:</p><p>(1) be completed in consultation with the client's current therapist and key providers and provide for ongoing consultation with the client's current therapist to ensure therapeutic continuity and to facilitate the client's return to the community. For clients under the age of 18, the treatment team must consult with parents and guardians in developing the treatment plan;</p><p>(2) if a need for substance use disorder treatment is indicated by validated assessment:</p><p>(i) identify goals, objectives, and strategies of substance use disorder treatment;</p><p>(ii) develop a schedule for accomplishing substance use disorder treatment goals and objectives; and</p><p>(iii) identify the individuals responsible for providing substance use disorder treatment services and supports; and</p><p>(3) provide for the client's transition out of intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services by defining the team's actions to assist the client and subsequent providers in the transition to less intensive or "stepped down" services.</p><p>(f) The treatment team shall actively and assertively engage the client's family members and significant others by establishing communication and collaboration with the family and significant others and educating the family and significant others about the client's mental illness, symptom management, and the family's role in treatment, unless the team knows or has reason to suspect that the client has suffered or faces a threat of suffering any physical or mental injury, abuse, or neglect from a family member or significant other.</p><p>(g) For a client age 18 or older, the treatment team may disclose to a family member, other relative, or a close personal friend of the client, or other person identified by the client, the protected health information directly relevant to such person's involvement with the client's care, as provided in Code of Federal Regulations, title 45, part 164.502(b). If the client is present, the treatment team shall obtain the client's agreement, provide the client with an opportunity to object, or reasonably infer from the circumstances, based on the exercise of professional judgment, that the client does not object. If the client is not present or is unable, by incapacity or emergency circumstances, to agree or object, the treatment team may, in the exercise of professional judgment, determine whether the disclosure is in the best interests of the client and, if so, disclose only the protected health information that is directly relevant to the family member's, relative's, friend's, or client-identified person's involvement with the client's health care. The client may orally agree or object to the disclosure and may prohibit or restrict disclosure to specific individuals.</p><p>(h) The treatment team shall provide interventions to promote positive interpersonal relationships.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Medical assistance payment and rate setting.</span></h2><p>(a) Payment for services in this section must be based on one daily encounter rate per provider inclusive of the following services received by an eligible client in a given calendar day: all rehabilitative services, supports, and ancillary activities under this section, staff travel time to provide rehabilitative services under this section, and crisis response services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0624">256B.0624</a>.</p><p>(b) Payment must not be made to more than one entity for each client for services provided under this section on a given day. If services under this section are provided by a team that includes staff from more than one entity, the team shall determine how to distribute the payment among the members.</p><p>(c) The commissioner shall establish regional cost-based rates for entities that will bill medical assistance for nonresidential intensive rehabilitative mental health services. In developing these rates, the commissioner shall consider:</p><p>(1) the cost for similar services in the health care trade area;</p><p>(2) actual costs incurred by entities providing the services;</p><p>(3) the intensity and frequency of services to be provided to each client;</p><p>(4) the degree to which clients will receive services other than services under this section; and</p><p>(5) the costs of other services that will be separately reimbursed.</p><p>(d) The rate for a provider must not exceed the rate charged by that provider for the same service to other payers.</p><p>(e) Effective for the rate years beginning on and after January 1, 2024, rates must be annually adjusted for inflation using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Economic Index, as forecasted in the third quarter of the calendar year before the rate year. The inflation adjustment must be based on the 12-month period from the midpoint of the previous rate year to the midpoint of the rate year for which the rate is being determined.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.7a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Noncovered services.</span></h2><p>(a) The rate for intensive rehabilitative mental health services does not include medical assistance payment for services in clauses (1) to (7). Services not covered under this paragraph may be billed separately:</p><p>(1) inpatient psychiatric hospital treatment;</p><p>(2) partial hospitalization;</p><p>(3) children's mental health day treatment services;</p><p>(4) physician services outside of care provided by a psychiatrist serving as a member of the treatment team;</p><p>(5) medical assistance room and board rate, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.056#stat.256B.056.5d">256B.056, subdivision 5d</a>;</p><p>(6) home and community-based waiver services; and</p><p>(7) other mental health services identified in the child's individualized education program.</p><p>(b) The following services are not covered under this section and are not eligible for medical assistance payment while youth are receiving intensive rehabilitative mental health services:</p><p>(1) mental health residential treatment; and</p><p>(2) mental health behavioral aide services, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0943">256B.0943</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (l).</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Provider enrollment.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall establish and administer treatment teams with consideration given to regional distribution. Providers shall apply directly to the commissioner for enrollment and must be reimbursed at rates established by contract. The commissioner shall perform the program review.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0947.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Service authorization.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall publish prior authorization criteria and standards to be used for intensive nonresidential rehabilitative mental health services, as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.25">256B.0625, subdivision 25</a>.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0947.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/4/#laws.2.13.0">1Sp2005 c 4 art 2 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.7.23.0">2009 c 79 art 7 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/200/#laws.1.7.0">2010 c 200 art 1 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/86/#laws.0.20.0">2011 c 86 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/11/#laws.3.12.0">1Sp2011 c 11 art 3 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/275/#laws.1.62.0">2014 c 275 art 1 s 62</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/78/#laws.2.14.0">2015 c 78 art 2 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.119.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 119</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/163/#laws.2.6.0">2016 c 163 art 2 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.2.25.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 2 s 25</a>-28; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.13.55.0">2021 c 30 art 13 s 55</a>; art 17 s 97-103; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.11.29.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 11 s 29</a>-31; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.132.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 132</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.151.0">2022 c 58 s 151</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.4.38.0">2022 c 98 art 4 s 38</a>,39; art 6 s 16-18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/25/#laws.0.142.0">2023 c 25 s 142</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.1.29.0">2023 c 70 art 1 s 29</a>; art 17 s 46; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.55.12.0">2024 c 127 art 55 s 12</a>; art 61 s 26</p></div><p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 7 by Laws 2023, chapter 70, article 1, section 29, is effective upon federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2023, chapter 70, article 1, section 29, the effective date.</p><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0948"><h1 class="shn">256B.0948 FOSTER CARE RATE LIMITS.</h1><p>The commissioner shall decrease by five percent rates for adult foster care and supportive living services that are reimbursed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>, and are above the 95th percentile of the statewide rates for the service. The reduction in rates shall take into account the acuity of individuals served based on the methodology used to allocate dollars to local lead agency budgets, and assure that affected service rates are not reduced below the rate level represented by the above percentile due to this rate change. Lead agency contracts for services specified in this section shall be amended to implement these rate changes for services rendered on or after July 1, 2009. The commissioner shall make corresponding reductions to waiver allocations and capitated rates.</p></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.0948.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.55.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 55</a></p></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.0949"><h1 class="shn">256B.0949 EARLY INTENSIVE DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION BENEFIT.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Purpose.</span></h2><p>This section authorizes the early intensive developmental and behavioral intervention (EIDBI) benefit to provide early intensive intervention to a person with an autism spectrum disorder or a related condition. This benefit must provide coverage for a comprehensive, multidisciplinary evaluation, ongoing progress monitoring, and medically necessary early intensive treatment of autism spectrum disorder or a related condition. Nothing in this section shall preclude coverage for other medical assistance benefits based on a person's diagnosis of an autism spectrum disorder or a related condition, including, but not limited to, coverage under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0943">256B.0943</a> of children's therapeutic services and supports.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>(a) The terms used in this section have the meanings given in this subdivision.</p><p>(b) "Advanced certification" means a person who has completed advanced certification in an approved modality under subdivision 13, paragraph (b).</p><p>(c) "Agency" means the legal entity that is enrolled with Minnesota health care programs as a medical assistance provider according to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0195">9505.0195</a>, to provide EIDBI services and that has the legal responsibility to ensure that its employees or contractors carry out the responsibilities defined in this section. Agency includes a licensed individual professional who practices independently and acts as an agency.</p><p>(d) "Autism spectrum disorder or a related condition" or "ASD or a related condition" means either autism spectrum disorder (ASD) as defined in the current version of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) or a condition that is found to be closely related to ASD, as identified under the current version of the DSM, and meets all of the following criteria:</p><p>(1) is severe and chronic;</p><p>(2) results in impairment of adaptive behavior and function similar to that of a person with ASD;</p><p>(3) requires treatment or services similar to those required for a person with ASD; and</p><p>(4) results in substantial functional limitations in three core developmental deficits of ASD: social or interpersonal interaction; functional communication, including nonverbal or social communication; and restrictive or repetitive behaviors or hyperreactivity or hyporeactivity to sensory input; and may include deficits or a high level of support in one or more of the following domains:</p><p>(i) behavioral challenges and self-regulation;</p><p>(ii) cognition;</p><p>(iii) learning and play;</p><p>(iv) self-care; or</p><p>(v) safety.</p><p>(e) "Person" means a person under 21 years of age.</p><p>(f) "Clinical supervision" means the overall responsibility for the control and direction of EIDBI service delivery, including individual treatment planning, staff supervision, individual treatment plan progress monitoring, and treatment review for each person. Clinical supervision is provided by a qualified supervising professional (QSP) who takes full professional responsibility for the service provided by each supervisee.</p><p>(g) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of human services, unless otherwise specified.</p><p>(h) "Comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation" or "CMDE" means a comprehensive evaluation of a person to determine medical necessity for EIDBI services based on the requirements in subdivision 5.</p><p>(i) "Department" means the Department of Human Services, unless otherwise specified.</p><p>(j) "Early intensive developmental and behavioral intervention benefit" or "EIDBI benefit" means a variety of individualized, intensive treatment modalities approved and published by the commissioner that are based in behavioral and developmental science consistent with best practices on effectiveness.</p><p>(k) "Generalizable goals" means results or gains that are observed during a variety of activities over time with different people, such as providers, family members, other adults, and people, and in different environments including, but not limited to, clinics, homes, schools, and the community.</p><p>(l) "Incident" means when any of the following occur:</p><p>(1) an illness, accident, or injury that requires first aid treatment;</p><p>(2) a bump or blow to the head; or</p><p>(3) an unusual or unexpected event that jeopardizes the safety of a person or staff, including a person leaving the agency unattended.</p><p>(m) "Individual treatment plan" or "ITP" means the person-centered, individualized written plan of care that integrates and coordinates person and family information from the CMDE for a person who meets medical necessity for the EIDBI benefit. An individual treatment plan must meet the standards in subdivision 6.</p><p>(n) "Legal representative" means the parent of a child who is under 18 years of age, a court-appointed guardian, or other representative with legal authority to make decisions about service for a person. For the purpose of this subdivision, "other representative with legal authority to make decisions" includes a health care agent or an attorney-in-fact authorized through a health care directive or power of attorney.</p><p>(o) "Mental health professional" means a staff person who is qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04">245I.04</a>, subdivision 2.</p><p>(p) "Person-centered" means a service that both responds to the identified needs, interests, values, preferences, and desired outcomes of the person or the person's legal representative and respects the person's history, dignity, and cultural background and allows inclusion and participation in the person's community.</p><p>(q) "Qualified EIDBI provider" means a person who is a QSP or a level I, level II, or level III treatment provider.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">EIDBI eligibility.</span></h2><p>An EIDBI service is available to a person enrolled in medical assistance who:</p><p>(1) has a diagnosis of ASD or a related condition that meets the criteria of subdivision 4; and</p><p>(2) meets the criteria for medical necessity for the EIDBI benefit.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.3a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Culturally and linguistically appropriate requirement.</span></h2><p>The person's and family's primary spoken language and culture, values, goals, and preferences must be reflected throughout the covered services. The CMDE provider and QSP must determine how to adapt the evaluation, treatment recommendations, and individual treatment plan to the person's and family's culture, values, and language preferences. A provider must have a limited English proficiency (LEP) plan in compliance with title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, United States Code, title 42, section 2000d to 2000d-7.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Diagnosis.</span></h2><p>(a) A diagnosis of ASD or a related condition must:</p><p>(1) be based upon current DSM criteria including direct observations of the person and information from the person's legal representative or primary caregivers;</p><p>(2) be completed by either (i) a licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant, or (ii) a mental health professional; and</p><p>(3) meet the requirements of a standard diagnostic assessment according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.10#stat.245I.10.6">245I.10, subdivision 6</a>.</p><p>(b) Additional assessment information may be considered to complete a diagnostic assessment including specialized tests administered through special education evaluations and licensed school personnel, and from professionals licensed in the fields of medicine, speech and language, psychology, occupational therapy, and physical therapy. A diagnostic assessment may include treatment recommendations.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation.</span></h2><p>(a) A CMDE must be completed to determine medical necessity of EIDBI services. For the commissioner to authorize EIDBI services, the CMDE provider must submit the CMDE to the commissioner and the person or the person's legal representative as determined by the commissioner. Information and assessments must be performed, reviewed, and relied upon for the eligibility determination, treatment and services recommendations, and treatment plan development for the person.</p><p>(b) The CMDE provider must review the diagnostic assessment to confirm the person has an eligible diagnosis and the diagnostic assessment meets standards required under subdivision 4. If the CMDE provider elects to complete the diagnostic assessment at the same time as the CMDE, the CMDE provider must certify that the CMDE meets all standards as required under subdivision 4.</p><p>(c) The CMDE must:</p><p>(1) include an assessment of the person's developmental skills, functional behavior, needs, and capacities based on direct observation of the person which must be administered by a CMDE provider, include medical or assessment information from the person's physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant, and may also include input from family members, school personnel, child care providers, or other caregivers, as well as any medical or assessment information from other licensed professionals such as rehabilitation or habilitation therapists, licensed school personnel, or mental health professionals;</p><p>(2) include and document the person's legal representative's or primary caregiver's preferences for involvement in the person's treatment; and</p><p>(3) provide information about the range of current EIDBI treatment modalities recognized by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.5a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation provider qualification.</span></h2><p>A CMDE provider must:</p><p>(1) be a licensed physician, an advanced practice registered nurse, a physician assistant, a mental health professional, or a clinical trainee who is qualified according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245I.04#stat.245I.04.6">245I.04, subdivision 6</a>;</p><p>(2) have at least 2,000 hours of clinical experience in the evaluation and treatment of people with ASD or a related condition or equivalent documented coursework at the graduate level by an accredited university in the following content areas: ASD or a related condition diagnosis, ASD or a related condition treatment strategies, and child development; and</p><p>(3) be able to diagnose, evaluate, or provide treatment within the provider's scope of practice and professional license.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Individual treatment plan.</span></h2><p>(a) The QSP, level I treatment provider, or level II treatment provider who integrates and coordinates person and family information from the CMDE and ITP progress monitoring process to develop the ITP must develop and monitor the ITP.</p><p>(b) Each person's ITP must be:</p><p>(1) culturally and linguistically appropriate, as required under subdivision 3a, individualized, and person-centered; and</p><p>(2) based on the diagnosis and CMDE information specified in subdivisions 4 and 5.</p><p>(c) The ITP must specify:</p><p>(1) the medically necessary treatment and service;</p><p>(2) the treatment modality that shall be used to meet the goals and objectives, including:</p><p>(i) baseline measures and projected dates of accomplishment;</p><p>(ii) the frequency, intensity, location, and duration of each service provided;</p><p>(iii) the level of legal representative or primary caregiver training and counseling;</p><p>(iv) any change or modification to the physical and social environments necessary to provide a service;</p><p>(v) significant changes in the person's condition or family circumstance;</p><p>(vi) techniques that support and are consistent with the person's communication mode and learning style;</p><p>(vii) the name of the QSP; and</p><p>(viii) progress monitoring results and goal mastery data; and</p><p>(3) the discharge criteria that must be used and a defined transition plan that meets the requirement of paragraph (g).</p><p>(d) Implementation of the ITP must be supervised by a QSP.</p><p>(e) The ITP must be submitted to the commissioner and the person or the person's legal representative for approval in a manner determined by the commissioner for this purpose.</p><p>(f) A service included in the ITP must meet all applicable requirements for medical necessity and coverage.</p><p>(g) To terminate service, the provider must send notice of termination to the person or the person's legal representative. The transition period begins when the person or the person's legal representative receives notice of termination from the EIDBI service and ends when the EIDBI service is terminated. Up to 30 days of continued service is allowed during the transition period. Services during the transition period shall be consistent with the ITP. The transition plan must include:</p><p>(1) protocols for changing service when medically necessary;</p><p>(2) how the transition will occur;</p><p>(3) the time allowed to make the transition; and</p><p>(4) a description of how the person or the person's legal representative will be informed of and involved in the transition.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Individual treatment plan progress monitoring.</span></h2><p>(a) An ITP progress monitoring must be submitted after each six months of treatment, or more frequently as determined by the CMDE provider or QSP, to determine if progress is being made toward targeted functional and generalizable goals specified in the ITP. Based on the results of ITP progress monitoring, the ITP must be adjusted as needed and must document that the EIDBI service continues to be medically necessary for the person or the person is referred to other services.</p><p>(b) The ITP progress monitoring must include:</p><p>(1) input from the person's legal representative or the person's primary caregiver;</p><p>(2) an observation of the person that is performed by the QSP, level I treatment provider, or level II treatment provider and may include input from licensed special education staff or other licensed health care provider;</p><p>(3) documentation of the person's current level of performance on primary treatment goal domains including when a goal or objective is achieved, changed, or discontinued;</p><p>(4) any significant change in the person's condition or family circumstances;</p><p>(5) any treatment plan modification and the rationale for any change made, including treatment modality, intensity, frequency, and duration; and</p><p>(6) recommendations for continued treatment.</p><p>(c) The ITP progress monitoring must be submitted to the commissioner and the person or the person's legal representative in a manner determined by the commissioner for the reauthorization of EIDBI services.</p><p>(d) A person who continues to make reasonable progress toward treatment goals as specified in the ITP is eligible to continue receiving EIDBI services.</p><p>(e) A person's treatment shall continue during the ITP progress monitoring using the process determined under this subdivision. Treatment may continue during an appeal pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Refining the benefit with stakeholders.</span></h2><p>Before making revisions to the EIDBI benefit or proposing statutory changes to this section, the commissioner must consult with stakeholders and consider recommendations from the Department of Human Services Early Intensive Developmental and Behavioral Intervention Advisory Council, the early intensive developmental and behavioral intervention learning collaborative, and the Departments of Health, Education, Employment and Economic Development, and Human Services. Revisions and proposed statutory changes subject to this subdivision include, but are not limited to, the following components:</p><p>(1) a definition of the qualifications, standards, and roles of the treatment team, including recommendations after stakeholder consultation on whether board-certified behavior analysts and other professionals certified in other treatment approaches recognized by the department or trained in ASD or a related condition and child development should be added as professionals qualified to provide EIDBI clinical supervision or other functions under medical assistance;</p><p>(2) refinement of uniform parameters for CMDE and ongoing ITP progress monitoring standards;</p><p>(3) the design of an effective and consistent process for assessing the person's and the person's legal representative's and the person's caregiver's preferences and options to participate in the person's early intervention treatment and efficacy of methods to involve and educate the person's legal representative and caregiver in the treatment of the person;</p><p>(4) formulation of a collaborative process in which professionals have opportunities to collectively inform provider standards and qualifications; standards for CMDE; medical necessity determination; efficacy of treatment apparatus, including modality, intensity, frequency, and duration; and ITP progress monitoring processes to support quality improvement of EIDBI services;</p><p>(5) coordination of this benefit and its interaction with other services provided by the Departments of Human Services, Health, Employment and Economic Development, and Education;</p><p>(6) evaluation, on an ongoing basis, of EIDBI services outcomes and efficacy of treatment modalities provided to people under this benefit; and</p><p>(7) as provided under subdivision 17, determination of the availability of qualified EIDBI providers with necessary expertise and training in ASD or a related condition throughout the state to assess whether there are sufficient professionals to provide timely access and prevent delay in the CMDE and treatment of a person with ASD or a related condition.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.0949.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Revision of treatment modalities.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner may revise covered treatment modalities as needed based on outcome data and other evidence.
