href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/99/#laws.1.43.0">2016 c 99 art 1 s 43</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.2t"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2t.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/99/#laws.1.43.0">2016 c 99 art 1 s 43</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Property-related costs after July 1, 1985.</span></h2><p>(a) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1985, the commissioner, by permanent rule, shall reimburse nursing facility providers that are vendors in the medical assistance program for the rental use of real estate and depreciable equipment. "Real estate" means land improvements, buildings, and attached fixtures used directly for resident care. "Depreciable equipment" means the standard movable resident care equipment and support service equipment generally used in long-term care facilities.</p><p>(b) In developing the method for determining payment rates for the rental use of nursing facilities, the commissioner shall consider factors designed to:</p><p>(1) simplify the administrative procedures for determining payment rates for property-related costs;</p><p>(2) minimize discretionary or appealable decisions;</p><p>(3) eliminate any incentives to sell nursing facilities;</p><p>(4) recognize legitimate costs of preserving and replacing property;</p><p>(5) recognize the existing costs of outstanding indebtedness allowable under the statutes and rules in effect on May 1, 1983;</p><p>(6) address the current value of, if used directly for patient care, land improvements, buildings, attached fixtures, and equipment;</p><p>(7) establish an investment per bed limitation;</p><p>(8) reward efficient management of capital assets;</p><p>(9) provide equitable treatment of facilities;</p><p>(10) consider a variable rate; and</p><p>(11) phase-in implementation of the rental reimbursement method.</p><p>(c) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1987, a nursing facility which has reduced licensed bed capacity after January 1, 1986, shall be allowed to:</p><p>(1) aggregate the applicable investment per bed limits based on the number of beds licensed prior to the reduction; and</p><p>(2) establish capacity days for each rate year following the licensure reduction based on the number of beds licensed on the previous April 1 if the commissioner is notified of the change by April 4. The notification must include a copy of the delicensure request that has been submitted to the commissioner of health.</p><p>(d) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1989, the interest expense that results from a refinancing of a nursing facility's demand call loan, when the loan that must be refinanced was incurred before May 22, 1983, is an allowable interest expense if:</p><p>(1) the demand call loan or any part of it was in the form of a loan that was callable at the demand of the lender;</p><p>(2) the demand call loan or any part of it was called by the lender through no fault of the nursing facility;</p><p>(3) the demand call loan or any part of it was made by a government agency operating under a statutory or regulatory loan program;</p><p>(4) the refinanced debt does not exceed the sum of the allowable remaining balance of the demand call loan at the time of payment on the demand call loan and refinancing costs;</p><p>(5) the term of the refinanced debt does not exceed the remaining term of the demand call loan, had the debt not been subject to an on-call payment demand; and</p><p>(6) the refinanced debt is not a debt between related organizations as defined in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0020">9549.0020</a>, subpart 38.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3c.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3d.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3e"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3e.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/99/#laws.1.43.0">2016 c 99 art 1 s 43</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3f"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3f.<span class="headnote">Property costs after July 1, 1988.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) For the rate year beginning July 1, 1988, the replacement-cost-new per bed limit must be $32,571 per licensed bed in multiple bedrooms and $48,857 per licensed bed in a single bedroom. For the rate year beginning July 1, 1989, the replacement-cost-new per bed limit for a single bedroom must be $49,907 adjusted according to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 4, item A, subitem (1). Beginning January 1, 1990, the replacement-cost-new per bed limits must be adjusted annually as specified in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 4, item A, subitem (1). Beginning January 1, 1991, the replacement-cost-new per bed limits will be adjusted annually as specified in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 4, item A, subitem (1), except that the index utilized will be the Bureau of Economic Analysis: Price Indexes for Private Fixed Investments in Structures; Special Care.</p><p class="in">(b) For the rate year beginning July 1, 1988, the commissioner shall increase the rental factor as established in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 8, item A, by 6.2 percent rounded to the nearest 100th percent for the purpose of reimbursing nursing facilities for soft costs and entrepreneurial profits not included in the cost valuation services used by the state's contracted appraisers. For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1989, the rental factor is the amount determined under this paragraph for the rate year beginning July 1, 1988.</p><p class="in">(c) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1988, in order to determine property-related payment rates under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, for all nursing facilities except those whose average length of stay in a skilled level of care within a nursing facility is 180 days or less, the commissioner shall use 95 percent of capacity days. For a nursing facility whose average length of stay in a skilled level of care within a nursing facility is 180 days or less, the commissioner shall use the greater of resident days or 80 percent of capacity days but in no event shall the divisor exceed 95 percent of capacity days.</p><p class="in">(d) For rate years beginning on July 1, 1988, and July 1, 1989, the commissioner shall add ten cents per resident per day to each nursing facility's property-related payment rate. The ten-cent property-related payment rate increase is not cumulative from rate year to rate year. For the rate year beginning July 1, 1990, the commissioner shall increase each nursing facility's equipment allowance as established in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 10, by ten cents per resident per day. For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1991, the adjusted equipment allowance must be adjusted annually for inflation as in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 10, item E. For the rate period beginning October 1, 1992, the equipment allowance for each nursing facility shall be increased by 28 percent. For rate years beginning after June 30, 1993, the allowance must be adjusted annually for inflation.</p><p class="in">(e) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1990, Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 5, item E, shall not apply to outstanding related organization debt incurred prior to May 23, 1983, provided that the debt was an allowable debt under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9510.0010">9510.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9510.0480">9510.0480</a>, the debt is subject to repayment through annual principal payments, and the nursing facility demonstrates to the commissioner's satisfaction that the interest rate on the debt was less than market interest rates for similar arm's-length transactions at the time the debt was incurred. If the debt was incurred due to a sale between family members, the nursing facility must also demonstrate that the seller no longer participates in the management or operation of the nursing facility. Debts meeting the conditions of this paragraph are subject to all other provisions of Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>.</p><p class="in">(f) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1990, a nursing facility with operating lease costs incurred for the nursing facility's buildings shall receive its building capital allowance computed in accordance with Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 8. If an operating lease provides that the lessee's rent is adjusted to recognize improvements made by the lessor and related debt, the costs for capital improvements and related debt shall be allowed in the computation of the lessee's building capital allowance, provided that reimbursement for these costs under an operating lease shall not exceed the rate otherwise paid.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3g"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3g.<span class="headnote">Property costs after July 1, 1990, for certain facilities.</span></h2><p>(a) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1990, nursing facilities that, on or after January 1, 1976, but prior to January 1, 1987, were newly licensed after new construction, or increased their licensed beds by a minimum of 35 percent through new construction, and whose building capital allowance is less than their allowable annual principal and interest on allowable debt prior to the application of the replacement-cost-new per bed limit and whose remaining weighted average debt amortization schedule as of January 1, 1988, exceeded 15 years, must receive a property-related payment rate equal to the greater of their rental per diem or their annual allowable principal and allowable interest without application of the replacement-cost-new per bed limit, divided by their capacity days as determined under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11, as modified by subdivision 3f, paragraph (c), for the preceding reporting year, plus their equipment allowance. A nursing facility that is eligible for a property-related payment rate under this subdivision and whose property-related payment rate in a subsequent rate year is its rental per diem must continue to have its property-related payment rates established for all future rate years based on the rental reimbursement method in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>.</p><p class="bl">The commissioner may require the nursing facility to apply for refinancing as a condition of receiving special rate treatment under this subdivision.</p><p>(b) If a nursing facility is eligible for a property-related payment rate under this subdivision, and the nursing facility's debt is refinanced after October 1, 1988, the provisions in paragraphs (1) to (7) also apply to the property-related payment rate for rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1990.</p><p>(1) A nursing facility's refinancing must not include debts with balloon payments.</p><p>(2) If the issuance costs, including issuance costs on the debt refinanced, are financed as part of the refinancing, the historical cost of capital assets limit in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 5, item A, subitem (6), includes issuance costs that do not exceed seven percent of the debt refinanced, plus the related issuance costs. For purposes of this paragraph, issuance costs means the fees charged by the underwriter, issuer, attorneys, bond raters, appraisers, and trustees, and includes the cost of printing, title insurance, registration tax, and a feasibility study for the refinancing of a nursing facility's debt. Issuance costs do not include bond premiums or discounts when bonds are sold at other than their par value, points, or a bond reserve fund. To the extent otherwise allowed under this paragraph, the straight-line amortization of the refinancing issuance costs is not an allowable cost.</p><p>(3) The annual principal and interest expense payments and any required annual municipal fees on the nursing facility's refinancing replace those of the refinanced debt and, together with annual principal and interest payments on other allowable debts, are allowable costs subject to the limitation on historical cost of capital assets plus issuance costs as limited in paragraph (2), if any.</p><p>(4) If the nursing facility's refinancing includes zero coupon bonds, the commissioner shall establish a monthly debt service payment schedule based on an annuity that will produce an amount equal to the zero coupon bonds at maturity. The term and interest rate is the term and interest rate of the zero coupon bonds. Any refinancing to repay the zero coupon bonds is not an allowable cost.</p><p>(5) The annual amount of annuity payments is added to the nursing facility's allowable annual principal and interest payment computed in paragraph (3).</p><p>(6) The property-related payment rate is equal to the amount in paragraph (5), divided by the nursing facility's capacity days as determined under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11, as modified by subdivision 3f, paragraph (c), for the preceding reporting year plus an equipment allowance.</p><p>(7) Except as provided in this subdivision, the provisions of Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a> apply.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3h"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3h.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.3i"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3i.</h2><p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.4.30.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 4 s 30</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.9a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9a.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.10"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Property rate adjustments and construction projects.</span></h2><p>A nursing facility completing a construction project that is eligible for a rate adjustment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434#stat.256B.434.4f">256B.434, subdivision 4f</a>, and that was not approved through the moratorium exception process in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a> must request from the commissioner a property-related payment rate adjustment. The effective date of the rate adjustment is the first of the month of January or July, whichever occurs first following both the construction project's completion date and submission of the provider's rate adjustment request. The commissioner shall provide a rate notice reflecting the allowable costs within 60 days after receiving all the necessary information to compute the rate adjustment. No sooner than the effective date of the rate adjustment for the construction project, a nursing facility may adjust its rates by the amount anticipated to be allowed. Any amounts collected from private pay residents in excess of the allowable rate must be repaid to private pay residents with interest at the rate used by the commissioner of revenue for the late payment of taxes and in effect on the date the rate increase is effective. Construction projects with completion dates within one year of the completion date associated with the property rate adjustment request and phased projects with project completion dates within three years of the last phase of the phased project must be aggregated for purposes of the minimum thresholds in subdivisions 16 and 17, and the maximum threshold in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.2">144A.071, subdivision 2</a>. "Construction project" and "project construction costs" have the meanings given them in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.1a">144A.071, subdivision 1a</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.11"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.12"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.13"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Hold-harmless property-related rates.</span></h2><p>(a) Terms used in subdivisions 13 to 21 shall be as defined in Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>, and this section.</p><p>(b) Except as provided in this subdivision, for rate periods beginning on October 1, 1992, and for rate years beginning after June 30, 1993, the property-related rate for a nursing facility shall be the greater of $4 or the property-related payment rate in effect on September 30, 1992. In addition, the incremental increase in the nursing facility's rental rate will be determined under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>, and this section.</p><p>(c) Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 13, item F, a nursing facility that has a sale permitted under subdivision 14 after June 30, 1992, shall receive the property-related payment rate in effect at the time of the sale or reorganization. For rate periods beginning after October 1, 1992, and for rate years beginning after June 30, 1993, a nursing facility shall receive, in addition to its property-related payment rate in effect at the time of the sale, the incremental increase allowed under subdivision 14.</p><p>(d) For rate years beginning after June 30, 1993, the property-related rate for a nursing facility licensed after July 1, 1989, after relocating its beds from a separate nursing home to a building formerly used as a hospital and sold during the cost reporting year ending September 30, 1991, shall be its property-related rate prior to the sale in addition to the incremental increases provided under this section effective on October 1, 1992, of 29 cents per day, and any incremental increases after October 1, 1992, calculated by using its rental rate under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>, and this section, recognizing the current appraised value of the facility at the new location, and including as allowable debt otherwise allowable debt incurred to remodel the facility in the new location prior to the relocation of beds.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.14"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.15"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.</h2><p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.4.30.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 4 s 30</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.16"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.</h2><p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.4.30.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 4 s 30</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.17"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Special provisions for moratorium exceptions.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 3, for rate periods beginning on October 1, 1992, and for rate years beginning after June 30, 1993, a nursing facility that (1) has completed a construction project approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.4a">144A.071, subdivision 4a</a>, clause (m); (2) has completed a construction project approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.4a">144A.071, subdivision 4a</a>, and effective after June 30, 1995; (3) has completed a construction project approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.4c">144A.071, subdivision 4c</a>; or (4) has completed a renovation, replacement, or upgrading project approved under the moratorium exception process in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a> shall be reimbursed for costs directly identified to that project as provided in subdivision 16 and subdivisions 17 to 17f.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.17a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17a.<span class="headnote">Allowable interest expense.</span></h2><p class="in">(a) Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subparts 5, item A, subitems (1) and (3), and 7, item D, allowable interest expense on debt shall include:</p><p class="in">(1) interest expense on debt related to the cost of purchasing or replacing depreciable equipment, excluding vehicles, not to exceed ten percent of the total historical cost of the project; and</p><p class="in">(2) interest expense on debt related to financing or refinancing costs, including costs related to points, loan origination fees, financing charges, legal fees, and title searches; and issuance costs including bond discounts, bond counsel, underwriter's counsel, corporate counsel, printing, and financial forecasts. Allowable debt related to items in this clause shall not exceed seven percent of the total historical cost of the project. To the extent these costs are financed, the straight-line amortization of the costs in this clause is not an allowable cost; and</p><p class="in">(3) interest on debt incurred for the establishment of a debt reserve fund, net of the interest earned on the debt reserve fund.</p><p class="in">(b) Debt incurred for costs under paragraph (a) is not subject to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 5, item A, subitem (5) or (6).</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.17b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17b.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.17c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17c.<span class="headnote">Replacement-costs-new per bed limit.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding subdivision 3f, paragraph (a), for rate periods beginning on October 1, 1992, and for rate years beginning after June 30, 1993, the replacement-costs-new per bed limit to be used in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 4, item B, for a nursing facility that has completed a renovation, replacement, or upgrading project that has been approved under the moratorium exception process in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, or that has completed an addition to or replacement of buildings, attached fixtures, or land improvements for which the total historical cost exceeds the lesser of $150,000 or ten percent of the most recent appraised value, must be $47,500 per licensed bed in multiple-bed rooms and $71,250 per licensed bed in a single-bed room. These amounts must be adjusted annually as specified in subdivision 3f, paragraph (a), beginning January 1, 1993.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.17d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17d.<span class="headnote">Determination of rental per diem for total replacement projects.</span></h2><p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, a total replacement means the complete replacement of the nursing facility's physical plant through the construction of a new physical plant, the transfer of the nursing facility's license from one physical plant location to another, or a new building addition to relocate beds from three- and four-bed wards. For total replacement projects completed on or after July 1, 1992, the commissioner shall compute the incremental change in the nursing facility's rental per diem, for rate years beginning on or after July 1, 1995, by replacing its appraised value, including the historical capital asset costs, and the capital debt and interest costs with the new nursing facility's allowable capital asset costs and the related allowable capital debt and interest costs. If the new nursing facility has decreased its licensed capacity, the aggregate investment per bed limit in subdivision 3a, paragraph (c), shall apply.</p><p>(b) If the new nursing facility has retained a portion of the original physical plant for nursing facility usage, then a portion of the appraised value prior to the replacement must be retained and included in the calculation of the incremental change in the nursing facility's rental per diem. For purposes of this subdivision, the original nursing facility means the nursing facility prior to the total replacement project. The portion of the appraised value to be retained shall be calculated according to clauses (1) to (3):</p><p>(1) The numerator of the allocation ratio shall be the square footage of the area in the original physical plant which is being retained for nursing facility usage.</p><p>(2) The denominator of the allocation ratio shall be the total square footage of the original nursing facility physical plant.</p><p>(3) Each component of the nursing facility's allowable appraised value prior to the total replacement project shall be multiplied by the allocation ratio developed by dividing clause (1) by clause (2).</p><p>(c) In the case of either type of total replacement as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, the provisions of subdivisions 17 to 17f shall also apply.</p><p>(d) For purposes of the moratorium exception authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.4a">144A.071, subdivision 4a</a>, paragraph (s), if the total replacement involves the renovation and use of an existing health care facility physical plant, the new allowable capital asset costs and related debt and interest costs shall include first the allowable capital asset costs and related debt and interest costs of the renovation, to which shall be added the allowable capital asset costs of the existing physical plant prior to the renovation, and if reported by the facility, the related allowable capital debt and interest costs.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.17e"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17e.<span class="headnote">Replacement-costs-new per bed limit effective October 1, 2007.</span></h2><p class="in">Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11, item C, subitem (2), for a total replacement, as defined in subdivision 17d, authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a> after July 1, 1999, any building project that is a relocation, renovation, upgrading, or conversion completed on or after July 1, 2001, or any building project eligible for reimbursement under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434#stat.256B.434.4f">256B.434, subdivision 4f</a>, the replacement-costs-new per bed limit shall be $74,280 per licensed bed in multiple-bed rooms, $92,850 per licensed bed in semiprivate rooms with a fixed partition separating the resident beds, and $111,420 per licensed bed in single rooms. Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11, item C, subitem (2), does not apply. These amounts must be adjusted annually as specified in subdivision 3f, paragraph (a), beginning January 1, 2000. These amounts must be increased annually as specified in subdivision 3f, paragraph (a), beginning October 1, 2012.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.17f"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17f.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.18"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Updating appraisals, additions, and replacements.</span></h2><p>(a) Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subparts 1 to 3, the appraised value, routine updating of the appraised value, and special reappraisals are subject to this subdivision.</p><p>For all rate years after June 30, 1993, the commissioner shall no longer conduct any appraisals under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, for the purpose of determining property-related payment rates.</p><p>(b) Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 2, for rate years beginning after June 30, 1993, the commissioner shall routinely update the appraised value of each nursing facility by adding the cost of capital asset acquisitions to its allowable appraised value.</p><p>The commissioner shall also annually index each nursing facility's allowable appraised value by the inflation index referenced in subdivision 3f, paragraph (a), for the purpose of computing the nursing facility's annual rental rate. In annually adjusting the nursing facility's appraised value, the commissioner must not include the historical cost of capital assets acquired during the reporting year in the nursing facility's appraised value.</p><p>In addition, the nursing facility's appraised value must be reduced by the historical cost of capital asset disposals or applicable credits such as public grants and insurance proceeds. Capital asset additions and disposals must be reported on the nursing facility's annual cost report in the reporting year of acquisition or disposal. The incremental increase in the nursing facility's rental rate resulting from this annual adjustment as determined under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>, and this section shall be added to the nursing facility's property-related payment rate for the rate year following the reporting year.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.19"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.20"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.21"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 21.<span class="headnote">Indexing thresholds.</span></h2><p>Beginning January 1, 1993, and each January 1 thereafter, the commissioner shall annually update the dollar thresholds in subdivisions 15, paragraph (e), 16, and 17, and in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071, subdivisions 2</a> and 4a, clauses (b) and (e), by the inflation index referenced in subdivision 3f, paragraph (a).</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.22"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22.<span class="headnote">Changes to nursing facility reimbursement.</span></h2><p> In the determination of incremental increases in the nursing facility's rental rate as required in subdivisions 14 to 21, except for a refinancing permitted under subdivision 19, the commissioner must adjust the nursing facility's property-related payment rate for both incremental increases and decreases in recomputations of its rental rate.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.23"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 23.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.86.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 86</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.24"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 24.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/449/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 449 s 15</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.25"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 25.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.26"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.27"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 27.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.28"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 28.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/262/#laws.4.9.0">2014 c 262 art 4 s 9</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.29"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 29.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.30"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 30.<span class="headnote">Bed layaway and delicensure.</span></h2><p>(a) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 2000, a nursing facility reimbursed under this section which has placed beds on layaway shall, for purposes of application of the downsizing incentive in subdivision 3a, paragraph (c), and calculation of the rental per diem, have those beds given the same effect as if the beds had been delicensed so long as the beds remain on layaway. At the time of a layaway, a facility may change its single bed election for use in calculating capacity days under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11. The property payment rate increase shall be effective the first day of the month of January or July, whichever occurs first following the date on which the layaway of the beds becomes effective under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.4b">144A.071, subdivision 4b</a>.</p><p>(b) For rate years beginning on or after July 1, 2000, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434">256B.434</a> or chapter 256R, a nursing facility reimbursed under that section or chapter that has placed beds on layaway shall, for so long as the beds remain on layaway, be allowed to:</p><p>(1) aggregate the applicable investment per bed limits based on the number of beds licensed immediately prior to entering the alternative payment system;</p><p>(2) retain or change the facility's single bed election for use in calculating capacity days under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11; and</p><p>(3) establish capacity days based on the number of beds immediately prior to the layaway and the number of beds after the layaway.</p><p class="in">The commissioner shall increase the facility's property payment rate by the incremental increase in the rental per diem resulting from the recalculation of the facility's rental per diem applying only the changes resulting from the layaway of beds and clauses (1), (2), and (3). If a facility reimbursed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434">256B.434</a> or chapter 256R completes a moratorium exception project after its base year, the base year property rate shall be the moratorium project property rate. The base year rate shall be inflated by the factors in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434#stat.256B.434.4">256B.434, subdivision 4</a>, paragraph (c). The property payment rate increase shall be effective the first day of the month of January or July, whichever occurs first following the date on which the layaway of the beds becomes effective.</p><p>(c) If a nursing facility removes a bed from layaway status in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.4b">144A.071, subdivision 4b</a>, the commissioner shall establish capacity days based on the number of licensed and certified beds in the facility not on layaway and shall reduce the nursing facility's property payment rate in accordance with paragraph (b).</p><p>(d) For the rate years beginning on or after July 1, 2000, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434">256B.434</a> or chapter 256R, a nursing facility reimbursed under that section or chapter that has delicensed beds after July 1, 2000, by giving notice of the delicensure to the commissioner of health according to the notice requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071#stat.144A.071.4b">144A.071, subdivision 4b</a>, shall be allowed to:</p><p>(1) aggregate the applicable investment per bed limits based on the number of beds licensed immediately prior to entering the alternative payment system;</p><p>(2) retain or change the facility's single bed election for use in calculating capacity days under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11; and</p><p>(3) establish capacity days based on the number of beds immediately prior to the delicensure and the number of beds after the delicensure.</p><p class="in">The commissioner shall increase the facility's property payment rate by the incremental increase in the rental per diem resulting from the recalculation of the facility's rental per diem applying only the changes resulting from the delicensure of beds and clauses (1), (2), and (3). If a facility reimbursed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434">256B.434</a> completes a moratorium exception project after its base year, the base year property rate shall be the moratorium project property rate. The base year rate shall be inflated by the factors in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434#stat.256B.434.4">256B.434, subdivision 4</a>, paragraph (c). The property payment rate increase shall be effective the first day of the month of January or July, whichever occurs first following the date on which the delicensure of the beds becomes effective.</p><p>(e) For nursing facilities reimbursed under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434">256B.434</a>, or chapter 256R, any beds placed on layaway shall not be included in calculating facility occupancy as it pertains to leave days defined in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0415">9505.0415</a>.</p><p>(f) For nursing facilities reimbursed under this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.434">256B.434</a>, or chapter 256R, the rental rate calculated after placing beds on layaway may not be less than the rental rate prior to placing beds on layaway.</p><p>(g) A nursing facility receiving a rate adjustment as a result of this section shall comply with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256R.06#stat.256R.06.5">256R.06, subdivision 5</a>.</p><p>(h) A facility that does not utilize the space made available as a result of bed layaway or delicensure under this subdivision to reduce the number of beds per room or provide more common space for nursing facility uses or perform other activities related to the operation of the nursing facility shall have its property rate increase calculated under this subdivision reduced by the ratio of the square footage made available that is not used for these purposes to the total square footage made available as a result of bed layaway or delicensure.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.31"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 31.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/262/#laws.4.9.0">2014 c 262 art 4 s 9</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.32"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 32.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/99/#laws.1.43.0">2016 c 99 art 1 s 43</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.431.45"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 45.<span class="headnote">Rate adjustments for some moratorium exception projects.</span></h2><p>Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, money available for moratorium exception projects under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073, subdivisions 2</a> and 11, shall be used to fund the incremental rate increases resulting from this section for any nursing facility with a moratorium exception project approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, and completed after August 30, 2010, where the replacement-costs-new limits under subdivision 17e were higher at any time after project approval than at the time of project completion. The commissioner shall calculate the property rate increase for these facilities using the highest set of limits; however, any rate increase under this section shall not be effective until on or after the effective date of this section, contingent upon federal approval. No property rate decrease shall result from this section.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.431.history

CONTRACTS AND AGREEMENTS.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2><p>[Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256R.03">256R.03, subd 5</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/99/#laws.1.43.0">2016 c 99 art 1 s 43</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2><p>[Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256R.03">256R.03, subd 6</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Alternate rates for nursing facilities.</span></h2><p class="in">Effective for the rate years beginning on and after January 1, 2019, a nursing facility's property payment rate for the second and subsequent years of a facility's contract under this section are the previous rate year's property payment rate plus an inflation adjustment. The index for the inflation adjustment must be based on the change in the Consumer Price Index-All Items (United States City average) (CPI-U) forecasted by the Reports and Forecasts Division of the Department of Human Services, as forecasted in the fourth quarter of the calendar year preceding the rate year. The inflation adjustment must be based on the 12-month period from the midpoint of the previous rate year to the midpoint of the rate year for which the rate is being determined.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4b.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4c.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4d.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4e"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4e.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4f"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4f.<span class="headnote">Construction project rate adjustments effective October 1, 2006.</span></h2><p>(a) Effective October 1, 2006, facilities reimbursed under this section may receive a property rate adjustment for construction projects exceeding the threshold in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 16, and below the threshold in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, paragraph (c), clause (1). For these projects, capital assets purchased shall be counted as construction project costs for a rate adjustment request made by a facility if they are: (1) purchased within 24 months of the completion of the construction project; (2) purchased after the completion date of any prior construction project; and (3) are not purchased prior to July 14, 2005. Except as otherwise provided in this subdivision, the definitions, rate calculation methods, and principles in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a> and Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>, shall be used to calculate rate adjustments for allowable construction projects under this subdivision and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>. Facilities completing construction projects between October 1, 2005, and October 1, 2006, are eligible to have a property rate adjustment effective October 1, 2006. Facilities completing projects after October 1, 2006, are eligible for a property rate adjustment effective on the first day of the month following the completion date. Facilities completing projects after January 1, 2018, are eligible for a property rate adjustment effective on the first day of the month of January or July, whichever occurs immediately following the completion date.</p><p>(b) Notwithstanding subdivision 18, as of July 14, 2005, facilities with rates set under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a> and Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>, that commenced a construction project on or after October 1, 2004, and do not have a contract under subdivision 3 by September 30, 2006, are eligible to request a rate adjustment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 10, through September 30, 2006. If the request results in the commissioner determining a rate adjustment is allowable, the rate adjustment is effective on the first of the month following project completion. These facilities shall be allowed to accumulate construction project costs for the period October 1, 2004, to September 30, 2006.</p><p>(c) Facilities shall be allowed construction project rate adjustments no sooner than 12 months after completing a previous construction project. Facilities must request the rate adjustment according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 10.</p><p>(d) Capacity days shall be computed according to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 11. For rate calculations under this section, the number of licensed beds in the nursing facility shall be the number existing after the construction project is completed and the number of days in the nursing facility's reporting period shall be 365.</p><p>(e) The value of assets to be recognized for a total replacement project as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 17d, shall be computed as described in clause (1). The value of assets to be recognized for all other projects shall be computed as described in clause (2).</p><p>(1) Replacement-cost-new limits under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 17e, and the number of beds allowed under subdivision 3a, paragraph (c), shall be used to compute the maximum amount of assets allowable in a facility's property rate calculation. If a facility's current request for a rate adjustment results from the completion of a construction project that was previously approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, the assets to be used in the rate calculation cannot exceed the lesser of the amount determined under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, subdivision 3b, or the actual allowable costs of the construction project. A current request that is not the result of a project under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a> cannot exceed the limit under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, paragraph (c), clause (1). Applicable credits must be deducted from the cost of the construction project.</p><p>(2)(i) Replacement-cost-new limits under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 17e, and the number of beds allowed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 3a, paragraph (c), shall be used to compute the maximum amount of assets allowable in a facility's property rate calculation.</p><p>(ii) The value of a facility's assets to be compared to the amount in item (i) begins with the total appraised value from the last rate notice a facility received when its rates were set under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a> and Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>. This value shall be indexed by the factor in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 3f, paragraph (a), for each rate year the facility received an inflation factor on its property-related rate when its rates were set under this section. The value of assets listed as previous capital additions, capital additions, and special projects on the facility's base year rate notice and the value of assets related to a construction project for which the facility received a rate adjustment when its rates were determined under this section shall be added to the indexed appraised value.</p><p>(iii) The maximum amount of assets to be recognized in computing a facility's rate adjustment after a project is completed is the lesser of the aggregate replacement-cost-new limit computed in (i) minus the assets recognized in (ii) or the actual allowable costs of the construction project.</p><p>(iv) If a facility's current request for a rate adjustment results from the completion of a construction project that was previously approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, the assets to be added to the rate calculation cannot exceed the lesser of the amount determined under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, subdivision 3b, or the actual allowable costs of the construction project. A current request that is not the result of a project under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a> cannot exceed the limit stated in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, paragraph (c), clause (1). Assets disposed of as a result of a construction project and applicable credits must be deducted from the cost of the construction project.</p><p>(f) For construction projects approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, allowable debt may never exceed the lesser of the cost of the assets purchased, the threshold limit in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, or the replacement-cost-new limit less previously existing capital debt.</p><p>(g) For construction projects that were not approved under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>, allowable debt is limited to the lesser of the threshold in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, for such construction projects or the applicable limit in paragraph (e), clause (1) or (2), less previously existing capital debt. Amounts of debt taken out that exceed the costs of a construction project shall not be allowed regardless of the use of the funds.</p><p>For all construction projects being recognized, interest expense and average debt shall be computed based on the first 12 months following project completion. "Previously existing capital debt" means capital debt recognized on the last rate determined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a> and Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0010">9549.0010</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0080">9549.0080</a>, and the amount of debt recognized for a construction project for which the facility received a rate adjustment when its rates were determined under this section.</p><p>For a total replacement project as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 17d, the value of previously existing capital debt shall be zero.</p><p>(h) In addition to the interest expense allowed from the application of paragraph (f), the amounts allowed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 17a, paragraph (a), clauses (2) and (3), will be added to interest expense.</p><p>(i) The equity portion of the construction project shall be computed as the allowable assets in paragraph (e), less the average debt in paragraph (f). The equity portion must be multiplied by 5.66 percent and the allowable interest expense in paragraph (f) must be added. This sum must be divided by 95 percent of capacity days to compute the construction project rate adjustment.</p><p>(j) For projects that are not a total replacement of a nursing facility, the amount in paragraph (i) is adjusted for nonreimbursable areas and then added to the current property payment rate of the facility.</p><p>(k) For projects that are a total replacement of a nursing facility, the amount in paragraph (i) becomes the new property payment rate after being adjusted for nonreimbursable areas. Any amounts existing in a facility's rate before the effective date of the construction project for equity incentives under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 16; capital repairs and replacements under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 15; or refinancing incentives under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 19, shall be removed from the facility's rates.</p><p>(l) No additional equipment allowance is allowed under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9549.0060">9549.0060</a>, subpart 10, as the result of construction projects under this section. Allowable equipment shall be included in the construction project costs.</p><p>(m) Capital assets purchased after the completion date of a construction project shall be counted as construction project costs for any future rate adjustment request made by a facility under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.071">144A.071</a>, subdivision 2, paragraph (c), clause (1), if they are purchased within 24 months of the completion of the future construction project.</p><p>(n) In subsequent rate years, the property payment rate for a facility that results from the application of this subdivision shall be the amount inflated in subdivision 4.</p><p>(o) Construction projects are eligible for an equity incentive under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 16. When computing the equity incentive for a construction project under this subdivision, only the allowable costs and allowable debt related to the construction project shall be used. The equity incentive shall not be a part of the property payment rate and not inflated under subdivision 4. Effective October 1, 2006, all equity incentives for nursing facilities reimbursed under this section shall be allowed for a duration determined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.431">256B.431</a>, subdivision 16, paragraph (c).</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4g"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4g.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4h"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4h.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.9.38.0">2012 c 216 art 9 s 38</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4i"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4i.<span class="headnote">Construction project rate adjustments for certain nursing facilities.</span></h2><p>(a) This subdivision applies to nursing facilities with at least 120 active beds as of January 1, 2015, that have projects approved in 2015 under the nursing facility moratorium exception process in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073">144A.073</a>. When each facility's moratorium exception construction project is completed, the facility must receive the rate adjustment allowed under subdivision 4f. In addition to that rate adjustment, facilities with at least 120 active beds, but not more than 149 active beds, as of January 1, 2015, must have their construction project rate adjustment increased by an additional $4; and facilities with at least 150 active beds, but not more than 160 active beds, as of January 1, 2015, must have their construction project rate adjustment increased by an additional $12.50.</p><p>(b) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, money available under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073#stat.144A.073.11">144A.073, subdivision 11</a>, after the completion of the moratorium exception approval process in 2015 under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073#stat.144A.073.3">144A.073, subdivision 3</a>, shall be used to reduce the fiscal impact to the medical assistance budget for the increases allowed in this subdivision.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4j"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4j.<span class="headnote">Construction project rate increase for certain nursing facilities.</span></h2><p>(a) This subdivision applies to nursing facilities:</p><p>(1) located in Ramsey County;</p><p>(2) with at least 130 active beds as of September 30, 2017;</p><p>(3) with a portion of beds dually certified for Medicare and Medicaid and a portion of beds certified for Medicaid only; and</p><p>(4) with debt service payments that are not being covered by the existing property payment rate on September 30, 2017.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall increase the property rate of each facility meeting the qualifications of this subdivision by $7.55.</p><p>(c) Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, money available under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073#stat.144A.073.15">144A.073, subdivision 15</a>, after the completion of the 2018 moratorium exception approval process under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.073#stat.144A.073.3">144A.073, subdivision 3</a>, shall be used to pay the medical assistance cost for the property rate increase in this subdivision.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.4k"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4k.<span class="headnote">Property rate increase for certain nursing facilities.</span></h2><p>(a) A rate increase under this subdivision ends upon the effective date of the transition of the facility's property rate to a property payment rate under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256R.26#stat.256R.26.8">256R.26, subdivision 8</a>, or May 31, 2026, whichever is earlier.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall increase the property rate of a nursing facility located in the city of St. Paul at 1415 Almond Avenue in Ramsey County by $10.65 on January 1, 2025.</p><p>(c) The commissioner shall increase the property rate of a nursing facility located in the city of Duluth at 3111 Church Place in St. Louis County by $20.81 on January 1, 2025.</p><p>(d) The commissioner shall increase the property rate of a nursing facility located in the city of Chatfield at 1102 Liberty Street SE in Fillmore County by $21.35 on January 1, 2025.</p><p>(e) Effective January 1, 2025, through June 30, 2025, the commissioner shall increase the property rate of a nursing facility located in the city of Fergus Falls at 1131 South Mabelle Avenue in Ottertail County by $38.56.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.5.41.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 5 s 41</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.434.6"><h2 class="section" id="stat.256B.439"><h1 class="shn">256B.439 LONG-TERM CARE QUALITY PROFILES.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Development and implementation of quality profiles.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner of human services, in cooperation with the commissioner of health, shall develop and implement quality profiles for nursing facilities and, beginning not later than July 1, 2014, for home and community-based services providers, except when the quality profile system would duplicate requirements under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.5011">256B.5011</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.5012">256B.5012</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.5013">256B.5013</a>. For purposes of this section, home and community-based services providers are defined as providers of home and community-based services under chapter 256S and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625">256B.0625, subdivisions 6a, 7, and 19a; 256B.0913</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>; and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.85">256B.85</a>, and intermediate care facilities for persons with developmental disabilities providers under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.5013">256B.5013</a>. To the extent possible, quality profiles must be developed for providers of services to older adults and people with disabilities, regardless of payor source, for the purposes of providing information to consumers. The quality profiles must be developed using existing data sets maintained by the commissioners of health and human services to the extent possible. The profiles must incorporate or be coordinated with information on quality maintained by area agencies on aging, long-term care trade associations, the ombudsman offices, counties, tribes, health plans, and other entities and the long-term care database maintained under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.975#stat.256.975.7">256.975, subdivision 7</a>. The profiles must be designed to provide information on quality to:</p><p>(1) consumers and their families to facilitate informed choices of service providers;</p><p>(2) providers to enable them to measure the results of their quality improvement efforts and compare quality achievements with other service providers; and</p><p>(3) public and private purchasers of long-term care services to enable them to purchase high-quality care.</p><p>(b) The profiles must be developed in consultation with the long-term care task force, area agencies on aging, and representatives of consumers, providers, and labor unions. Within the limits of available appropriations, the commissioners may employ consultants to assist with this project.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Quality measurement tools for nursing facilities.</span></h2><p>The commissioners shall identify and apply existing quality measurement tools to:</p><p>(1) emphasize quality of care and its relationship to quality of life; and</p><p>(2) address the needs of various users of long-term care services, including, but not limited to, short-stay residents, persons with behavioral problems, persons with dementia, and persons who are members of minority groups.</p><p class="in">The tools must be identified and applied, to the extent possible, without requiring providers to supply information beyond state and federal requirements.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.2a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Quality measurement tools for home and community-based services. </span></h2><p>(a) The commissioners shall identify and apply quality measurement tools to:</p><p>(1) emphasize service quality and its relationship to quality of life; and</p><p>(2) address the needs of various users of home and community-based services.</p><p>(b) The tools must include, but not be limited to, surveys of consumers of home and community-based services. The tools must be identified and applied, to the extent possible, without requiring providers to supply information beyond state and federal requirements, for purposes of this subdivision.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Consumer surveys of nursing facilities residents.</span></h2><p>Following identification of the quality measurement tool, the commissioners shall conduct surveys of long-term care service consumers of nursing facilities to develop quality profiles of providers. To the extent possible, surveys must be conducted face-to-face by state employees or contractors. At the discretion of the commissioners, surveys may be conducted by telephone or by provider staff. Surveys must be conducted periodically to update quality profiles of individual nursing facilities providers.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.3a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Consumer surveys for home and community-based services. </span></h2><p>Following identification of the quality measurement tool, and within the limits of the appropriation, the commissioner shall conduct surveys of home and community-based services consumers to develop quality profiles of providers. To the extent possible, surveys must be conducted face-to-face by state employees or contractors. At the discretion of the commissioner, surveys may be conducted by an alternative method. Surveys must be conducted periodically to update quality profiles of individual service providers.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.3b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.</h2><p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/25/#laws.0.190.0">2023 c 25 s 190</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.3c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3c.<span class="headnote">Contact and demographic information for consumer surveys for home and community-based services.</span></h2><p>For purposes of conducting the consumer surveys under subdivision 3a, the commissioner may request contact information of clients and associated key representatives and aggregate, de-identified demographic information of clients served by the provider. The commissioner may request the following demographic information: (1) age; (2) race; (3) ethnicity; and (4) gender identity. Providers must furnish the contact and demographic information available to the provider and must provide notice to clients and associated key representatives that their contact information and aggregate demographic information has been provided to the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.3d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3d.<span class="headnote">Resident experience survey and family survey for assisted living facilities.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall develop and administer a resident experience survey for assisted living facility residents and a family survey for families of assisted living facility residents. Money appropriated to the commissioner to administer the resident experience survey and family survey is available in either fiscal year of the biennium in which it is appropriated. Assisted living facilities licensed under chapter 144G must participate in the surveys when the commissioner requests their participation.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.3e"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3e.<span class="headnote">Demographic information for home and community-based services report card.</span></h2><p>(a) For purposes of including relevant information in the home and community-based services report card for consumers on the populations served by providers and for other data analysis, the commissioner may request from providers the following summary data about clients served by the provider:</p><p>(1) age;</p><p>(2) race;</p><p>(3) ethnicity; and</p><p>(4) gender identity.</p><p>(b) For the purposes of this subdivision, "summary data" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.19">13.02, subdivision 19</a>. Providers must furnish the summary data only if the data on individuals is available to the provider. A provider is not required to collect any demographic data from clients for the sole purpose of providing the information requested by the commissioner under this subdivision. If a provider furnishes the requested summary data to the commissioner, the provider must provide notice to clients and associated key representatives that the client's demographic information was included in the summary data provided to the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Dissemination of quality profiles.</span></h2><p>By July 1, 2014, the commissioners shall implement a public awareness effort to disseminate the quality profiles. Profiles may be disseminated through the Senior LinkAge Line and Disability Hub and to consumers, providers, and purchasers of long-term care services.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Implementation of home and community-based services performance-based incentive payment program. </span></h2><p>By April 1, 2014, the commissioner shall develop incentive-based grants for home and community-based services providers for achieving outcomes specified in a contract. The commissioner may solicit proposals from home and community-based services providers and implement those that, on a competitive basis, best meet the state's policy objectives. The commissioner shall determine the types of home and community-based services providers that will participate in the program. The determination of participating provider types may be revised annually by the commissioner. The commissioner shall limit the amount of any incentive-based grants and the number of grants under this subdivision to operate the incentive payments within funds appropriated for this purpose. The grant agreements may specify various levels of payment for various levels of performance. In establishing the specified outcomes and related criteria, the commissioner shall consider the following state policy objectives:</p><p>(1) provide more efficient, higher quality services;</p><p>(2) encourage home and community-based services providers to innovate;</p><p>(3) equip home and community-based services providers with organizational tools and expertise to improve their quality;</p><p>(4) incentivize home and community-based services providers to invest in better services; and</p><p>(5) disseminate successful performance improvement strategies statewide.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Calculation of home and community-based services quality score. </span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall determine a quality score for each participating home and community-based services provider using quality measures established in subdivisions 1 and 2a, according to methods determined by the commissioner in consultation with stakeholders and experts. These methods shall be exempt from the rulemaking requirements under chapter 14.</p><p>(b) For each quality measure, a score shall be determined with a maximum number of points available and number of points assigned as determined by the commissioner using the methodology established according to this subdivision. The determination of the quality measures to be used and the methods of calculating scores may be revised annually by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.439.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Calculation of home and community-based services quality add-on. </span></h2><p>On July 1, 2015, the commissioner shall determine the quality add-on rate change and adjust payment rates for all home and community-based services providers for services rendered on or after that date. The adjustment to a provider payment rate determined under this subdivision shall become part of the ongoing rate paid to that provider. The payment rate for the quality add-on shall be a variable amount based on each provider's quality score as determined in subdivisions 1 and 2a. All home and community-based services providers shall receive a minimum rate increase under this subdivision. In addition to a minimum rate increase, a home and community-based services provider shall receive a quality add-on payment. The commissioner shall limit the types of home and community-based services providers that may receive the quality add-on based on availability of quality measures and outcome data. The commissioner shall limit the amount of the minimum rate increase and quality add-on payments to the equivalent of a one percent rate increase for all home and community-based services providers.</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.439.history
