Laws 2023, chapter 61, article 1, section 23, the effective date.</p><div class="section" id="stat.256B.4912"><h1 class="shn">256B.4912 HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED WAIVERS; PROVIDERS AND PAYMENT.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Provider qualifications.</span></h2><p>(a) For the home and community-based waivers providing services to seniors and individuals with disabilities under chapter 256S and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913">256B.0913</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>, the commissioner shall establish:</p><p>(1) agreements with enrolled waiver service providers to ensure providers meet Minnesota health care program requirements;</p><p>(2) regular reviews of provider qualifications, and including requests of proof of documentation; and</p><p>(3) processes to gather the necessary information to determine provider qualifications.</p><p>(b) A provider shall not require or coerce any service recipient to change waiver programs or move to a different location, consistent with the informed choice and independent living policies under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.4905">256B.4905, subdivisions 1a</a>, 2a, 3a, 7, and 8.</p><p class="in">(c) Beginning July 1, 2012, staff that provide direct contact, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.02#stat.245C.02.11">245C.02, subdivision 11</a>, for services specified in the federally approved waiver plans must meet the requirements of chapter 245C prior to providing waiver services and as part of ongoing enrollment. Upon federal approval, this requirement must also apply to consumer-directed community supports.</p><p class="in">(d) Beginning January 1, 2014, service owners and managerial officials overseeing the management or policies of services that provide direct contact as specified in the federally approved waiver plans must meet the requirements of chapter 245C prior to reenrollment or revalidation or, for new providers, prior to initial enrollment if they have not already done so as a part of service licensure requirements.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.1a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Annual labor market reporting.</span></h2><p>(a) As determined by the commissioner, a provider of home and community-based services for the elderly under chapter 256S and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913">256B.0913</a>, home and community-based services for people with developmental disabilities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>, and home and community-based services for people with disabilities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a> shall submit data to the commissioner on the following:</p><p>(1) number of direct-care staff;</p><p>(2) wages of direct-care staff;</p><p>(3) hours worked by direct-care staff;</p><p>(4) overtime wages of direct-care staff;</p><p>(5) overtime hours worked by direct-care staff;</p><p>(6) benefits paid and accrued by direct-care staff;</p><p>(7) direct-care staff retention rates;</p><p>(8) direct-care staff job vacancies;</p><p>(9) amount of travel time paid;</p><p>(10) program vacancy rates; and</p><p>(11) other related data requested by the commissioner.</p><p>(b) The commissioner may adjust reporting requirements for a self-employed direct-care staff.</p><p>(c) For the purposes of this subdivision, "direct-care staff" means employees, including self-employed individuals and individuals directly employed by a participant in a consumer-directed service delivery option, providing direct service provision to people receiving services under this section. Direct-care staff does not include executive, managerial, or administrative staff.</p><p>(d) This subdivision also applies to a provider of personal care assistance services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>; community first services and supports under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.85">256B.85</a>; nursing services and home health services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625">256B.0625, subdivision </a>6a; home care nursing services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.7">256B.0625, subdivision 7</a>; or day training and habilitation services for residents of intermediate care facilities for persons with developmental disabilities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.501">256B.501</a>.</p><p>(e) This subdivision also applies to financial management services providers for participants who directly employ direct-care staff through consumer support grants under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.476">256.476</a>; the personal care assistance choice program under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, subdivisions 18 to 20; community first services and supports under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.85">256B.85</a>; and the consumer-directed community supports option available under the alternative care program, the brain injury waiver, the community alternative care waiver, the community access for disability inclusion waiver, the developmental disabilities waiver, the elderly waiver, and the Minnesota senior health option, except financial management services providers are not required to submit the data listed in paragraph (a), clauses (7) to (11).</p><p>(f) The commissioner shall ensure that data submitted under this subdivision is not duplicative of data submitted under any other section of this chapter or any other chapter.</p><p>(g) A provider shall submit the data annually on a date specified by the commissioner. The commissioner shall give a provider at least 30 calendar days to submit the data. If a provider fails to submit the requested data by the date specified by the commissioner, the commissioner may delay medical assistance reimbursement until the requested data is submitted.</p><p>(h) Individually identifiable data submitted to the commissioner in this section are considered private data on an individual, as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>.</p><p>(i) The commissioner shall analyze data annually for workforce assessments and how the data impact service access.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.1b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Direct support professional annual labor market survey.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall develop and administer a survey of direct care staff who work for organizations that provide services under the following programs:</p><p>(1) home and community-based services for seniors under chapter 256S and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913">256B.0913</a>; home and community-based services for people with developmental disabilities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>; and home and community-based services for people with disabilities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>;</p><p>(2) personal care assistance services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.19a">256B.0625, subdivision 19a</a>; community first services and supports under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.85">256B.85</a>; nursing services and home health services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.6a">256B.0625, subdivision 6a</a>; and home care nursing services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.7">256B.0625, subdivision 7</a>; and</p><p>(3) financial management services for participants who directly employ direct-care staff through consumer support grants under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.476">256.476</a>; the personal care assistance choice program under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659, subdivisions 18</a> to 20; community first services and supports under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.85">256B.85</a>; and the consumer-directed community supports option available under the alternative care program, the brain injury waiver, the community alternative care waiver, the community access for disability inclusion waiver, the developmental disabilities waiver, the elderly waiver, and the Minnesota senior health option, except financial management services providers are not required to submit the data listed in subdivision 1a, clauses (7) to (11).</p><p>(b) The survey must collect information about the individual experience of the direct-care staff and any other information necessary to assess the overall economic viability and well-being of the workforce.</p><p>(c) For purposes of this subdivision, "direct-care staff" means employees, including self-employed individuals and individuals directly employed by a participant in a consumer-directed service delivery option, providing direct service to participants under this section. Direct-care staff does not include executive, managerial, or administrative staff.</p><p>(d) Individually identifiable data submitted to the commissioner under this section are considered private data on individuals as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>.</p><p>(e) The commissioner shall analyze data submitted under this section annually to assess the overall economic viability and well-being of the workforce and the impact of the state of the workforce on access to services.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.1c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.<span class="headnote">Annual labor market report.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall publish annual reports on provider and state-level labor market data, including but not limited to the data outlined in subdivisions 1a and 1b.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Payment methodologies.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall establish, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.4914">256B.4914</a>, statewide payment methodologies that meet federal waiver requirements for home and community-based waiver services for individuals with disabilities. The payment methodologies must abide by the principles of transparency and equitability across the state. The methodologies must involve a uniform process of structuring rates for each service and must promote quality and participant choice.</p><p class="in">(b) As of January 1, 2012, counties shall not implement changes to established processes for rate-setting methodologies for individuals using components of or data from research rates.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Payment requirements.</span></h2><p>The payment methodologies established under this section shall accommodate:</p><p>(1) supervision costs;</p><p>(2) staff compensation;</p><p>(3) staffing and supervisory patterns;</p><p>(4) program-related expenses;</p><p>(5) general and administrative expenses; and</p><p>(6) consideration of recipient intensity.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Payment rate criteria.</span></h2><p>(a) The payment methodologies under this section shall reflect the payment rate criteria in paragraphs (b), (c), and (d).</p><p class="in">(b) Payment rates shall reflect the reasonable, ordinary, and necessary costs of service delivery.</p><p class="in">(c) Payment rates shall be sufficient to enlist enough providers so that care and services are available at least to the extent that such care and services are available to the general population in the geographic area as required by section 1902(a)(30)(A) of the Social Security Act.</p><p>(d) The commissioner must not reimburse:</p><p>(1) unauthorized service delivery;</p><p>(2) services provided under a receipt of a special grant;</p><p>(3) services provided under contract to a local school district;</p><p>(4) extended employment services under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/3300.6000">3300.6000</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/3300.6070">3300.6070</a>, or vocational rehabilitation services provided under the federal Rehabilitation Act, as amended, Title I, section 110, or Title VI-C, and not through use of medical assistance or county social service funds; or</p><p>(5) services provided to a client by a licensed medical, therapeutic, or rehabilitation practitioner or any other vendor of medical care which are billed separately on a fee-for-service basis.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">County and tribal provider contract elimination.</span></h2><p>County and tribal contracts with providers of home and community-based waiver services provided under chapter 256S and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913">256B.0913</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a> are eliminated effective January 1, 2014.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Program standards.</span></h2><p>The commissioner of human services must establish uniform program standards for services identified in chapter 245D for persons with disabilities and people age 65 and older. The commissioner must grant licenses according to the provisions of chapter 245A.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Applicant and license holder training.</span></h2><p>An applicant or license holder for the home and community-based waivers providing services to seniors and individuals with disabilities under chapter 256S and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913">256B.0913</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49 </a>that is not enrolled as a Minnesota health care program home and community-based services waiver provider at the time of application must ensure that at least one controlling individual completes a onetime training on the requirements for providing home and community-based services as determined by the commissioner, before a provider is enrolled or license is issued. Within six months of enrollment, a newly enrolled home and community-based waiver service provider must ensure that at least one controlling individual has completed training on waiver and related program billing. Exemptions to new waiver provider training requirements may be granted, as determined by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Data on use of emergency use of manual restraint.</span></h2><p>Beginning July 1, 2013, facilities and services to be licensed under chapter 245D shall submit data regarding the use of emergency use of manual restraint as identified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.061">245D.061</a> in a format and at a frequency identified by the commissioner.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>(a) For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p><p>(b) "Controlling individual" means a public body, governmental agency, business entity, officer, owner, or managerial official whose responsibilities include the direction of the management or policies of a program.</p><p>(c) "Managerial official" means an individual who has decision-making authority related to the operation of the program and responsibility for the ongoing management of or direction of the policies, services, or employees of the program.</p><p>(d) "Owner" means an individual who has direct or indirect ownership interest in a corporation or partnership, or business association enrolling with the Department of Human Services as a provider of waiver services.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.10"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Enrollment requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b), the following home and community-based waiver providers must provide, at the time of enrollment and within 30 days of a request, in a format determined by the commissioner, information and documentation that includes proof of liability insurance:</p><p>(1) waiver services providers required to meet the provider standards in chapter 245D;</p><p>(2) foster care providers whose services are funded by the elderly waiver or alternative care program;</p><p>(3) fiscal support entities;</p><p>(4) adult day care providers;</p><p>(5) providers of customized living services; and</p><p>(6) residential care providers.</p><p>(b) Providers of foster care services covered by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.814">245.814</a> are exempt from this subdivision.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.11"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Home and community-based service billing requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) A home and community-based service is eligible for reimbursement if:</p><p>(1) the service is provided according to a federally approved waiver plan as authorized under chapter 256S and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913">256B.0913</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>;</p><p>(2) the service is provided on days and times during the days and hours of operation specified on any license required under chapter 245A or 245D, if applicable; and</p><p>(3) the provider complies with subdivisions 12 to 15, if applicable.</p><p>(b) The provider must maintain documentation that, upon employment and annually thereafter, staff providing a service have attested to reviewing and understanding the following statement: "It is a federal crime to provide materially false information on service billings for medical assistance or services provided under a federally approved waiver plan as authorized under Minnesota Statutes, chapter 256S, and Minnesota Statutes, sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913">256B.0913</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>."</p><p>(c) The department may recover payment according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.064">256B.064</a> and Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.2160">9505.2160</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.2245">9505.2245</a>, for a service that does not satisfy this subdivision.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.12"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Home and community-based service documentation requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) Documentation may be collected and maintained electronically or in paper form by providers and must be produced upon request by the commissioner.</p><p>(b) Documentation of a delivered service must be in English and must be legible according to the standard of a reasonable person.</p><p>(c) If the service is reimbursed at an hourly or specified minute-based rate, each documentation of the provision of a service, unless otherwise specified, must include:</p><p>(1) the date the documentation occurred;</p><p>(2) the day, month, and year when the service was provided;</p><p>(3) the start and stop times with a.m. and p.m. designations, except for case management services as defined under chapter 256S and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0913#stat.256B.0913.7">256B.0913, subdivision 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092#stat.256B.092.1a">256B.092, subdivision 1a</a>; and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49#stat.256B.49.13">256B.49, subdivision 13</a>;</p><p>(4) the service name or description of the service provided; and</p><p>(5) the name, signature, and title, if any, of the provider of service. If the service is provided by multiple staff members, the provider may designate a staff member responsible for verifying services and completing the documentation required by this paragraph.</p><p>(d) If the service is reimbursed at a daily rate or does not meet the requirements in paragraph (c), each documentation of the provision of a service, unless otherwise specified, must include:</p><p>(1) the date the documentation occurred;</p><p>(2) the day, month, and year when the service was provided;</p><p>(3) the service name or description of the service provided; and</p><p>(4) the name, signature, and title, if any, of the person providing the service. If the service is provided by multiple staff, the provider may designate a staff member responsible for verifying services and completing the documentation required by this paragraph.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.13"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Waiver transportation documentation and billing requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) A waiver transportation service must be a waiver transportation service that: (1) is not covered by medical transportation under the Medicaid state plan; and (2) is not included as a component of another waiver service.</p><p>(b) In addition to the documentation requirements in subdivision 12, a waiver transportation service provider must maintain:</p><p>(1) odometer and other records pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.17b">256B.0625, subdivision 17b</a>, paragraph (b), clause (3), sufficient to distinguish an individual trip with a specific vehicle and driver for a waiver transportation service that is billed directly by the mile. A common carrier as defined by Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9505.0315">9505.0315</a>, subpart 1, item B, or a publicly operated transit system provider are exempt from this clause; and</p><p>(2) documentation demonstrating that a vehicle and a driver meet the transportation waiver service provider standards and qualifications according to the federally approved waiver plan.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.14"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Equipment and supply documentation requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) In addition to the requirements in subdivision 12, an equipment and supply services provider must for each documentation of the provision of a service include:</p><p>(1) the recipient's assessed need for the equipment or supply;</p><p>(2) the reason the equipment or supply is not covered by the Medicaid state plan;</p><p>(3) the type and brand name of the equipment or supply delivered to or purchased by the recipient, including whether the equipment or supply was rented or purchased;</p><p>(4) the quantity of the equipment or supply delivered or purchased; and</p><p>(5) the cost of the equipment or supply if the amount paid for the service depends on the cost.</p><p>(b) A provider must maintain a copy of the shipping invoice or a delivery service tracking log or other documentation showing the date of delivery that proves the equipment or supply was delivered to the recipient or a receipt if the equipment or supply was purchased by the recipient.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.15"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Adult day service documentation and billing requirements.</span></h2><p>(a) In addition to the requirements in subdivision 12, a provider of adult day services as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.02#stat.245A.02.2a">245A.02, subdivision 2a</a>, and licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.9600">9555.9600</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.9730">9555.9730</a>, must maintain documentation of:</p><p>(1) a needs assessment and current plan of care according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.143">245A.143</a>, subdivisions 4 to 7, or Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.9700">9555.9700</a>, for each recipient, if applicable;</p><p>(2) attendance records as specified under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.14#stat.245A.14.14">245A.14, subdivision 14</a>, paragraph (a), including the date of attendance with the day, month, and year; and the pickup and drop-off time in hours and minutes with a.m. and p.m. designations;</p><p>(3) the monthly and quarterly program requirements in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9555.9710">9555.9710</a>, subparts 1, items E and H; 3; 4; and 6, if applicable;</p><p>(4) the name and qualification of each registered physical therapist, registered nurse, and registered dietitian who provides services to the adult day services or nonresidential program; and</p><p>(5) the location where the service was provided. If the location is an alternate location from the usual place of service, the documentation must include the address, or a description if the address is not available, of both the origin site and destination site; the length of time at the alternate location with a.m. and p.m. designations; and a list of participants who went to the alternate location.</p><p>(b) A provider must not exceed the provider's licensed capacity. If a provider exceeds the provider's licensed capacity, the department must recover all Minnesota health care programs payments from the date the provider exceeded licensed capacity.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4912.16"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Rates established by the commissioner.</span></h2><p>For homemaker services eligible for reimbursement under the developmental disabilities waiver, the brain injury waiver, the community alternative care waiver, and the community access for disability inclusion waiver, the commissioner must establish rates equal to the rates established under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256S.21">256S.21 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256S.215">256S.215</a> for the corresponding homemaker services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.4912.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.8.69.0">2009 c 79 art 8 s 69</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/216/#laws.18.26.0">2012 c 216 art 18 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.8.52.0">2013 c 108 art 8 s 52</a>-56; art 13 s 7,8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.8.9.0">2014 c 291 art 8 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.27.60.0">2014 c 312 art 27 s 60</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/54/#laws.1.33.0">2019 c 54 art 1 s 33</a>; art 2 s 35-37; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.2.122.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 2 s 122</a>-126; art 5 s 54; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.13.56.0">2021 c 30 art 13 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.134.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 134</a>,135; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/25/#laws.0.143.0">2023 c 25 s 143</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/61/#laws.1.24.0">2023 c 61 art 1 s 24</a>-26; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/125/#laws.1.24.0">2024 c 125 art 1 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.46.24.0">2024 c 127 art 46 s 24</a></p></div><p><b>NOTE: </b>Subdivision 16, as added by Laws 2023, chapter 61, article 1, section 26, is effective upon federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2023, chapter 61, article 1, section 26, the effective date.</p><div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.256B.4913"><h1>256B.4913 </h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.13.14.0">2013 c 108 art 13 s 14</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.13.14.0">2013 c 108 art 13 s 14</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.13.14.0">2013 c 108 art 13 s 14</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.13.14.0">2013 c 108 art 13 s 14</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.4a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.</h2><p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.5.94.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 5 s 94</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2><p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.5.94.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 5 s 94</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2><p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.5.94.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 5 s 94</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4913.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2><p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.5.94.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 5 s 94</a>]</p></div></div><div class="section" id="stat.256B.4914"><h1 class="shn">256B.4914 HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES WAIVERS; RATE SETTING.</h1><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.1"><h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2><p>The payment methodologies in this section apply to home and community-based services waivers under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>. This section does not change existing waiver policies and procedures.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.2"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2><p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.</p><p>(b) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of human services.</p><p>(c) "Comparable occupations" means the occupations, excluding direct care staff, as represented by the Bureau of Labor Statistics standard occupational classification codes that have the same classification for:</p><p>(1) typical education needed for entry;</p><p>(2) work experience in a related occupation; and</p><p>(3) typical on-the-job training competency as the most predominant classification for direct care staff.</p><p>(d) "Component value" means underlying factors that are part of the cost of providing services that are built into the waiver rates methodology to calculate service rates.</p><p>(e) "Customized living tool" means a methodology for setting service rates that delineates and documents the amount of each component service included in a recipient's customized living service plan.</p><p>(f) "Direct care staff" means employees providing direct service to people receiving services under this section. Direct care staff excludes executive, managerial, and administrative staff.</p><p>(g) "Disability waiver rates system" means a statewide system that establishes rates that are based on uniform processes and captures the individualized nature of waiver services and recipient needs.</p><p>(h) "Individual direct staffing hours" means the time spent as a one-to-one interaction specific to an individual recipient by staff to provide direct support and assistance with activities of daily living, instrumental activities of daily living, and training to participants, and is based on the requirements in each individual's support plan under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.4b">245D.02, subdivision 4b</a>; any support plan addendum under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.4c">245D.02, subdivision 4c</a>; and an assessment tool. Provider observation of an individual's needs must also be considered.</p><p>(i) "Lead agency" means a county, partnership of counties, or Tribal agency charged with administering waivered services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>.</p><p>(j) "Payment or rate" means reimbursement to an eligible provider for services provided to a qualified individual based on an approved service authorization.</p><p>(k) "Rates management system" means a web-based software application that uses a framework and component values, as determined by the commissioner, to establish service rates.</p><p>(l) "Recipient" means a person receiving home and community-based services funded under any of the disability waivers.</p><p>(m) "Shared direct staffing hours" means time spent by employees, not defined under paragraph (f), providing or available to provide more than one individual with direct support and assistance with activities of daily living as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659#stat.256B.0659.1">256B.0659, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (b); instrumental activities of daily living as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0659">256B.0659</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (i); ancillary activities needed to support individual services; and training to participants, and is based on the requirements in each individual's support plan under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.4b">245D.02, subdivision 4b</a>; any support plan addendum under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.4c">245D.02, subdivision 4c</a>; an assessment tool; and provider observation of an individual's service need. Total shared staffing hours are divided proportionally by the number of individuals who receive the shared service provisions.</p><p>(n) "Staffing ratio" means the number of recipients a service provider employee supports during a unit of service based on a uniform assessment tool, provider observation, case history, and the recipient's services of choice, and not based on the staffing ratios under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.31">245D.31</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.3"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Applicable services.</span></h2><p>(a) Applicable services are those authorized under the state's home and community-based services waivers under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>, including the following, as defined in the federally approved home and community-based services plan:</p><p>(1) 24-hour customized living;</p><p>(2) adult day services;</p><p>(3) adult day services bath;</p><p>(4) community residential services;</p><p>(5) customized living;</p><p>(6) day support services;</p><p>(7) employment development services;</p><p>(8) employment exploration services;</p><p>(9) employment support services;</p><p>(10) family residential services;</p><p>(11) individualized home supports;</p><p>(12) individualized home supports with family training;</p><p>(13) individualized home supports with training;</p><p>(14) integrated community supports;</p><p>(15) life sharing;</p><p>(16) night supervision;</p><p>(17) positive support services;</p><p>(18) prevocational services;</p><p>(19) residential support services;</p><p>(20) respite services;</p><p>(21) transportation services; and</p><p>(22) other services as approved by the federal government in the state home and community-based services waiver plan.</p><p>(b) Effective January 1, 2024, or upon federal approval, whichever is later, respite services under paragraph (a), clause (20), are not an applicable service under this section.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.4"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Data collection for rate determination.</span></h2><p>(a) Rates for applicable home and community-based waivered services, including customized rates under subdivision 12, are set by the rates management system.</p><p>(b) Data and information in the rates management system must be used to calculate an individual's rate.</p><p>(c) Service providers, with information from the support plan and oversight by lead agencies, shall provide values and information needed to calculate an individual's rate in the rates management system. Lead agencies must use forms provided by the commissioner to collect this information. The determination of service levels must be part of a discussion with members of the support team as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.34">245D.02, subdivision 34</a>. This discussion must occur prior to the final establishment of each individual's rate. The values and information include:</p><p>(1) shared staffing hours;</p><p>(2) individual staffing hours;</p><p>(3) direct registered nurse hours;</p><p>(4) direct licensed practical nurse hours;</p><p>(5) staffing ratios;</p><p>(6) information to document variable levels of service qualification for variable levels of reimbursement in each framework;</p><p>(7) shared or individualized arrangements for unit-based services, including the staffing ratio;</p><p>(8) number of trips and miles for transportation services; and</p><p>(9) service hours provided through monitoring technology.</p><p>(d) Updates to individual data must include:</p><p>(1) data for each individual that is updated annually when renewing service plans; and</p><p>(2) requests by individuals or lead agencies to update a rate whenever there is a change in an individual's service needs, with accompanying documentation.</p><p>(e) Lead agencies shall review and approve all services reflecting each individual's needs, and the values to calculate the final payment rate for services with variables under subdivisions 6 to 9 for each individual. Lead agencies must notify the individual and the service provider of the final agreed-upon values and rate, and provide information that is identical to what was entered into the rates management system. If a value used was mistakenly or erroneously entered and used to calculate a rate, a provider may petition lead agencies to correct it. Lead agencies must respond to these requests. When responding to the request, the lead agency must consider:</p><p>(1) meeting the health and welfare needs of the individual or individuals receiving services by service site, identified in their support plan under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.4b">245D.02, subdivision 4b</a>, and any addendum under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.02#stat.245D.02.4c">245D.02, subdivision 4c</a>;</p><p>(2) meeting the requirements for staffing under subdivision 2, paragraphs (h), (n), and (o); and meeting or exceeding the licensing standards for staffing required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.09#stat.245D.09.1">245D.09, subdivision 1</a>; and</p><p>(3) meeting the staffing ratio requirements under subdivision 2, paragraph (o), and meeting or exceeding the licensing standards for staffing required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.31">245D.31</a>.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.5"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Base wage index; establishment and updates.</span></h2><p>(a) The base wage index is established to determine staffing costs associated with providing services to individuals receiving home and community-based services. For purposes of calculating the base wage, Minnesota-specific wages taken from job descriptions and standard occupational classification (SOC) codes from the Bureau of Labor Statistics as defined in the Occupational Handbook must be used.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall update the base wage index in subdivision 5a, publish these updated values, and load them into the rate management system as follows:</p><p>(1) on January 1, 2022, based on wage data by SOC from the Bureau of Labor Statistics available as of December 31, 2019;</p><p>(2) on January 1, 2024, based on wage data by SOC from the Bureau of Labor Statistics published in March 2022; and</p><p>(3) on January 1, 2026, and every two years thereafter, based on wage data by SOC from the Bureau of Labor Statistics published in the spring approximately 21 months prior to the scheduled update.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.5a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Base wage index; calculations.</span></h2><p>The base wage index must be calculated as follows:</p><p>(1) for supervisory staff, 100 percent of the median wage for community and social services specialist (SOC code 21-1099), with the exception of the supervisor of positive supports professional, positive supports analyst, and positive supports specialist, which is 100 percent of the median wage for clinical counseling and school psychologist (SOC code 19-3031);</p><p>(2) for registered nurse staff, 100 percent of the median wage for registered nurses (SOC code 29-1141);</p><p>(3) for licensed practical nurse staff, 100 percent of the median wage for licensed practical nurses (SOC code 29-2061);</p><p>(4) for residential asleep-overnight staff, the minimum wage in Minnesota for large employers;</p><p>(5) for residential direct care staff, the sum of:</p><p>(i) 15 percent of the subtotal of 50 percent of the median wage for home health and personal care aide (SOC code 31-1120); 30 percent of the median wage for nursing assistant (SOC code 31-1131); and 20 percent of the median wage for social and human services aide (SOC code 21-1093); and</p><p>(ii) 85 percent of the subtotal of 40 percent of the median wage for home health and personal care aide (SOC code 31-1120); 20 percent of the median wage for nursing assistant (SOC code 31-1131); 20 percent of the median wage for psychiatric technician (SOC code 29-2053); and 20 percent of the median wage for social and human services aide (SOC code 21-1093);</p><p>(6) for adult day services staff, 70 percent of the median wage for nursing assistant (SOC code 31-1131); and 30 percent of the median wage for home health and personal care aide (SOC code 31-1120);</p><p>(7) for day support services staff and prevocational services staff, 20 percent of the median wage for nursing assistant (SOC code 31-1131); 20 percent of the median wage for psychiatric technician (SOC code 29-2053); and 60 percent of the median wage for social and human services aide (SOC code 21-1093);</p><p>(8) for positive supports analyst staff, 100 percent of the median wage for substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselor (SOC code 21-1018);</p><p>(9) for positive supports professional staff, 100 percent of the median wage for clinical counseling and school psychologist (SOC code 19-3031);</p><p>(10) for positive supports specialist staff, 100 percent of the median wage for psychiatric technicians (SOC code 29-2053);</p><p>(11) for individualized home supports with family training staff, 20 percent of the median wage for nursing aide (SOC code 31-1131); 30 percent of the median wage for community social service specialist (SOC code 21-1099); 40 percent of the median wage for social and human services aide (SOC code 21-1093); and ten percent of the median wage for psychiatric technician (SOC code 29-2053);</p><p>(12) for individualized home supports with training services staff, 40 percent of the median wage for community social service specialist (SOC code 21-1099); 50 percent of the median wage for social and human services aide (SOC code 21-1093); and ten percent of the median wage for psychiatric technician (SOC code 29-2053);</p><p>(13) for employment support services staff, 50 percent of the median wage for rehabilitation counselor (SOC code 21-1015); and 50 percent of the median wage for community and social services specialist (SOC code 21-1099);</p><p>(14) for employment exploration services staff, 50 percent of the median wage for education, guidance, school, and vocational counselor (SOC code 21-1012); and 50 percent of the median wage for community and social services specialist (SOC code 21-1099);</p><p>(15) for employment development services staff, 50 percent of the median wage for education, guidance, school, and vocational counselors (SOC code 21-1012); and 50 percent of the median wage for community and social services specialist (SOC code 21-1099);</p><p>(16) for individualized home support without training staff, 50 percent of the median wage for home health and personal care aide (SOC code 31-1120); and 50 percent of the median wage for nursing assistant (SOC code 31-1131); and</p><p>(17) for night supervision staff, 40 percent of the median wage for home health and personal care aide (SOC code 31-1120); 20 percent of the median wage for nursing assistant (SOC code 31-1131); 20 percent of the median wage for psychiatric technician (SOC code 29-2053); and 20 percent of the median wage for social and human services aide (SOC code 21-1093).</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.5b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.<span class="headnote">Standard component value adjustments.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall update the client and programming support, transportation, and program facility cost component values as required in subdivisions 6 to 9 and the rates identified in subdivision 19 for changes in the Consumer Price Index. The commissioner shall adjust these values higher or lower, publish these updated values, and load them into the rate management system as follows:</p><p>(1) on January 1, 2022, by the percentage change in the CPI-U from the date of the previous update to the data available on December 31, 2019;</p><p>(2) on January 1, 2024, by the percentage change in the CPI-U from the date of the previous update to the data available as of December 31, 2022; and</p><p>(3) on January 1, 2026, and every two years thereafter, by the percentage change in the CPI-U from the date of the previous update to the data available 24 months and one day prior to the scheduled update.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.5c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5c.<span class="headnote">Removal of after-framework adjustments.</span></h2><p>Any rate adjustments applied to the service rates calculated under this section outside of the cost components and rate methodology specified in this section shall be removed from rate calculations upon implementation of the updates under subdivisions 5 and 5b.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.5d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5d.<span class="headnote">Unavailable data for updates and adjustments.</span></h2><p>If Bureau of Labor Statistics occupational codes or Consumer Price Index items specified in subdivision 5 or 5b are unavailable in the future, the commissioner shall recommend to the legislature codes or items to update and replace.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.5e"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5e.<span class="headnote">Inflationary update spending requirement.</span></h2><p>(a) At least 80 percent of the marginal increase in revenue from the rate adjustment applied to the service rates calculated under subdivisions 5 and 5b beginning on January 1, 2022, for services rendered between January 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024, must be used to increase compensation-related costs for employees directly employed by the program on or after January 1, 2022.</p><p>(b) For the purposes of this subdivision, compensation-related costs include:</p><p>(1) wages and salaries;</p><p>(2) the employer's share of FICA taxes, Medicare taxes, state and federal unemployment taxes, workers' compensation, and mileage reimbursement;</p><p>(3) the employer's paid share of health and dental insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, long-term care insurance, uniform allowance, pensions, and contributions to employee retirement accounts; and</p><p>(4) benefits that address direct support professional workforce needs above and beyond what employees were offered prior to January 1, 2022, including retention and recruitment bonuses and tuition reimbursement.</p><p class="in">(c) Compensation-related costs for persons employed in the central office of a corporation or entity that has an ownership interest in the provider or exercises control over the provider, or for persons paid by the provider under a management contract, do not count toward the 80 percent requirement under this subdivision.</p><p class="in">(d) A provider agency or individual provider that receives a rate subject to the requirements of this subdivision shall prepare, and upon request submit to the commissioner, a distribution plan that specifies the amount of money the provider expects to receive that is subject to the requirements of this subdivision, including how that money was or will be distributed to increase compensation-related costs for employees. Within 60 days of final implementation of a rate adjustment subject to the requirements of this subdivision, the provider must post the distribution plan and leave it posted for a period of at least six months in an area of the provider's operation to which all direct support professionals have access.</p><p class="in">(e) This subdivision expires June 30, 2024.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.6"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote"> Residential support services; generally.</span></h2><p>(a) For purposes of this section, residential support services includes 24-hour customized living services, community residential services, customized living services, and integrated community supports.</p><p>(b) A unit of service for residential support services is a day. Any portion of any calendar day, within allowable Medicaid rules, where an individual spends time in a residential setting is billable as a day. The number of days authorized for all individuals enrolling in residential support services must include every day that services start and end.</p><p>(c) When the available shared staffing hours in a residential setting are insufficient to meet the needs of an individual who enrolled in residential support services after January 1, 2014, then individual staffing hours shall be used.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.6a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6a.<span class="headnote">Community residential services; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) Component values for community residential services are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(6) program-related expense ratio: 1.3 percent; and</p><p>(7) absence and utilization factor ratio: 3.9 percent.</p><p>(b) Payments for community residential services must be calculated as follows:</p><p>(1) determine the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours to meet a recipient's needs provided on site or through monitoring technology;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided on site or through monitoring technology and nursing hours by the appropriate staff wages;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided on site or through monitoring technology and nursing hours by the product of the supervision span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), excluding any shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided through monitoring technology, and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing cost;</p><p>(8) for employee-related expenses, multiply the direct staffing cost, excluding any shared direct staffing and individual hours provided through monitoring technology, by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(9) for client programming and supports, add $2,260.21 divided by 365. The commissioner shall update the amount in this clause as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(10) for transportation, if provided, add $1,742.62 divided by 365, or $3,111.81 divided by 365 if customized for adapted transport, based on the resident with the highest assessed need. The commissioner shall update the amounts in this clause as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(11) subtotal clauses (8) to (10) and the direct staffing cost of any shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided through monitoring technology that was excluded in clause (8);</p><p>(12) sum the standard general administrative support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(13) divide the result of clause (11) by one minus the result of clause (12). This is the total payment amount; and</p><p>(14) adjust the result of clause (13) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.6b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6b.<span class="headnote">Family residential services; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) Component values for family residential services are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) general administrative support ratio: 3.3 percent;</p><p>(6) program-related expense ratio: 1.3 percent; and</p><p>(7) absence factor: 1.7 percent.</p><p>(b) Payments for family residential services must be calculated as follows:</p><p>(1) determine the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours to meet a recipient's needs provided on site or through monitoring technology;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided on site or through monitoring technology and nursing hours by the appropriate staff wages;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided on site or through monitoring technology and nursing hours by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), excluding any shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided through monitoring technology, and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing cost;</p><p>(8) for employee-related expenses, multiply the direct staffing cost, excluding any shared and individual direct staffing hours provided through monitoring technology, by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(9) for client programming and supports, add $2,260.21 divided by 365. The commissioner shall update the amount in this clause as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(10) for transportation, if provided, add $1,742.62 divided by 365, or $3,111.81 divided by 365 if customized for adapted transport, based on the resident with the highest assessed need. The commissioner shall update the amounts in this clause as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(11) subtotal clauses (8) to (10) and the direct staffing cost of any shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours provided through monitoring technology that was excluded in clause (8);</p><p>(12) sum the standard general administrative support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(13) divide the result of clause (11) by one minus the result of clause (12). This is the total payment rate; and</p><p>(14) adjust the result of clause (13) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.6c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6c.<span class="headnote">Integrated community supports; component values and calculation of payment rates. </span></h2><p>(a) Component values for integrated community supports are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(6) program-related expense ratio: 1.3 percent; and</p><p>(7) absence and utilization factor ratio: 3.9 percent.</p><p>(b) Payments for integrated community supports must be calculated as follows:</p><p>(1) determine the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours to meet a recipient's needs. The base shared direct staffing hours must be eight hours divided by the number of people receiving support in the integrated community support setting, and the individual direct staffing hours must be the average number of direct support hours provided directly to the service recipient;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours in clause (1) by the appropriate staff wages;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of shared direct staffing and individual direct staffing hours in clause (1) by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6) and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing cost;</p><p>(8) for employee-related expenses, multiply the direct staffing cost by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(9) for client programming and supports, add $2,260.21 divided by 365. The commissioner shall update the amount in this clause as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(10) add the results of clauses (8) and (9);</p><p>(11) add the standard general administrative support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(12) divide the result of clause (10) by one minus the result of clause (11). This is the total payment amount; and</p><p>(13) adjust the result of clause (12) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.6d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6d.<span class="headnote">Payment for customized living.</span></h2><p>(a) The payment methodology for customized living and 24-hour customized living must be the customized living tool. The commissioner shall revise the customized living tool to reflect the services and activities unique to disability-related recipient needs and adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p>(b) The rate adjustments described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256S.205">256S.205</a> do not apply to rates paid under this section.</p><p>(c) Customized living and 24-hour customized living rates determined under this section shall not include more than 24 hours of support in a daily unit.</p><p>(d) The commissioner shall establish the following acuity-based customized living tool input limits, based on case mix, for customized living and 24-hour customized living rates determined under this section:</p><p>(1) no more than two hours of mental health management per day for people assessed for case mixes A, D, and G;</p><p>(2) no more than four hours of activities of daily living assistance per day for people assessed for case mix B; and</p><p>(3) no more than six hours of activities of daily living assistance per day for people assessed for case mix D.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.7"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote"> Day programs; generally.</span></h2><p>(a) For the purposes of this section, day programs include adult day services, day support services, and prevocational services.</p><p>(b) The staffing ratios for the units of service provided by a day program to a recipient in a typical week must be averaged to determine an individual's staffing ratio.</p><p>(c) The commissioner, in consultation with service providers, shall develop a uniform staffing ratio worksheet to be used by day programs to determine staffing ratios for day programs.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.7a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Adult day services; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) Component values for adult day services are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) program plan support ratio: 5.6 percent;</p><p>(6) client programming and support ratio: 7.4 percent, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(7) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(8) program-related expense ratio: 1.8 percent; and</p><p>(9) absence and utilization factor ratio: 9.4 percent.</p><p>(b) A unit of service for adult day services is either a day or 15 minutes. A day unit of service is six or more hours of time spent providing direct service.</p><p>(c) Payments for adult day services must be calculated as follows:</p><p>(1) determine the number of units of service and the staffing ratio to meet a recipient's needs;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of day program direct staffing hours and nursing hours by the appropriate staff wage;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of day program direct staffing hours by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing rate;</p><p>(8) for program plan support, multiply the result of clause (7) by one plus the program plan support ratio;</p><p>(9) for employee-related expenses, multiply the result of clause (8) by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(10) for client programming and supports, multiply the result of clause (9) by one plus the client programming and support ratio;</p><p>(11) for program facility costs, add $19.30 per week with consideration of staffing ratios to meet individual needs, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(12) for adult day bath services, add $7.01 per 15 minute unit;</p><p>(13) this is the subtotal rate;</p><p>(14) sum the standard general administrative rate support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(15) divide the result of clause (13) by one minus the result of clause (14). This is the total payment amount; and</p><p>(16) adjust the result of clause (15) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.7b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7b.<span class="headnote">Day support services; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) Component values for day support services are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) program plan support ratio: 5.6 percent;</p><p>(6) client programming and support ratio: 10.37 percent, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(7) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(8) program-related expense ratio: 1.8 percent; and</p><p>(9) absence and utilization factor ratio: 9.4 percent.</p><p>(b) A unit of service for day support services is 15 minutes.</p><p>(c) Payments for day support services must be calculated as follows:</p><p>(1) determine the number of units of service and the staffing ratio to meet a recipient's needs;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of day program direct staffing hours and nursing hours by the appropriate staff wage;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of day program direct staffing hours by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing rate;</p><p>(8) for program plan support, multiply the result of clause (7) by one plus the program plan support ratio;</p><p>(9) for employee-related expenses, multiply the result of clause (8) by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(10) for client programming and supports, multiply the result of clause (9) by one plus the client programming and support ratio;</p><p>(11) for program facility costs, add $19.30 per week with consideration of staffing ratios to meet individual needs, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(12) this is the subtotal rate;</p><p>(13) sum the standard general administrative rate support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(14) divide the result of clause (12) by one minus the result of clause (13). This is the total payment amount; and</p><p>(15) adjust the result of clause (14) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.7c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7c.<span class="headnote">Prevocational services; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) Component values for prevocational services are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) program plan support ratio: 5.6 percent;</p><p>(6) client programming and support ratio: 10.37 percent, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(7) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(8) program-related expense ratio: 1.8 percent; and</p><p>(9) absence and utilization factor ratio: 9.4 percent.</p><p>(b) A unit of service for prevocational services is either a day or 15 minutes. A day unit of service is six or more hours of time spent providing direct service.</p><p>(c) Payments for prevocational services must be calculated as follows:</p><p>(1) determine the number of units of service and the staffing ratio to meet a recipient's needs;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of day program direct staffing hours and nursing hours by the appropriate staff wage;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of day program direct staffing hours by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing rate;</p><p>(8) for program plan support, multiply the result of clause (7) by one plus the program plan support ratio;</p><p>(9) for employee-related expenses, multiply the result of clause (8) by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(10) for client programming and supports, multiply the result of clause (9) by one plus the client programming and support ratio;</p><p>(11) for program facility costs, add $19.30 per week with consideration of staffing ratios to meet individual needs, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(12) this is the subtotal rate;</p><p>(13) sum the standard general administrative rate support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(14) divide the result of clause (12) by one minus the result of clause (13). This is the total payment amount; and</p><p>(15) adjust the result of clause (14) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.8"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote"> Unit-based services with programming; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) For the purpose of this section, unit-based services with programming include employment exploration services, employment development services, employment support services, individualized home supports with family training, individualized home supports with training, and positive support services provided to an individual outside of any service plan for a day program or residential support service.</p><p>(b) Component values for unit-based services with programming are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) program plan support ratio: 15.5 percent;</p><p>(6) client programming and support ratio: 4.7 percent, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(7) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(8) program-related expense ratio: 6.1 percent; and</p><p>(9) absence and utilization factor ratio: 3.9 percent.</p><p>(c) A unit of service for unit-based services with programming is 15 minutes.</p><p>(d) Payments for unit-based services with programming must be calculated as follows, unless the services are reimbursed separately as part of a residential support services or day program payment rate:</p><p>(1) determine the number of units of service to meet a recipient's needs;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of direct staffing hours by the appropriate staff wage;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of direct staffing hours by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing rate;</p><p>(8) for program plan support, multiply the result of clause (7) by one plus the program plan support ratio;</p><p>(9) for employee-related expenses, multiply the result of clause (8) by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(10) for client programming and supports, multiply the result of clause (9) by one plus the client programming and support ratio;</p><p>(11) this is the subtotal rate;</p><p>(12) sum the standard general administrative support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(13) divide the result of clause (11) by one minus the result of clause (12). This is the total payment amount;</p><p>(14) for services provided in a shared manner, divide the total payment in clause (13) as follows:</p><p>(i) for employment exploration services, divide by the number of service recipients, not to exceed five;</p><p>(ii) for employment support services, divide by the number of service recipients, not to exceed six;</p><p>(iii) for individualized home supports with training and individualized home supports with family training, divide by the number of service recipients, not to exceed three; and</p><p>(iv) for night supervision, divide by the number of service recipients, not to exceed two; and</p><p>(15) adjust the result of clause (14) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.9"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote"> Unit-based services without programming; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) For the purposes of this section, unit-based services without programming include individualized home supports without training and night supervision provided to an individual outside of any service plan for a day program or residential support service.
