Unit-based services without programming do not include respite.</p><p>(b) Component values for unit-based services without programming are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 6.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) program plan support ratio: 7.0 percent;</p><p>(6) client programming and support ratio: 2.3 percent, updated as specified in subdivision 5b;</p><p>(7) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(8) program-related expense ratio: 2.9 percent; and</p><p>(9) absence and utilization factor ratio: 3.9 percent.</p><p>(c) A unit of service for unit-based services without programming is 15 minutes.</p><p>(d) Payments for unit-based services without programming must be calculated as follows unless the services are reimbursed separately as part of a residential support services or day program payment rate:</p><p>(1) determine the number of units of service to meet a recipient's needs;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 to 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring customization for deaf and hard-of-hearing language accessibility under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of direct staffing hours by the appropriate staff wage;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of direct staffing hours by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing rate;</p><p>(8) for program plan support, multiply the result of clause (7) by one plus the program plan support ratio;</p><p>(9) for employee-related expenses, multiply the result of clause (8) by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(10) for client programming and supports, multiply the result of clause (9) by one plus the client programming and support ratio;</p><p>(11) this is the subtotal rate;</p><p>(12) sum the standard general administrative support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(13) divide the result of clause (11) by one minus the result of clause (12). This is the total payment amount;</p><p>(14) for individualized home supports without training provided in a shared manner, divide the total payment amount in clause (13) by the number of service recipients, not to exceed three; and</p><p>(15) adjust the result of clause (14) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.9a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9a.<span class="headnote">Respite services; component values and calculation of payment rates.</span></h2><p>(a) For the purposes of this section, respite services include respite services provided to an individual outside of any service plan for a day program or residential support service.</p><p>(b) Component values for respite services are:</p><p>(1) competitive workforce factor: 4.7 percent;</p><p>(2) supervisory span of control ratio: 11 percent;</p><p>(3) employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio: 8.71 percent;</p><p>(4) employee-related cost ratio: 23.6 percent;</p><p>(5) general administrative support ratio: 13.25 percent;</p><p>(6) program-related expense ratio: 2.9 percent; and</p><p>(7) absence and utilization factor ratio: 3.9 percent.</p><p>(c) A unit of service for respite services is 15 minutes.</p><p>(d) Payments for respite services must be calculated as follows unless the service is reimbursed separately as part of a residential support services or day program payment rate:</p><p>(1) determine the number of units of service to meet an individual's needs;</p><p>(2) determine the appropriate hourly staff wage rates derived by the commissioner as provided in subdivisions 5 and 5a;</p><p>(3) except for subdivision 5a, clauses (1) to (4), multiply the result of clause (2) by the product of one plus the competitive workforce factor;</p><p>(4) for a recipient requiring deaf and hard-of-hearing customization under subdivision 12, add the customization rate provided in subdivision 12 to the result of clause (3);</p><p>(5) multiply the number of direct staffing hours by the appropriate staff wage;</p><p>(6) multiply the number of direct staffing hours by the product of the supervisory span of control ratio and the appropriate supervisory staff wage in subdivision 5a, clause (1);</p><p>(7) combine the results of clauses (5) and (6), and multiply the result by one plus the employee vacation, sick, and training allowance ratio. This is defined as the direct staffing rate;</p><p>(8) for employee-related expenses, multiply the result of clause (7) by one plus the employee-related cost ratio;</p><p>(9) this is the subtotal rate;</p><p>(10) sum the standard general administrative support ratio, the program-related expense ratio, and the absence and utilization factor ratio;</p><p>(11) divide the result of clause (9) by one minus the result of clause (10). This is the total payment amount;</p><p>(12) for respite services provided in a shared manner, divide the total payment amount in clause (11) by the number of service recipients, not to exceed three; and</p><p>(13) adjust the result of clause (12) by a factor to be determined by the commissioner to adjust for regional differences in the cost of providing services.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.10"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Evaluation of information and data.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall, within available resources, conduct research and gather data and information from existing state systems or other outside sources on the following items:</p><p>(1) differences in the underlying cost to provide services and care across the state;</p><p>(2) mileage, vehicle type, lift requirements, incidents of individual and shared rides, and units of transportation for all day services, which must be collected from providers using the rate management worksheet and entered into the rates management system; and</p><p>(3) the distinct underlying costs for services provided by a license holder under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.05">245D.05</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.06">245D.06</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.07">245D.07</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.071">245D.071</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.081">245D.081</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.09">245D.09</a>, and for services provided by a license holder certified under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.33">245D.33</a>.</p><p>(b) The commissioner, in consultation with stakeholders, shall review and evaluate the following values already in subdivisions 6 to 9, or issues that impact all services, including, but not limited to:</p><p>(1) values for transportation rates;</p><p>(2) values for services where monitoring technology replaces staff time;</p><p>(3) values for indirect services;</p><p>(4) values for nursing;</p><p>(5) values for the facility use rate in day services, and the weightings used in the day service ratios and adjustments to those weightings;</p><p>(6) values for workers' compensation as part of employee-related expenses;</p><p>(7) values for unemployment insurance as part of employee-related expenses;</p><p>(8) direct care workforce labor market measures;</p><p>(9) any changes in state or federal law with a direct impact on the underlying cost of providing home and community-based services;</p><p>(10) outcome measures, determined by the commissioner, for home and community-based services rates determined under this section; and</p><p>(11) different competitive workforce factors by service, as determined under subdivision 10b.</p><p>(c) Beginning July 1, 2022, the commissioner shall renew analysis and implement changes to the regional adjustment factors once every six years. Prior to implementation, the commissioner shall consult with stakeholders on the methodology to calculate the adjustment.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.10a"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10a.<span class="headnote">Reporting and analysis of cost data.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner must ensure that wage values and component values in subdivisions 5 to 9 reflect the cost to provide the service. As determined by the commissioner, in consultation with stakeholders identified in subdivision 17, a provider enrolled to provide services with rates determined under this section must submit requested cost data to the commissioner to support research on the cost of providing services that have rates determined by the disability waiver rates system. Requested cost data may include, but is not limited to:</p><p>(1) worker wage costs;</p><p>(2) benefits paid;</p><p>(3) supervisor wage costs;</p><p>(4) executive wage costs;</p><p>(5) vacation, sick, and training time paid;</p><p>(6) taxes, workers' compensation, and unemployment insurance costs paid;</p><p>(7) administrative costs paid;</p><p>(8) program costs paid;</p><p>(9) transportation costs paid;</p><p>(10) vacancy rates; and</p><p>(11) other data relating to costs required to provide services requested by the commissioner.</p><p>(b) At least once in any five-year period, a provider must submit cost data for a fiscal year that ended not more than 18 months prior to the submission date. The commissioner shall provide each provider a 90-day notice prior to its submission due date. If a provider fails to submit required reporting data, the commissioner shall provide notice to providers that have not provided required data 30 days after the required submission date, and a second notice for providers who have not provided required data 60 days after the required submission date. The commissioner shall temporarily suspend payments to the provider if cost data is not received 90 days after the required submission date. Withheld payments shall be made once data is received by the commissioner.</p><p>(c) The commissioner shall conduct a random validation of data submitted under paragraph (a) to ensure data accuracy. The commissioner shall analyze cost documentation in paragraph (a) and provide recommendations for adjustments to cost components.</p><p>(d) The commissioner shall analyze cost data submitted under paragraph (a). The commissioner shall release cost data in an aggregate form. Cost data from individual providers must not be released except as provided for in current law.</p><p>(e) The commissioner shall use data collected in paragraph (a) to determine the compliance with requirements identified under subdivision 10d. The commissioner shall identify providers who have not met the thresholds identified under subdivision 10d on the Department of Human Services website for the year for which the providers reported their costs.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.10b"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10b.<span class="headnote">Provider submission of labor market data.</span></h2><p>(a) Providers enrolled to provide services with rates determined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.4914">256B.4914</a>, subdivision 3, shall submit labor market data to the commissioner annually on or before November 1, including but not limited to:</p><p>(1) number of direct care staff;</p><p>(2) wages of direct care staff;</p><p>(3) overtime wages of direct care staff;</p><p>(4) hours worked by direct care staff;</p><p>(5) overtime hours worked by direct care staff;</p><p>(6) benefits provided to direct care staff;</p><p>(7) direct care staff job vacancies; and</p><p>(8) direct care staff retention rates.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall publish annual reports on provider and state-level labor market data, including but not limited to the data obtained under paragraph (a).</p><p>(c) The commissioner may temporarily suspend payments to the provider if data requested under paragraph (a) is not received 90 days after the required submission date. Withheld payments shall be made once data is received by the commissioner.</p><p>(d) Providers who receive payment under this section for less than 25 percent of their clients in the year prior to the report may attest to the commissioner in a manner determined by the commissioner that they are declining to provide the data required under paragraph (a) and will not be subject to the payment suspension in paragraph (c).</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.10c"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10c.<span class="headnote">Reporting and analysis of competitive workforce factor.</span></h2><p>(a) Beginning February 1, 2025, and every two years thereafter, the commissioner shall report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees and divisions with jurisdiction over health and human services policy and finance an analysis of the competitive workforce factor.</p><p>(b) The report must include:</p><p>(1) the most recently available wage data by SOC code for the weighted average wage for direct care staff for residential services and direct care staff for day services;</p><p>(2) the most recently available wage data by SOC code of the weighted average wage of comparable occupations; and</p><p>(3) workforce data as required under subdivision 10b.</p><p class="in">(c) This subdivision expires June 30, 2031.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.10d"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10d.<span class="headnote">Direct care staff; compensation.</span></h2><p>(a) A provider paid with rates determined under subdivision 6 must use a minimum of 66 percent of the revenue generated by rates determined under that subdivision for direct care staff compensation.</p><p>(b) A provider paid with rates determined under subdivision 7 must use a minimum of 45 percent of the revenue generated by rates determined under that subdivision for direct care staff compensation.</p><p>(c) A provider paid with rates determined under subdivision 8 or 9 must use a minimum of 60 percent of the revenue generated by rates determined under those subdivisions for direct care staff compensation.</p><p>(d) Compensation under this subdivision includes:</p><p>(1) wages;</p><p>(2) taxes and workers' compensation;</p><p>(3) health insurance;</p><p>(4) dental insurance;</p><p>(5) vision insurance;</p><p>(6) life insurance;</p><p>(7) short-term disability insurance;</p><p>(8) long-term disability insurance;</p><p>(9) retirement spending;</p><p>(10) tuition reimbursement;</p><p>(11) wellness programs;</p><p>(12) paid vacation time;</p><p>(13) paid sick time; or</p><p>(14) other items of monetary value provided to direct care staff.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.11"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2><p>MS 2020 [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/33/#laws.0.1.0">2022 c 33 s 1</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.12"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Customization of rates for individuals. </span></h2><p>(a) For persons determined to have higher needs based on being deaf or hard-of-hearing, the direct-care costs must be increased by an adjustment factor prior to calculating the rate under subdivisions 6 to 9. The customization rate with respect to deaf or hard-of-hearing persons shall be $2.50 per hour for waiver recipients who meet the respective criteria as determined by the commissioner.</p><p>(b) For the purposes of this section, "deaf and hard-of-hearing" means:</p><p>(1) the person has a developmental disability and:</p><p>(i) an assessment score which indicates a hearing impairment that is severe or that the person has no useful hearing;</p><p>(ii) an expressive communications score that indicates the person uses single signs or gestures, uses an augmentative communication aid, or does not have functional communication, or the person's expressive communications is unknown; and</p><p>(iii) a communication score which indicates the person comprehends signs, gestures, and modeling prompts or does not comprehend verbal, visual, or gestural communication, or that the person's receptive communication score is unknown; or</p><p>(2) the person receives long-term care services and has an assessment score that indicates the person hears only very loud sounds, the person has no useful hearing, or a determination cannot be made; and the person receives long-term care services and has an assessment that indicates the person communicates needs with sign language, symbol board, written messages, gestures, or an interpreter; communicates with inappropriate content, makes garbled sounds or displays echolalia, or does not communicate needs.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.13"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Transportation.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall require that the purchase of transportation services be cost-effective and be limited to market rates where the transportation mode is generally available and accessible.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.14"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Exceptions.</span></h2><p>(a) In a format prescribed by the commissioner, lead agencies must identify individuals with exceptional needs that cannot be met under the disability waiver rate system. The commissioner shall use that information to evaluate and, if necessary, approve an alternative payment rate for those individuals. Whether granted, denied, or modified, the commissioner shall respond to all exception requests in writing. The commissioner shall include in the written response the basis for the action and provide notification of the right to appeal under paragraph (h).</p><p>(b) Lead agencies must act on an exception request within 30 days and notify the initiator of the request of their recommendation in writing. A lead agency shall submit all exception requests along with its recommendation to the commissioner.</p><p>(c) An application for a rate exception may be submitted for the following criteria:</p><p>(1) an individual has service needs that cannot be met through additional units of service;</p><p>(2) an individual's rate determined under subdivisions 6 to 9 is so insufficient that it has resulted in an individual receiving a notice of discharge from the individual's provider; or</p><p>(3) an individual's service needs, including behavioral changes, require a level of service which necessitates a change in provider or which requires the current provider to propose service changes beyond those currently authorized.</p><p>(d) Exception requests must include the following information:</p><p>(1) the service needs required by each individual that are not accounted for in subdivisions 6 to 9;</p><p>(2) the service rate requested and the difference from the rate determined in subdivisions 6 to 9;</p><p>(3) a basis for the underlying costs used for the rate exception and any accompanying documentation; and</p><p>(4) any contingencies for approval.</p><p>(e) Approved rate exceptions shall be managed within lead agency allocations under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.092">256B.092</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a>.</p><p>(f) Individual disability waiver recipients, an interested party, or the license holder that would receive the rate exception increase may request that a lead agency submit an exception request. A lead agency that denies such a request shall notify the individual waiver recipient, interested party, or license holder of its decision and the reasons for denying the request in writing no later than 30 days after the request has been made and shall submit its denial to the commissioner in accordance with paragraph (b). The reasons for the denial must be based on the failure to meet the criteria in paragraph (c).</p><p>(g) The commissioner shall determine whether to approve or deny an exception request no more than 30 days after receiving the request. If the commissioner denies the request, the commissioner shall notify the lead agency and the individual disability waiver recipient, the interested party, and the license holder in writing of the reasons for the denial.</p><p>(h) The individual disability waiver recipient may appeal any denial of an exception request by either the lead agency or the commissioner, pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.0451">256.0451</a>. When the denial of an exception request results in the proposed demission of a waiver recipient from a residential or day habilitation program, the commissioner shall issue a temporary stay of demission, when requested by the disability waiver recipient, consistent with the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256.045">256.045, subdivisions 4a</a> and 6, paragraph (c). The temporary stay shall remain in effect until the lead agency can provide an informed choice of appropriate, alternative services to the disability waiver.</p><p>(i) Providers may petition lead agencies to update values that were entered incorrectly or erroneously into the rate management system, based on past service level discussions and determination in subdivision 4, without applying for a rate exception.</p><p>(j) The starting date for the rate exception will be the later of the date of the recipient's change in support or the date of the request to the lead agency for an exception.</p><p>(k) The commissioner shall track all exception requests received and their dispositions. The commissioner shall issue quarterly public exceptions statistical reports, including the number of exception requests received and the numbers granted, denied, withdrawn, and pending. The report shall include the average amount of time required to process exceptions.</p><p>(l) Approved rate exceptions remain in effect in all cases until an individual's needs change as defined in paragraph (c).</p><p>(m) Rates determined under subdivision 19 are ineligible for rate exceptions.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.15"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">County or Tribal allocations.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall establish a method of tracking and reporting the fiscal impact of the disability waiver rates management system on individual lead agencies.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall make annual adjustments to lead agencies' home and community-based waivered service budget allocations to adjust for rate differences and the resulting impact on county allocations upon implementation of the disability waiver rates system.</p><p>(c) Lead agencies exceeding their allocations shall be subject to the provisions under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0916#stat.256B.0916.11">256B.0916, subdivision 11,</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49#stat.256B.49.26">256B.49, subdivision 26</a>.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.16"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.</h2><p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.1.54.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 1 s 54</a>]</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.17"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Stakeholder consultation and county training.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall continue consultation at regular intervals with the existing stakeholder group established as part of the rate-setting methodology process and others, to gather input, concerns, and data, to assist in the implementation of the rate payment system, and to make pertinent information available to the public through the department's website.</p><p>(b) The commissioner shall offer training at least annually for county personnel responsible for administering the rate-setting framework in a manner consistent with this section.</p><p>(c) The commissioner shall maintain an online instruction manual explaining the rate-setting framework. The manual shall be consistent with this section, and shall be accessible to all stakeholders including recipients, representatives of recipients, county or Tribal agencies, and license holders.</p><p>(d) The commissioner shall not defer to the county or Tribal agency on matters of technical application of the rate-setting framework, and a county or Tribal agency shall not set rates in a manner that conflicts with this section.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.18"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Legislatively approved changes; public notice.</span></h2><p>(a) The commissioner shall provide a public notice via LISTSERV in October of each year containing information detailing legislatively approved changes in:</p><p>(1) calculation values including derived wage rates and related employee and administrative factors;</p><p>(2) service utilization;</p><p>(3) county and Tribal allocation changes; and</p><p>(4) information on adjustments made to calculation values and the timing of those adjustments.</p><p>(b) The information in this notice must be effective January 1 of the following year.</p></div><div class="subd" id="stat.256B.4914.19"><h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Payments for family residential and life sharing services.</span></h2><p>The commissioner shall establish rates for family residential services and life sharing services based on a person's assessed need, as described in the federally-approved waiver plans. Rates for life sharing services must be ten percent higher than the corresponding family residential services rate.</p><p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p></div></div><div class="history" id="stat.256B.4914.history
			"><h2>History: </h2><p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.13.12.0">2013 c 108 art 13 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.27.62.0">2014 c 312 art 27 s 62</a>-69; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.7.37.0">2015 c 71 art 7 s 37</a>-42; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.126.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 126</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/90/#laws.0.21.0">2017 c 90 s 21</a>-24; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.1.22.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 1 s 22</a>-31; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.2.1.0">2019 c 50 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.5.56.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 5 s 56</a>-68; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.13.42.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 13 s 42</a>,43; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/33/#laws.0.1.0">2022 c 33 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.17.26.0">2022 c 98 art 17 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/50/#laws.4.6.0">2023 c 50 art 4 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/61/#laws.1.27.0">2023 c 61 art 1 s 27</a>-47; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/108/#laws.1.18.0">2024 c 108 art 1 s 18</a>; art 6 s 2,3</p></div><p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 3, paragraph (a), by Laws 2023, chapter 61, article 1, section 27, is effective January 1, 2026, or upon federal approval, whichever is later. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2023, chapter 61, article 1, section 27, the effective date.</p><p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendments to subdivision 4, 5, 6a, 6b, 6c, 7a, 7b, 7c, 8, 9, 10, and 12, by Laws 2023, chapter 61, article 1, sections 28, 29, 33 to 41, and 45, are effective upon federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained. Laws 2023, chapter 61, article 1, sections 28, 29, 33 to 41, and 45, the effective dates.</p><p><b>NOTE: </b>The service name changes in subdivisions 5a, clauses (7), (11), and (12); 6a; 6c; 7b; and 7c, made by Laws 2019, First Special Session chapter 9, article 5, section 59, are effective upon federal approval. The commissioner of human services shall notify the revisor of statutes when federal approval is obtained.
